text_mt: “Therefore, whom should I ask? Who would be a superior guru?” / Reflecting thus, he asked the venerable elder Gautama.

sanskrit_iast:
śukra uvāca
ko guruḥ syān muniśreṣṭha mama brūhi gurur bhavet
trayāṇām api lokānāṃ yo gurus taṃ vrajāmy aham //
meaning:
शुक्र उवाच
को गुरुः स्यान् मुनिश्रेष्ठ मम ब्रूहि गुरुर् भवेत्
त्रयाणाम् अपि लोकानां यो गुरुस् तं व्रजाम्य् अहम् //
text_mt: Śukra said: / “Who can be a guru, O best of sages? Tell me who could be my guru. / I shall go to him who is the guru of even the three worlds.”

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
sa prāha jagatām īśaṃ śaṃbhuṃ devaṃ jagadgurum
kvārādhayāmi giriśam ity uktaḥ prāha gautamaḥ //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
स प्राह जगताम् ईशं शंभुं देवं जगद्गुरुम्
क्वाराधयामि गिरिशम् इत्य् उक्तः प्राह गौतमः //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / He named Śambhu, the Lord of the worlds, the god who is the guru of the universe. / When asked, “Where may I worship the mountain-dwelling Lord?”, Gautama replied:

sanskrit_iast:
gautama uvāca
gautamyāṃ tu śucir bhūtvā stotrais toṣaya śaṃkaram
tatas tuṣṭo jagannāthaḥ sa te vidyāṃ pradāsyati //
meaning:
गौतम उवाच
गौतम्यां तु शुचिर् भूत्वा स्तोत्रैस् तोषय शंकरम्
ततस् तुष्टो जगन्नाथः स ते विद्यां प्रदास्यति //
text_mt: Gautama said: / “Having become pure at the Gautamī, please Śaṅkara with hymns of praise. / Then, being pleased, the Lord of the Universe will grant you knowledge.”

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
gautamasya tu tadvākyāt prāgād gaṅgāṃ sa bhārgavaḥ
snātvā bhūtvā śuciḥ samyak stutiṃ cakre sa bālakaḥ //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
गौतमस्य तु तद्वाक्यात् प्रागाद् गङ्गां स भार्गवः
स्नात्वा भूत्वा शुचिः सम्यक् स्तुतिं चक्रे स बालकः //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / By those words of Gautama, that descendant of Bhṛgu went to the Gaṅgā. / Having bathed and become thoroughly pure, the boy offered praise.

sanskrit_iast:
śukra uvāca
bālo 'haṃ bālabuddhiś ca bālacandradhara prabho
nāhaṃ jānāmi te kiṃcit stutiṃ kartuṃ namo 'stu te //
meaning:
शुक्र उवाच
बालो ऽहं बालबुद्धिश् च बालचन्द्रधर प्रभो
नाहं जानामि ते किंचित् स्तुतिं कर्तुं नमो ऽस्तु ते //
text_mt: Śukra said: / “I am a boy and child-minded, O Lord who bears the crescent moon! / I do not know how to compose any praise of you; obeisance be to you!

sanskrit_iast:
parityaktasya guruṇā na mamāsti suhṛt sakhā
tvaṃ prabhuḥ sarvabhāvena jagannātha namo 'stu te //
meaning:
परित्यक्तस्य गुरुणा न ममास्ति सुहृत् सखा
त्वं प्रभुः सर्वभावेन जगन्नाथ नमो ऽस्तु ते //
text_mt: Abandoned by my guru, I have neither friend nor companion. / You are the Lord in every respect, O Lord of the Universe! Obeisance be to you!

sanskrit_iast:
gurur gurumatāṃ deva mahatāṃ ca mahān asi
aham alpataro bālo jaganmaya namo 'stu te //
meaning:
गुरुर् गुरुमतां देव महतां च महान् असि
अहम् अल्पतरो बालो जगन्मय नमो ऽस्तु ते //
text_mt: You are the guru of those who possess gurus, O God, and great among the great. / I am a tiny boy, O you who pervade the universe! Obeisance be to you!

sanskrit_iast:
vidyārthaṃ hi sureśāna nāhaṃ vedmi bhavadgatim
māṃ tvaṃ ca kṛpayā paśya lokasākṣin namo 'stu te //
meaning:
विद्यार्थं हि सुरेशान नाहं वेद्मि भवद्गतिम्
मां त्वं च कृपया पश्य लोकसाक्षिन् नमो ऽस्तु ते //
text_mt: For the sake of knowledge, O Lord of the gods, though I do not understand your course, / look upon me with compassion, O witness of the world! Obeisance be to you!”

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
evaṃ tu stuvatas tasya prasanno 'bhūt sureśvaraḥ //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवं तु स्तुवतस् तस्य प्रसन्नो ऽभूत् सुरेश्वरः //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / As he was praising him thus, the Lord of the gods became pleased.

sanskrit_iast:
śiva uvāca
kāmaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te yac cāpi suradurlabham //
meaning:
शिव उवाच
कामं वरय भद्रं ते यच् चापि सुरदुर्लभम् //
text_mt: Śiva said: / “Choose a boon as you wish, bless you, even that which is difficult for gods to attain.”

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
kavir apy āha deveśaṃ kṛtāñjalir udāradhīḥ //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
कविर् अप्य् आह देवेशं कृताञ्जलिर् उदारधीः //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Kavi too, noble-minded, with folded hands said to the Lord of the gods:

sanskrit_iast:
śukra uvāca
brahmādibhiś ca ṛṣibhir yā vidyā naiva gocarā
tāṃ vidyāṃ nātha yāciṣye tvaṃ gurur mama daivatam //
meaning:
शुक्र उवाच
ब्रह्मादिभिश् च ऋषिभिर् या विद्या नैव गोचरा
तां विद्यां नाथ याचिष्ये त्वं गुरुर् मम दैवतम् //
text_mt: Śukra said: / “The knowledge that is beyond the scope even of Brahmā and other sages— / that knowledge I shall ask for, O Lord; you are my guru, my divinity.”

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
mṛtasaṃjīvinīṃ vidyām ajñātāṃ tridaśair api
tāṃ dattavān suraśreṣṭhas tasmai śukrāya yācate //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
मृतसंजीविनीं विद्याम् अज्ञातां त्रिदशैर् अपि
तां दत्तवान् सुरश्रेष्ठस् तस्मै शुक्राय याचते //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / The lore that brings the dead back to life, unknown even to the thirty [gods]— / that the best of gods gave to Śukra who asked for it.

sanskrit_iast:
itarā laukikī vidyā vaidikī cānyagocarā
kiṃ punaḥ śaṃkare tuṣṭe vicāryam avaśiṣyate //
meaning:
इतरा लौकिकी विद्या वैदिकी चान्यगोचरा
किं पुनः शंकरे तुष्टे विचार्यम् अवशिष्यते //
text_mt: Other knowledge is worldly, and Vedic [lore] is within the reach of others; / what further deliberation remains once Śaṅkara is pleased?

sanskrit_iast:
sa tu labdhvā mahāvidyāṃ prāyāt svapitaraṃ gurum
daityānāṃ ca guruś cāsīd vidyayā pūjitaḥ kaviḥ //
meaning:
स तु लब्ध्वा महाविद्यां प्रायात् स्वपितरं गुरुम्
दैत्यानां च गुरुश् चासीद् विद्यया पूजितः कविः //
text_mt: Having obtained the great lore, he went to his own father, his teacher; / and Kavi, honoured for his knowledge, became the guru of the Daityas.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ kadācit tāṃ vidyāṃ kasmiṃścit kāraṇāntare
kaco bṛhaspatisuto vidyāṃ prāptaḥ kaves tu tām //
meaning:
ततः कदाचित् तां विद्यां कस्मिंश्चित् कारणान्तरे
कचो बृहस्पतिसुतो विद्यां प्राप्तः कवेस् तु ताम् //
text_mt: Then, once, on a certain occasion, / Kaca, the son of Bṛhaspati, obtained that lore from Kavi.

sanskrit_iast:
kacād bṛhaspatiś cāpi tato devāḥ pṛthak pṛthak
avāpur mahatīṃ vidyāṃ yām āhur mṛtajīvinīm //
meaning:
कचाद् बृहस्पतिश् चापि ततो देवाः पृथक् पृथक्
अवापुर् महतीं विद्यां याम् आहुर् मृतजीविनीम् //
text_mt: From Kaca, Bṛhaspati as well, and then the gods one by one, / obtained the great lore which is called the reviver of the dead.

sanskrit_iast:
yatra sā kavinā prāptā vidyāpūjya maheśvaram
gautamyā uttare pāre śukratīrthaṃ tad ucyate //
meaning:
यत्र सा कविना प्राप्ता विद्यापूज्य महेश्वरम्
गौतम्या उत्तरे पारे शुक्रतीर्थं तद् उच्यते //
text_mt: Where that lore was obtained by Kavi having worshipped Maheśvara, / on the northern bank of the Gautamī, is called Śukratīrtha.

sanskrit_iast:
mṛtasaṃjīvinītīrtham āyurārogyavardhanam
snānaṃ dānaṃ ca yat kiṃcit sarvam akṣayapuṇyadam //
meaning:
मृतसंजीविनीतीर्थम् आयुरारोग्यवर्धनम्
स्नानं दानं च यत् किंचित् सर्वम् अक्षयपुण्यदम् //
text_mt: The Mṛtasaṃjīvinī tīrtha increases longevity and health; / whatever bathing and gift [is performed there], it all grants imperishable merit.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
indratīrtham iti khyātaṃ brahmahatyāvināśanam
smaraṇād api pāpaughakleśasaṃghavināśanam //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इन्द्रतीर्थम् इति ख्यातं ब्रह्महत्याविनाशनम्
स्मरणाद् अपि पापौघक्लेशसंघविनाशनम् //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Known as Indratīrtha, it destroys [the sin of] killing a brahmin; / even by memory of it, the mass of sins and multitude of afflictions are destroyed.

sanskrit_iast:
purā vṛtravadhe vṛtte brahmahatyā tu nārada
śacīpatiṃ cānugatā tāṃ dṛṣṭvā bhītavad dhariḥ //
meaning:
पुरा वृत्रवधे वृत्ते ब्रह्महत्या तु नारद
शचीपतिं चानुगता तां दृष्ट्वा भीतवद् धरिः //
text_mt: Formerly, when the slaying of Vṛtra took place, [the sin of] killing a brahmin, O Nārada, / pursued Śacī's husband; seeing it, Hari, as if terrified—

sanskrit_iast:
indras tato vṛtrahantā itaś cetaś ca dhāvati
yatra yatra tv asau yāti hatyā sāpīndragāminī //
meaning:
इन्द्रस् ततो वृत्रहन्ता इतश् चेतश् च धावति
यत्र यत्र त्व् असौ याति हत्या सापीन्द्रगामिनी //
text_mt: Then Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, ran hither and thither; / wherever he went, that [brahman-]murder also followed Indra.

sanskrit_iast:
sa mahat sara āviśya padmanālam upāgamat
tatrāsau tantuvad bhūtvā vāsaṃ cakre śacīpatiḥ //
meaning:
स महत् सर आविश्य पद्मनालम् उपागमत्
तत्रासौ तन्तुवद् भूत्वा वासं चक्रे शचीपतिः //
text_mt: Entering a great lake, he crept into a lotus stalk; / there, becoming fine as a thread, Śacī's lord took up his abode.

sanskrit_iast:
sarastīre 'pi hatyāsīd divyaṃ varṣasahasrakam
etasminn antare devā nirindrā hy abhavan mune //
meaning:
सरस्तीरे ऽपि हत्यासीद् दिव्यं वर्षसहस्रकम्
एतस्मिन्न् अन्तरे देवा निरिन्द्रा ह्य् अभवन् मुने //
text_mt: And on the bank of the lake, the murder waited for a divine thousand years. / In the meantime, O sage, the gods became indraless.

sanskrit_iast:
mantrayām āsur avyagrāḥ katham indro bhaved iti
tatrāham avadaṃ devān hatyāsthānaṃ prakalpya ca //
meaning:
मन्त्रयाम् आसुर् अव्यग्राः कथम् इन्द्रो भवेद् इति
तत्राहम् अवदं देवान् हत्यास्थानं प्रकल्प्य च //
text_mt: Undismayed, they deliberated: "How can there be an Indra?" / There I spoke to the gods, having assigned a place for the murder:

sanskrit_iast:
indrasya pāvanārthāya gautamyām abhiṣicyatām
yatrābhiṣiktaḥ pūtātmā punar indro bhaviṣyati //
meaning:
इन्द्रस्य पावनार्थाय गौतम्याम् अभिषिच्यताम्
यत्राभिषिक्तः पूतात्मा पुनर् इन्द्रो भविष्यति //
text_mt: "For the purification of Indra, let him be consecrated in the Gautamī; / where, having been consecrated, his self purified, he will again become Indra."

sanskrit_iast:
tathā te niścayaṃ kṛtvā gautamīṃ śīghram āgaman
tatra snātaṃ surapatiṃ devāś ca ṛṣayas tathā //
meaning:
तथा ते निश्चयं कृत्वा गौतमीं शीघ्रम् आगमन्
तत्र स्नातं सुरपतिं देवाश् च ऋषयस् तथा //
text_mt: Having thus made their resolve, they swiftly went to the Gautamī; / there, when the lord of the gods had bathed, the gods and sages likewise,

sanskrit_iast:
abhiṣektukāmās te sarve śacīkāntaṃ ca tasthire
abhiṣicyamānam indraṃ taṃ prakopād gautamo 'bravīt //
meaning:
अभिषेक्तुकामास् ते सर्वे शचीकान्तं च तस्थिरे
अभिषिच्यमानम् इन्द्रं तं प्रकोपाद् गौतमो ऽब्रवीत् //
text_mt: all wishing to consecrate Śacī's beloved, took their stand. / As Indra was being consecrated, Gautama said in great fury:

sanskrit_iast:
gautama uvāca
abhiṣekṣyanti pāpiṣṭhaṃ mahendraṃ gurutalpagam
tān sarvān bhasmasāt kuryāṃ śīghraṃ yāntv asurārayaḥ //
meaning:
गौतम उवाच
अभिषेक्ष्यन्ति पापिष्ठं महेन्द्रं गुरुतल्पगम्
तान् सर्वान् भस्मसात् कुर्यां शीघ्रं यान्त्व् असुरारयः //
text_mt: Gautama said: / "If they consecrate the wicked Mahendra, who defiled his guru's bed, / I will reduce them all to ashes! Let the enemies of the asuras depart swiftly!"

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
tad ṛṣer vacanaṃ śrutvā parihṛtya ca gautamīm
narmadām agaman sarva indram ādāya satvarāḥ //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तद् ऋषेर् वचनं श्रुत्वा परिहृत्य च गौतमीम्
नर्मदाम् अगमन् सर्व इन्द्रम् आदाय सत्वराः //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Hearing that speech of the sage and leaving the Gautamī, / they all quickly took Indra and went to the Narmadā.

sanskrit_iast:
uttare narmadātīre abhiṣekāya tasthire
abhiṣekṣyamāṇam indraṃ taṃ māṇḍavyo bhagavān ṛṣiḥ //
meaning:
उत्तरे नर्मदातीरे अभिषेकाय तस्थिरे
अभिषेक्ष्यमाणम् इन्द्रं तं माण्डव्यो भगवान् ऋषिः //
text_mt: On the northern bank of the Narmadā they stood ready for the consecration. / As Indra was about to be consecrated, the venerable sage Māṇḍavya

sanskrit_iast:
abravīd bhasmasāt kuryāṃ yadi syād abhiṣecanam
pūjayām āsur amarā māṇḍavyaṃ yuktibhiḥ stavaiḥ //
meaning:
अब्रवीद् भस्मसात् कुर्यां यदि स्याद् अभिषेचनम्
पूजयाम् आसुर् अमरा माण्डव्यं युक्तिभिः स्तवैः //
text_mt: said: "I will reduce [you] to ashes if the consecration takes place!" / The immortals worshipped Māṇḍavya with reasoned arguments and hymns of praise.

sanskrit_iast:
devā ūcuḥ
ayam indraḥ sahasrākṣo yasmin deśe 'bhiṣicyate
tatrātidāruṇaṃ vighnaṃ mune samupajāyate //
meaning:
देवा ऊचुः
अयम् इन्द्रः सहस्राक्षो यस्मिन् देशे ऽभिषिच्यते
तत्रातिदारुणं विघ्नं मुने समुपजायते //
text_mt: The gods said: / "In whatever place this thousand-eyed Indra is consecrated, / a very dreadful obstacle arises there, O sage.

sanskrit_iast:
tacchāntiṃ kuru kalyāṇa prasīda varado bhava
malaniryātanaṃ yasmin kurmas tasmin varān bahūn //
meaning:
तच्छान्तिं कुरु कल्याण प्रसीद वरदो भव
मलनिर्यातनं यस्मिन् कुर्मस् तस्मिन् वरान् बहून् //
text_mt: Bring about its appeasement, O auspicious one! Be pleased, be a giver of boons! / In whatever region we perform the removal of his taint,

sanskrit_iast:
deśe dāsyāmahe sarve tad anujñātum arhasi
yasmin deśe surendrasya abhiṣeko bhaviṣyati //
meaning:
देशे दास्यामहे सर्वे तद् अनुज्ञातुम् अर्हसि
यस्मिन् देशे सुरेन्द्रस्य अभिषेको भविष्यति //
text_mt: we shall all grant many boons to that region; you ought to permit it. / In the region where the consecration of the lord of the gods will take place,

sanskrit_iast:
sa sarvakāmadaḥ puṃsāṃ dhānyavṛkṣaphalair yutaḥ
nānāvṛṣṭir na durbhikṣaṃ bhaved atra kadācana //
meaning:
स सर्वकामदः पुंसां धान्यवृक्षफलैर् युतः
नानावृष्टिर् न दुर्भिक्षं भवेद् अत्र कदाचन //
text_mt: it shall grant all desires to men, endowed with grain, trees, and fruits; / here there shall never be untimely rain or famine."

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
mene tato muniśreṣṭho māṇḍavyo lokapūjitaḥ
abhiṣekaḥ kṛtas tatra malaniryātanaṃ tathā //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
मेने ततो मुनिश्रेष्ठो माण्डव्यो लोकपूजितः
अभिषेकः कृतस् तत्र मलनिर्यातनं तथा //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Then the best of sages, Māṇḍavya, revered by the world, assented; / the consecration was performed there, and likewise the removal of the taint.

sanskrit_iast:
devais tadokto munibhiḥ sa deśo mālavas tataḥ
abhiṣikte surapatau jāte ca vimale tadā //
meaning:
देवैस् तदोक्तो मुनिभिः स देशो मालवस् ततः
अभिषिक्ते सुरपतौ जाते च विमले तदा //
text_mt: Because it was addressed then by the gods [and] sages, that region was called Mālava thereafter. / When the lord of the gods was consecrated and had become free of taint,

sanskrit_iast:
ānīya gautamīṃ gaṅgāṃ taṃ puṇyāyābhiṣecire
surāś ca ṛṣayaś caiva ahaṃ viṣṇus tathaiva ca //
meaning:
आनीय गौतमीं गङ्गां तं पुण्यायाभिषेचिरे
सुराश् च ऋषयश् चैव अहं विष्णुस् तथैव च //
text_mt: bringing the Gautamī Gaṅgā, the gods and sages, / and I and Viṣṇu likewise, consecrated him for [greater] sanctity;

sanskrit_iast:
vasiṣṭho gautamaś cāpi agastyo 'triś ca kaśyapaḥ
ete cānye ca ṛṣayo devā yakṣāḥ sapannagāḥ //
meaning:
वसिष्ठो गौतमश् चापि अगस्त्यो ऽत्रिश् च कश्यपः
एते चान्ये च ऋषयो देवा यक्षाः सपन्नगाः //
text_mt: Vasiṣṭha and Gautama, Agastya, Atri, and Kaśyapa, / these and other sages, gods, yakṣas, together with serpents,

sanskrit_iast:
snānaṃ tatpuṇyatoyena akurvann abhiṣecanam
mayā punaḥ śacībhartā kamaṇḍalubhavena ca //
meaning:
स्नानं तत्पुण्यतोयेन अकुर्वन्न् अभिषेचनम्
मया पुनः शचीभर्ता कमण्डलुभवेन च //
text_mt: performed his ablution and consecration with its sacred water. / Furthermore, Śacī's lord was consecrated by me with water arisen from my water-pot,

sanskrit_iast:
vāriṇāpy abhiṣiktaś ca tatra puṇyābhavan nadī
siktā ceti ca tatrāsīt te gaṅgāyāṃ ca saṃgate //
meaning:
वारिणाप्य् अभिषिक्तश् च तत्र पुण्याभवन् नदी
सिक्ता चेति च तत्रासीत् ते गङ्गायां च संगते //
text_mt: and there arose the holy river Puṇyā, / and there was the Siktā; both met at the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃgamau tatra vikhyātau sarvadā munisevitau
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrthaṃ puṇyāsaṃgamam ucyate //
meaning:
संगमौ तत्र विख्यातौ सर्वदा मुनिसेवितौ
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थं पुण्यासंगमम् उच्यते //
text_mt: The two confluences there are renowned, always frequented by sages; / from that time forward that tīrtha is called Puṇyāsaṃgama.

sanskrit_iast:
siktāyāḥ saṃgame puṇyam aindraṃ tad abhidhīyate
tatra sapta sahasrāṇi tīrthāny āsañ śubhāni ca //
meaning:
सिक्तायाः संगमे पुण्यम् ऐन्द्रं तद् अभिधीयते
तत्र सप्त सहस्राणि तीर्थान्य् आसञ् शुभानि च //
text_mt: The confluence of the Siktā is called the holy Aindra tīrtha. / There seven thousand auspicious tīrthas came into being.

sanskrit_iast:
teṣu snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca viśeṣeṇa tu saṃgame
sarvaṃ tad akṣayaṃ vidyān nātra kāryā vicāraṇā //
meaning:
तेषु स्नानं च दानं च विशेषेण तु संगमे
सर्वं तद् अक्षयं विद्यान् नात्र कार्या विचारणा //
text_mt: Bathing and giving in them, especially at the confluence— / one should know all that to be imperishable; there should be no doubt about this.

sanskrit_iast:
yad etat puṇyam ākhyānaṃ yaḥ paṭhec ca śṛṇoti vā
sarvapāpaiḥ sa mucyeta manovākkāyakarmajaiḥ //
meaning:
यद् एतत् पुण्यम् आख्यानं यः पठेच् च शृणोति वा
सर्वपापैः स मुच्येत मनोवाक्कायकर्मजैः //
text_mt: Whoever recites or hears this sacred narrative / will be freed from all sins born of mind, speech, and bodily action.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
paulastyaṃ tīrtham ākhyātaṃ sarvasiddhipradaṃ nṛṇām
prabhāvaṃ tasya vakṣyāmi bhraṣṭarājyapradāyakam //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
पौलस्त्यं तीर्थम् आख्यातं सर्वसिद्धिप्रदं नृणाम्
प्रभावं तस्य वक्ष्यामि भ्रष्टराज्यप्रदायकम् //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / The Paulastya tīrtha has been proclaimed, bestowing all accomplishments on men; / I will declare its power, which restores a lost kingdom.

sanskrit_iast:
uttarāśāpatiḥ pūrvam ṛddhisiddhisamanvitaḥ
purā laṅkāpatiś cāsīj jyeṣṭho viśravasaḥ sutaḥ //
meaning:
उत्तराशापतिः पूर्वम् ऋद्धिसिद्धिसमन्वितः
पुरा लङ्कापतिश् चासीज् ज्येष्ठो विश्रवसः सुतः //
text_mt: Formerly, the lord of the northern quarter, endowed with prosperity and perfection, / the eldest son of Viśravas, was the lord of Laṅkā.

sanskrit_iast:
tasyaite bhrātaraś cāsan balavanto 'mitaprabhāḥ
sāpatnā rāvaṇaś caiva kumbhakarṇo vibhīṣaṇaḥ //
meaning:
तस्यैते भ्रातरश् चासन् बलवन्तो ऽमितप्रभाः
सापत्ना रावणश् चैव कुम्भकर्णो विभीषणः //
text_mt: His half-brothers, mighty and of boundless splendour, / were Rāvaṇa, Kumbhakarṇa, and Vibhīṣaṇa.

sanskrit_iast:
te 'pi viśravasaḥ putrā rākṣasyāṃ rākṣasās tu te
maddattena vimānena dhanado bhrātṛbhiḥ saha //
meaning:
ते ऽपि विश्रवसः पुत्रा राक्षस्यां राक्षसास् तु ते
मद्दत्तेन विमानेन धनदो भ्रातृभिः सह //
text_mt: They too were sons of Viśravas, but born of a rākṣasī, and were rākṣasas. / By means of an aerial chariot given by me, Dhanada, along with his brothers,

sanskrit_iast:
mamāntikaṃ bhaktiyukto nityam eti tu yāti ca
rāvaṇasya tu yā mātā kupitā sābravīt sutān //
meaning:
ममान्तिकं भक्तियुक्तो नित्यम् एति तु याति च
रावणस्य तु या माता कुपिता साब्रवीत् सुतान् //
text_mt: used to come and go constantly into my presence, filled with devotion. / But Rāvaṇa's mother became enraged and spoke to her sons:

sanskrit_iast:
rāvaṇamātovāca
mariṣye na ca jīviṣye putrā vairūpyakāraṇāt
devāś ca dānavāś cāsan sāpatnā bhrātaro mithaḥ //
meaning:
रावणमातोवाच
मरिष्ये न च जीविष्ये पुत्रा वैरूप्यकारणात्
देवाश् च दानवाश् चासन् सापत्ना भ्रातरो मिथः //
text_mt: Rāvaṇa's mother said: / "I shall die, I will not live, O sons, on account of this humiliation! / The gods and the dānavas were half-brothers to one another;

sanskrit_iast:
anyonyavadham īpsante jayaiśvaryavaśānugāḥ
tadbhavanto na puruṣā na śaktā na jayaiṣiṇaḥ
sāpatnyaṃ yo 'numanyate tasya jīvo nirarthakaḥ //
meaning:
अन्योन्यवधम् ईप्सन्ते जयैश्वर्यवशानुगाः
तद्भवन्तो न पुरुषा न शक्ता न जयैषिणः
सापत्न्यं यो ऽनुमन्यते तस्य जीवो निरर्थकः //
text_mt: subject to the sway of victory and sovereignty, they seek each other's destruction. / Therefore you are not men, nor powerful, nor desirous of victory! / Whoever tolerates rivalry with a co-wife's son, his life is meaningless!"

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
tan mātṛvacanaṃ śrutvā bhrātaras te trayo mune
jagmus te tapase 'raṇyaṃ kṛtavantas tapo mahat //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तन् मातृवचनं श्रुत्वा भ्रातरस् ते त्रयो मुने
जग्मुस् ते तपसे ऽरण्यं कृतवन्तस् तपो महत् //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Hearing that speech of their mother, those three brothers, O sage, / went to the forest for austerities and performed great asceticism.

sanskrit_iast:
matto varān avāpuś ca traya ete ca rākṣasāḥ
mātulena marīcena tathā mātāmahena tu //
meaning:
मत्तो वरान् अवापुश् च त्रय एते च राक्षसाः
मातुलेन मरीचेन तथा मातामहेन तु //
text_mt: And from me these three rākṣasas obtained boons. / At the instigation of their maternal uncle Marīca and also their maternal grandfather,

sanskrit_iast:
tanmātṛvacanāc cāpi tato laṅkām ayācata
rakṣobhāvān mātṛdoṣād bhrātror vairam abhūn mahat //
meaning:
तन्मातृवचनाच् चापि ततो लङ्काम् अयाचत
रक्षोभावान् मातृदोषाद् भ्रात्रोर् वैरम् अभून् महत् //
text_mt: and by their mother's word, [Rāvaṇa] then demanded Laṅkā. / Due to the rākṣasa nature and the mother's fault, great enmity arose between the two brothers.

sanskrit_iast:
tatas tad abhavad yuddhaṃ devadānavayor iva
yuddhe jitvāgrajaṃ śāntaṃ dhanadaṃ bhrātaraṃ tathā //
meaning:
ततस् तद् अभवद् युद्धं देवदानवयोर् इव
युद्धे जित्वाग्रजं शान्तं धनदं भ्रातरं तथा //
text_mt: Then a battle took place like that between the gods and dānavas; / having conquered in battle his peaceful elder brother Dhanada,

sanskrit_iast:
puṣpakaṃ ca purīṃ laṅkāṃ sarvaṃ caiva vyapāharat
rāvaṇo ghoṣayām āsa trailokye sacarācare //
meaning:
पुष्पकं च पुरीं लङ्कां सर्वं चैव व्यपाहरत्
रावणो घोषयाम् आस त्रैलोक्ये सचराचरे //
text_mt: he seized the Puṣpaka, the city of Laṅkā, and everything else. / Rāvaṇa caused a proclamation to be made throughout the three worlds, with all that is moving and unmoving:

sanskrit_iast:
yo dadyād āśrayaṃ bhrātuḥ sa ca vadhyo bhaven mama
bhrātrā nirasto vaiśravaṇo naiva prāpāśrayaṃ kvacit
pitāmahaṃ pulastyaṃ taṃ gatvā natvābravīd vacaḥ //
meaning:
यो दद्याद् आश्रयं भ्रातुः स च वध्यो भवेन् मम
भ्रात्रा निरस्तो वैश्रवणो नैव प्रापाश्रयं क्वचित्
पितामहं पुलस्त्यं तं गत्वा नत्वाब्रवीद् वचः //
text_mt: "Whoever gives shelter to my brother, he shall be killed by me!" / Banished by his brother, Vaiśravaṇa found no shelter anywhere; / going to his grandfather Pulastya and bowing down, he spoke these words:

sanskrit_iast:
dhanada uvāca
bhrātrā nirasto duṣṭena kiṃ karomi vadasva me
āśrayaḥ śaraṇaṃ yat syād daivaṃ vā tīrtham eva ca //
meaning:
धनद उवाच
भ्रात्रा निरस्तो दुष्टेन किं करोमि वदस्व मे
आश्रयः शरणं यत् स्याद् दैवं वा तीर्थम् एव च //
text_mt: Dhanada said: / "Banished by my wicked brother, tell me, what should I do? / What shelter, refuge, deity, or tīrtha may there be?"

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
tat pautravacanaṃ śrutvā pulastyo vākyam abravīt //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तत् पौत्रवचनं श्रुत्वा पुलस्त्यो वाक्यम् अब्रवीत् //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Hearing that speech of his grandson, Pulastya spoke these words:

sanskrit_iast:
pulastya uvāca
gautamīṃ gaccha putra tvaṃ stuhi devaṃ maheśvaram
tatra nāsya praveśaḥ syād gaṅgāyā jalamadhyataḥ //
meaning:
पुलस्त्य उवाच
गौतमीं गच्छ पुत्र त्वं स्तुहि देवं महेश्वरम्
तत्र नास्य प्रवेशः स्याद् गङ्गाया जलमध्यतः //
text_mt: Pulastya said: / "Go to the Gautamī, O son, and praise the god Maheśvara; / he cannot enter there, within the water of the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit_iast: siddhiṃ prāpsyasi kalyāṇīṃ tathā kuru mayā saha //
meaning: सिद्धिं प्राप्स्यसि कल्याणीं तथा कुरु मया सह //
text_mt: You will attain auspicious success; do so together with me."

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
tathety uktvā jagāmāsau sabhāryo dhanadas tathā
pitrā mātrā ca vṛddhena pulastyena dhaneśvaraḥ //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तथेत्य् उक्त्वा जगामासौ सभार्यो धनदस् तथा
पित्रा मात्रा च वृद्धेन पुलस्त्येन धनेश्वरः //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Saying "So be it," Dhanada departed with his wife; / and together with his father, mother, and aged Pulastya, the lord of wealth went.

sanskrit_iast:
gatvā tu gautamīṃ gaṅgāṃ śuciḥ snātvā yatavrataḥ
tuṣṭāva devadeveśaṃ bhuktimuktipradaṃ śivam //
meaning:
गत्वा तु गौतमीं गङ्गां शुचिः स्नात्वा यतव्रतः
तुष्टाव देवदेवेशं भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदं शिवम् //
text_mt: Having gone to the Gautamī Gaṅgā, purified, having bathed and restrained his vows, / he praised Śiva, the lord of the gods, who bestows worldly enjoyment and liberation:

sanskrit_iast:
dhanada uvāca
svāmī tvam evāsya carācarasya
viśvasya śaṃbho na paro 'sti kaścit
tvām apy avajñāya yadīha mohāt
pragalbhate kopi sa śocya eva
meaning:
धनद उवाच
स्वामी त्वम् एवास्य चराचरस्य
विश्वस्य शंभो न परो ऽस्ति कश्चित्
त्वाम् अप्य् अवज्ञाय यदीह मोहात्
प्रगल्भते कोपि स शोच्य एव
text_mt: Dhanada said: / "You alone are the master of this universe, moving and unmoving, / O Śambhu; there is none other! / If anyone here, having disregarded even you, should behave insolently / out of delusion, he is truly to be pitied."

sanskrit_iast:
tvam aṣṭamūrtyā sakalaṃ bibharṣi
tvadājñayā vartata eva sarvam
tathāpi vedeti budho bhavantaṃ
na jātv avidvān mahimā purātanam
meaning:
त्वम् अष्टमूर्त्या सकलं बिभर्षि
त्वदाज्ञया वर्तत एव सर्वम्
तथापि वेदेति बुधो भवन्तं
न जात्व् अविद्वान् महिमा पुरातनम्
text_mt: You support everything through your eightfold form; / everything moves solely by your command. / Even so, the wise man knows you as such, / while the ignorant man never knows your primeval majesty.

sanskrit_iast:
malaprasūtaṃ yad avocad ambā
hāsyāt suto 'yaṃ tava deva śūraḥ
tvatprekṣitād yaḥ sa ca vighnarājo
jajñe tv aho ceṣṭitam īśadṛṣṭeḥ
meaning:
मलप्रसूतं यद् अवोचद् अम्बा
हास्यात् सुतो ऽयं तव देव शूरः
त्वत्प्रेक्षिताद् यः स च विघ्नराजो
जज्ञे त्व् अहो चेष्टितम् ईशदृष्टेः
text_mt: When the Mother said in jest of what was born from bodily impurity, / 'This heroic child is your son, O Lord,' / and that Lord of Obstacles was born from your gaze— / oh, how wondrous is the action of the Lord's glance!

sanskrit_iast:
aśruplutāṅgī girijā samīkṣya
viyuktadāṃpatyam itīśam ūce
manobhavo 'bhūn madano ratiś ca
saubhāgyapūrvatvam avāpa somāt
meaning:
अश्रुप्लुताङ्गी गिरिजा समीक्ष्य
वियुक्तदांपत्यम् इतीशम् ऊचे
मनोभवो ऽभून् मदनो रतिश् च
सौभाग्यपूर्वत्वम् अवाप सोमात्
text_mt: Seeing the mountain-born goddess her limbs bathed in tears, / the Lord said thus: 'Let the couple be reunited.' / Love, born of the mind, came to life, and Rati / attained her former good fortune from Soma.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
ityādi stuvatas tasya purato 'bhūt trilocanaḥ
vareṇa cchandayām āsa harṣān novāca kiṃcana //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इत्यादि स्तुवतस् तस्य पुरतो ऽभूत् त्रिलोचनः
वरेण च्छन्दयाम् आस हर्षान् नोवाच किंचन //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / As he was praising him thus, the three-eyed Lord appeared before him / and offered him a boon; out of joy he said nothing at all.

sanskrit_iast:
tūṣṇīṃbhūte tu dhanade pulastye ca maheśvare
punaḥ punar varasveti śive vādini harṣite //
meaning:
तूष्णींभूते तु धनदे पुलस्त्ये च महेश्वरे
पुनः पुनर् वरस्वेति शिवे वादिनि हर्षिते //
text_mt: While Dhanada fell silent, and Pulastya and Maheśvara were there, / and Śiva, delighted, repeatedly said, 'Choose a boon!'—

sanskrit_iast:
etasminn antare tatra vāg uvācāśarīriṇī
prāptavyaṃ dhanapālatvaṃ vadantīdaṃ maheśvaram //
meaning:
एतस्मिन्न् अन्तरे तत्र वाग् उवाचाशरीरिणी
प्राप्तव्यं धनपालत्वं वदन्तीदं महेश्वरम् //
text_mt: at that moment a bodiless voice spoke there, / saying this to Maheśvara: 'He must attain the guardianship of wealth.'

sanskrit_iast:
pulastyasya tu yac cittaṃ pitur vaiśravaṇasya tu
viditveva tadā vāṇī śubham artham udīrayat //
meaning:
पुलस्त्यस्य तु यच् चित्तं पितुर् वैश्रवणस्य तु
विदित्वेव तदा वाणी शुभम् अर्थम् उदीरयत् //
text_mt: As though knowing the mind of Pulastya / and of the father Vaiśravaṇa, the voice then uttered an auspicious purpose:

sanskrit_iast:
bhūtavad bhavitavyaṃ syād dāsyamānaṃ tu dattavat
prāptavyaṃ prāptavat tatra daivī vāg abhavac chubhā //
meaning:
भूतवद् भवितव्यं स्याद् दास्यमानं तु दत्तवत्
प्राप्तव्यं प्राप्तवत् तत्र दैवी वाग् अभवच् छुभा //
text_mt: 'Let what must be happen as though already done, and what is to be given as though already given; / let what is to be attained be as though attained.' There the divine voice was auspicious.

sanskrit_iast:
prabhūtaśatruḥ paribhūtaduḥkhaḥ
saṃpūjya someśvaram āpa liṅgam
digīśvaratvaṃ draviṇaprabhutvam
apāradātṛtvakalatraputrān
meaning:
प्रभूतशत्रुः परिभूतदुःखः
संपूज्य सोमेश्वरम् आप लिङ्गम्
दिगीश्वरत्वं द्रविणप्रभुत्वम्
अपारदातृत्वकलत्रपुत्रान्
text_mt: Having abundant enemies and overcoming his sorrow, / he worshipped the liṅga Someśvara and attained / lordship over the directions, mastery of wealth, / boundless generosity, wives, and sons.

sanskrit_iast:
tāṃ vācaṃ dhanadaḥ śrutvā devadevaṃ triśūlinam
evaṃ bhavatu nāmeti dhanado vākyam abravīt //
meaning:
तां वाचं धनदः श्रुत्वा देवदेवं त्रिशूलिनम्
एवं भवतु नामेति धनदो वाक्यम् अब्रवीत् //
text_mt: Hearing that voice, Dhanada addressed the God of Gods, / the trident-bearer, saying: 'So be it indeed.'

sanskrit_iast:
tathaivāstv iti deveśo daivīṃ vācam amanyata
pulastyaṃ ca varaiḥ puṇyais tathā viśravasaṃ munim //
meaning:
तथैवास्त्व् इति देवेशो दैवीं वाचम् अमन्यत
पुलस्त्यं च वरैः पुण्यैस् तथा विश्रवसं मुनिम् //
text_mt: The Lord of the Gods assented to the divine voice, saying, 'So let it be,' / and gratified Pulastya with holy boons, as well as the sage Viśravas.

sanskrit_iast:
dhanapālaṃ ca deveśo hy abhinandya yayau śivaḥ
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrthaṃ paulastyaṃ dhanadaṃ viduḥ //
meaning:
धनपालं च देवेशो ह्य् अभिनन्द्य ययौ शिवः
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थं पौलस्त्यं धनदं विदुः //
text_mt: The Lord of the Gods, Śiva, commended Dhanapāla and departed. / From that time forth, they know that holy bathing place as Paulastya and Dhanada.

sanskrit_iast:
tathā vaiśravasaṃ puṇyaṃ sarvakāmapradaṃ śubham
teṣu snānādi yat kiṃcit tat sarvaṃ bahupuṇyadam //
meaning:
तथा वैश्रवसं पुण्यं सर्वकामप्रदं शुभम्
तेषु स्नानादि यत् किंचित् तत् सर्वं बहुपुण्यदम् //
text_mt: And likewise the holy Vaiśravasa, auspicious, granting all desires. / Whatever bathing and other rites are performed there, all that bestows great merit.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
agnitīrtham iti khyātaṃ sarvakratuphalapradam
sarvavighnopaśamanaṃ tattīrthasya phalaṃ śṛṇu //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
अग्नितीर्थम् इति ख्यातं सर्वक्रतुफलप्रदम्
सर्वविघ्नोपशमनं तत्तीर्थस्य फलं शृणु //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Renowned as Agnitīrtha, it grants the fruit of all rituals / and pacifies all obstacles. Hear the fruit of that holy place:

sanskrit_iast:
jātavedā iti khyāto agner bhrātā sa havyavāṭ
havyaṃ vahantaṃ devānāṃ gautamyās tīra eva tu //
meaning:
जातवेदा इति ख्यातो अग्नेर् भ्राता स हव्यवाट्
हव्यं वहन्तं देवानां गौतम्यास् तीर एव तु //
text_mt: Known as Jātavedas, he was Agni's brother, the bearer of oblations. / As he was carrying the sacrificial offering of the gods on the very bank of the Gautamī,

sanskrit_iast:
ṛṣīṇāṃ sattrasadane agner bhrātaram uttamam
bhrātuḥ priyaṃ tathā dakṣaṃ madhur ditisuto balī //
meaning:
ऋषीणां सत्त्रसदने अग्नेर् भ्रातरम् उत्तमम्
भ्रातुः प्रियं तथा दक्षं मधुर् दितिसुतो बली //
text_mt: in the sacrificial hall of the sages, that excellent brother of Agni, / dear to his brother and capable, the mighty Diti-son Madhu

sanskrit_iast:
jaghāna ṛṣimukhyeṣu paśyatsu ca sureṣv api
havyaṃ devā naiva cāpur mṛte vai jātavedasi //
meaning:
जघान ऋषिमुख्येषु पश्यत्सु च सुरेष्व् अपि
हव्यं देवा नैव चापुर् मृते वै जातवेदसि //
text_mt: slew, while the foremost sages and even the gods looked on. / And when Jātavedas was dead, the gods obtained no sacrificial food at all.

sanskrit_iast:
mṛte bhrātari sa tv agniḥ priye vai jātavedasi
kopena mahatāviṣṭo gāṅgam ambhaḥ samāviśat //
meaning:
मृते भ्रातरि स त्व् अग्निः प्रिये वै जातवेदसि
कोपेन महताविष्टो गाङ्गम् अम्भः समाविशत् //
text_mt: When his brother, his dear Jātavedas, was dead, / Agni, overcome with great rage, plunged into the waters of the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit_iast:
gaṅgāmbhasi samāviṣṭe hy agnau devāś ca mānuṣāḥ
jīvam utsarjayām āsur agnijīvā yato matāḥ //
meaning:
गङ्गाम्भसि समाविष्टे ह्य् अग्नौ देवाश् च मानुषाः
जीवम् उत्सर्जयाम् आसुर् अग्निजीवा यतो मताः //
text_mt: When Agni had entered the waters of the Gaṅgā, gods and humans / abandoned their life-breath, since they are considered to live by fire.

sanskrit_iast:
yatrāgnir jalam āviṣṭas taṃ deśaṃ sarva eva te
ājagmur vibudhāḥ sarva ṛṣayaḥ pitaras tathā //
meaning:
यत्राग्निर् जलम् आविष्टस् तं देशं सर्व एव ते
आजग्मुर् विबुधाः सर्व ऋषयः पितरस् तथा //
text_mt: Where Agni had entered the water, to that place all of them came— / all the deities, the sages, and the ancestors.

sanskrit_iast:
vināgninā na jīvāmaḥ stuvanto 'gniṃ viśeṣataḥ
agniṃ jalagataṃ dṛṣṭvā priyaṃ cocur divaukasaḥ //
meaning:
विनाग्निना न जीवामः स्तुवन्तो ऽग्निं विशेषतः
अग्निं जलगतं दृष्ट्वा प्रियं चोचुर् दिवौकसः //
text_mt: Saying, 'Without fire we do not live,' praising Agni exceedingly, / and seeing Agni residing in the water, the denizens of heaven spoke kindly to him.

sanskrit_iast:
devā ūcuḥ
devāñ jīvaya havyena kavyena ca pitṝṃs tathā
mānuṣān annapākena bījānāṃ kledanena ca //
meaning:
देवा ऊचुः
देवाञ् जीवय हव्येन कव्येन च पितॄंस् तथा
मानुषान् अन्नपाकेन बीजानां क्लेदनेन च //
text_mt: The gods said: / Revive the gods with the offering to the gods, and likewise the ancestors with the offering to the manes, / and humans by the cooking of food and the moistening of seeds.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
agnir apy āha tān devāñ śakto yo me gato 'nujaḥ
kriyamāṇe bhavatkārye yā gatir jātavedasaḥ //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
अग्निर् अप्य् आह तान् देवाञ् शक्तो यो मे गतो ऽनुजः
क्रियमाणे भवत्कार्ये या गतिर् जातवेदसः //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Agni also said to those gods: 'My capable younger brother is gone; / the fate that befell Jātavedas while performing your task,

sanskrit_iast:
sā vāpi syān mama surā notsahe kāryasādhane
kāryaṃ tu sarvatas tasya bhavatāṃ jātavedasaḥ //
meaning:
सा वापि स्यान् मम सुरा नोत्सहे कार्यसाधने
कार्यं तु सर्वतस् तस्य भवतां जातवेदसः //
text_mt: that very fate may befall me too, O gods; I dare not accomplish the task. / Yet that task of yours was accomplished everywhere by Jātavedas.

sanskrit_iast:
imāṃ sthitim anuprāpto na jāne me kathaṃ bhavet
iha cāmutra ca vyāptau śaktir apy atra no bhavet //
meaning:
इमां स्थितिम् अनुप्राप्तो न जाने मे कथं भवेत्
इह चामुत्र च व्याप्तौ शक्तिर् अप्य् अत्र नो भवेत् //
text_mt: Having reached this state, I do not know how it will be for me; / nor would I have the power to pervade both here and the hereafter.'

sanskrit_iast:
athāpi kriyamāṇe vai kārye saiva gatir mama
devās tam ūcur bhāvena sarveṇa ṛṣayas tathā //
meaning:
अथापि क्रियमाणे वै कार्ये सैव गतिर् मम
देवास् तम् ऊचुर् भावेन सर्वेण ऋषयस् तथा //
text_mt: And yet, [he said,] 'If the task is performed, that same fate will be mine.' / The gods and the sages spoke to him with all affection:

sanskrit_iast:
āyuḥ karmaṇi ca prītir vyāptau śaktiś ca dīyate
prayājān anuyājāṃś ca dāsyāmo havyavāhana //
meaning:
आयुः कर्मणि च प्रीतिर् व्याप्तौ शक्तिश् च दीयते
प्रयाजान् अनुयाजांश् च दास्यामो हव्यवाहन //
text_mt: 'Longevity and pleasure in your work, and the power of pervasion are granted; / and we shall grant the fore-offerings and the after-offerings, O bearer of oblations!

sanskrit_iast:
devānāṃ tvaṃ mukhaṃ śreṣṭham āhutyaḥ prathamās tava
tvayā dattaṃ tu yad dravyaṃ bhokṣyāmaḥ surasattama //
meaning:
देवानां त्वं मुखं श्रेष्ठम् आहुत्यः प्रथमास् तव
त्वया दत्तं तु यद् द्रव्यं भोक्ष्यामः सुरसत्तम //
text_mt: You are the supreme mouth of the gods; the first offerings are yours; / whatever substance is given by you, that we shall enjoy, O best of gods!'

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
tatas tuṣṭo 'bhavad vahnir devavākyād yathākramam
iha cāmutra ca vyāptau havye vā laukike tathā //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततस् तुष्टो ऽभवद् वह्निर् देववाक्याद् यथाक्रमम्
इह चामुत्र च व्याप्तौ हव्ये वा लौकिके तथा //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Then fire was satisfied in due course by the word of the gods, / to pervade both here and the hereafter, whether in the sacred offering or in worldly affairs.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvatra vahnir abhayaḥ samartho 'bhūt surājñayā
jātavedā bṛhadbhānuḥ saptārcir nīlalohitaḥ //
meaning:
सर्वत्र वह्निर् अभयः समर्थो ऽभूत् सुराज्ञया
जातवेदा बृहद्भानुः सप्तार्चिर् नीललोहितः //
text_mt: Fire became fearless and capable everywhere by the command of the gods— / Jātavedas, Bṛhadbhānu, seven-flamed, blue-and-red;

sanskrit_iast:
jalagarbhaḥ śamīgarbho yajñagarbhaḥ sa ucyate
jalād ākṛṣya vibudhā abhiṣicya vibhāvasum //
meaning:
जलगर्भः शमीगर्भो यज्ञगर्भः स उच्यते
जलाद् आकृष्य विबुधा अभिषिच्य विभावसुम् //
text_mt: he is called born of the water, born of the śamī tree, and born of the sacrifice. / Having drawn the fire out of the water and consecrated him,

sanskrit_iast:
ubhayatra pade vāsaḥ sarvago 'gnis tato 'bhavat
yathāgataṃ surā jagmur vahnitīrthaṃ tad ucyate //
meaning:
उभयत्र पदे वासः सर्वगो ऽग्निस् ततो ऽभवत्
यथागतं सुरा जग्मुर् वह्नितीर्थं तद् उच्यते //
text_mt: fire then became all-pervading, dwelling in both realms. / The gods went away as they had come; that is called Vahnitīrtha.

sanskrit_iast:
tatra sapta śatāny āsaṃs tīrthāni guṇavanti ca
teṣu snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca yaḥ karoti jitātmavān //
meaning:
तत्र सप्त शतान्य् आसंस् तीर्थानि गुणवन्ति च
तेषु स्नानं च दानं च यः करोति जितात्मवान् //
text_mt: There were seven hundred virtuous holy places there; / whoever performs bathing and giving in them, self-controlled,

sanskrit_iast:
aśvamedhaphalaṃ sāgraṃ prāpnoty avikalaṃ śubham
devatīrthaṃ ca tatraiva āgneyaṃ jātavedasam //
meaning:
अश्वमेधफलं साग्रं प्राप्नोत्य् अविकलं शुभम्
देवतीर्थं च तत्रैव आग्नेयं जातवेदसम् //
text_mt: obtains the complete, entire, auspicious fruit of a horse-sacrifice. / Right there is the Devatīrtha, related to Agni and Jātavedas.

sanskrit_iast:
agnipratiṣṭhitaṃ liṅgaṃ tatrāste 'nekavarṇavat
taddevadarśanād eva sarvakratuphalaṃ labhet //
meaning:
अग्निप्रतिष्ठितं लिङ्गं तत्रास्ते ऽनेकवर्णवत्
तद्देवदर्शनाद् एव सर्वक्रतुफलं लभेत् //
text_mt: A liṅga established by Agni stands there, having various colors; / merely by seeing that deity, one obtains the fruit of all sacrifices.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
ṛṇapramocanaṃ nāma tīrthaṃ vedavido viduḥ
tasya svarūpaṃ vakṣyāmi śṛṇu nārada tanmanāḥ //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ऋणप्रमोचनं नाम तीर्थं वेदविदो विदुः
तस्य स्वरूपं वक्ष्यामि शृणु नारद तन्मनाः //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Those who know the Vedas know of a holy place named Ṛṇapramocana; / I shall explain its nature—listen with attentive mind, O Nārada!

sanskrit_iast:
āsīt pṛthuśravā nāma priyaḥ kakṣīvataḥ sutaḥ
na dārasaṃgrahaṃ lebhe vairāgyān nāgnipūjanam //
meaning:
आसीत् पृथुश्रवा नाम प्रियः कक्षीवतः सुतः
न दारसंग्रहं लेभे वैराग्यान् नाग्निपूजनम् //
text_mt: There was a dear son of Kakṣīvat named Pṛthuśravas; / because of dispassion, he did not take a wife nor did he worship the sacred fires.

sanskrit_iast:
kanīyāṃs tu samartho 'pi parivittibhayān mune
nākarod dārakarmādi naivāgnīnām upāsanam //
meaning:
कनीयांस् तु समर्थो ऽपि परिवित्तिभयान् मुने
नाकरोद् दारकर्मादि नैवाग्नीनाम् उपासनम् //
text_mt: The younger brother, though capable, out of fear of marrying before his elder brother, O sage, / did not perform the marriage rites and so forth, nor did he attend to the fires.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ procuḥ pitṛgaṇāḥ putraṃ kakṣīvataḥ śubham
jyeṣṭhaṃ caiva kaniṣṭhaṃ ca pṛthak pṛthag idaṃ vacaḥ //
meaning:
ततः प्रोचुः पितृगणाः पुत्रं कक्षीवतः शुभम्
ज्येष्ठं चैव कनिष्ठं च पृथक् पृथग् इदं वचः //
text_mt: Then the hosts of ancestors addressed the auspicious sons of Kakṣīvat, / the elder and the younger, each with these words:

sanskrit_iast:
pitara ūcuḥ
ṛṇatrayāpanodāya kriyatāṃ dārasaṃgrahaḥ //
meaning:
पितर ऊचुः
ऋणत्रयापनोदाय क्रियतां दारसंग्रहः //
text_mt: The ancestors said: / 'To dispel the three debts, let marriage be undertaken!'

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
nety uvāca tato jyeṣṭhaḥ kim ṛṇaṃ kena yujyate
kanīyāṃs tu pitṝn prāha na yogyo dārasaṃgrahaḥ //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
नेत्य् उवाच ततो ज्येष्ठः किम् ऋणं केन युज्यते
कनीयांस् तु पितॄन् प्राह न योग्यो दारसंग्रहः //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Then the elder said, 'No! What debt is bound to whom?' / But the younger said to the ancestors, 'Marriage is not proper for me

sanskrit_iast:
jyeṣṭhe sati mahāprājñaḥ parivittibhayād iti
tāv ubhau punar apy evam ūcus te vai pitāmahāḥ //
meaning:
ज्येष्ठे सति महाप्राज्ञः परिवित्तिभयाद् इति
ताव् उभौ पुनर् अप्य् एवम् ऊचुस् ते वै पितामहाः //
text_mt: while the elder is here, out of fear of marrying before the elder,' O very wise one. / To both of them those grandfathers spoke again thus:

sanskrit_iast:
pitara ūcuḥ
yātām ubhau gautamīṃ tu puṇyāṃ kakṣīvataḥ sutau
kurutāṃ gautamīsnānaṃ sarvābhīṣṭapradāyakam //
meaning:
पितर ऊचुः
याताम् उभौ गौतमीं तु पुण्यां कक्षीवतः सुतौ
कुरुतां गौतमीस्नानं सर्वाभीष्टप्रदायकम् //
text_mt: The ancestors said: / 'Let both sons of Kakṣīvat go to the holy Gautamī; / perform the Gautamī bath, which grants all desired things.'

sanskrit_iast:
gacchatāṃ gautamīṃ gaṅgāṃ lokatritayapāvanīm
snānaṃ ca tarpaṇaṃ tasyāṃ kurutāṃ śraddhayānvitau //
meaning:
गच्छतां गौतमीं गङ्गां लोकत्रितयपावनीम्
स्नानं च तर्पणं तस्यां कुरुतां श्रद्धयान्वितौ //
text_mt: “Let them go to the Gautamī Gaṅgā, the purifier of the three worlds, / and let both perform bathing and water-offerings in it, endowed with faith.

sanskrit_iast:
dṛṣṭāvanāmitā dhyātā gautamī sarvakāmadā
na deśakālajātyādiniyamo 'trāvagāhane
jyeṣṭho 'nṛṇas tato bhūyāt parivittir na cetaraḥ //
meaning:
दृष्टावनामिता ध्याता गौतमी सर्वकामदा
न देशकालजात्यादिनियमो ऽत्रावगाहने
ज्येष्ठो ऽनृणस् ततो भूयात् परिवित्तिर् न चेतरः //
text_mt: When seen, bowed to, and meditated upon, the Gautamī fulfills all desires. / There is no restriction of place, time, caste, or anything else for plunging into it here. / Then the elder brother will be free of debt, and the other will not become a younger brother married before the elder.”

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
tataḥ pṛthuśravā jyeṣṭhaḥ kṛtvā snānaṃ satarpaṇam
trayāṇām api lokānāṃ kākṣīvato 'nṛṇo 'bhavat //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततः पृथुश्रवा ज्येष्ठः कृत्वा स्नानं सतर्पणम्
त्रयाणाम् अपि लोकानां काक्षीवतो ऽनृणो ऽभवत् //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Then Pṛthuśravas, the elder, having performed the bath together with water-offerings, / Kakṣīvat’s son, became free of debt to the three worlds as well.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrtham ṛṇamocanam ucyate
śrautasmārta-ṛṇebhyaś ca itarebhyaś ca nārada
tatra snānena dānena ṛṇī muktaḥ sukhī bhavet //
meaning:
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थम् ऋणमोचनम् उच्यते
श्रौतस्मार्त-ऋणेभ्यश् च इतरेभ्यश् च नारद
तत्र स्नानेन दानेन ऋणी मुक्तः सुखी भवेत् //
text_mt: From then on, that sacred place is called Ṛṇamocana. / From debts prescribed by Vedic and traditional authority, and from others, O Nārada, / by bathing and giving gifts there, a debtor will become free and happy.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
suparṇāsaṃgamaṃ nāma kādravāsaṃgamaṃ tathā
maheśvaro yatra devo gaṅgāpulinam āśritaḥ //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
सुपर्णासंगमं नाम काद्रवासंगमं तथा
महेश्वरो यत्र देवो गङ्गापुलिनम् आश्रितः //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / There is the confluence called Suparṇāsaṃgama, and likewise the Kādravāsaṃgama, / where the god Maheśvara resides on the sandy bank of the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit_iast:
agnikuṇḍaṃ ca tatraiva raudraṃ vaiṣṇavam eva ca
sauraṃ saumyaṃ tathā brāhmaṃ kaumāraṃ vāruṇaṃ tathā //
meaning:
अग्निकुण्डं च तत्रैव रौद्रं वैष्णवम् एव च
सौरं सौम्यं तथा ब्राह्मं कौमारं वारुणं तथा //
text_mt: And right there is the Agnikuṇḍa, and the pool belonging to Rudra, that to Viṣṇu, / that to Sūrya, that to Soma, likewise to Brahmā, to Kumāra, and likewise to Varuṇa;

sanskrit_iast:
apsarā ca nadī yatra saṃgatā gaṅgayā tathā
tattīrthasmaraṇād eva kṛtakṛtyo bhaven naraḥ //
meaning:
अप्सरा च नदी यत्र संगता गङ्गया तथा
तत्तीर्थस्मरणाद् एव कृतकृत्यो भवेन् नरः //
text_mt: and where the Apsaras River also joins with the Gaṅgā. / Merely from remembering that sacred place, a man will have accomplished his purpose.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvapāpapraśamanaṃ śṛṇu yatnena nārada
indreṇa hiṃsitāḥ pūrvaṃ vālakhilyā maharṣayaḥ
dattārdhatapasaḥ sarve procus te kāśyapaṃ munim //
meaning:
सर्वपापप्रशमनं शृणु यत्नेन नारद
इन्द्रेण हिंसिताः पूर्वं वालखिल्या महर्षयः
दत्तार्धतपसः सर्वे प्रोचुस् ते काश्यपं मुनिम् //
text_mt: Listen attentively, O Nārada, to that which quells all sins. / Formerly, the great sages, the Vālakhilyas, were harmed by Indra. / Having offered half their ascetic fervor, they all spoke to the sage Kaśyapa.

sanskrit_iast:
vālakhilyā ūcuḥ
putram utpādayānena indradarpaharaṃ śubham
tapaso 'rdhaṃ tu dāsyāmas tathety āha munis tu tān //
meaning:
वालखिल्या ऊचुः
पुत्रम् उत्पादयानेन इन्द्रदर्पहरं शुभम्
तपसो ऽर्धं तु दास्यामस् तथेत्य् आह मुनिस् तु तान् //
text_mt: The Vālakhilyas said: / “By means of this, beget an auspicious son who will destroy Indra’s pride. / We shall give half our ascetic fervor.” The sage said to them: “So be it.”

sanskrit_iast:
suparṇāyāṃ tato garbham ādadhe sa prajāpatiḥ
kadrvāṃ caiva śanair brahman sarpāṇāṃ sarpamātari //
meaning:
सुपर्णायां ततो गर्भम् आदधे स प्रजापतिः
कद्र्वां चैव शनैर् ब्रह्मन् सर्पाणां सर्पमातरि //
text_mt: Then that lord of creatures placed an embryo in Suparṇā, / and also, O brahman, slowly in Kadrū, the mother of serpents.

sanskrit_iast:
te garbhiṇyāv ubhe āha gantukāmaḥ prajāpatiḥ
aparādho na ca kvāpi kāryo gamanam eva ca //
meaning:
ते गर्भिण्याव् उभे आह गन्तुकामः प्रजापतिः
अपराधो न च क्वापि कार्यो गमनम् एव च //
text_mt: Desiring to depart, the lord of creatures said to both pregnant wives: / “No transgression must be committed anywhere, nor should you wander away.

sanskrit_iast: anyatra gamanāc chāpo bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ //
meaning: अन्यत्र गमनाच् छापो भविष्यति न संशयः //
text_mt: From going elsewhere, a curse will follow without doubt.”

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
ity uktvā sa yayau patnyau gate bhartari te ubhe
tadaiva jagmatuḥ sattram ṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इत्य् उक्त्वा स ययौ पत्न्यौ गते भर्तरि ते उभे
तदैव जग्मतुः सत्त्रम् ऋषीणां भावितात्मनाम् //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Having spoken thus, he went away. When their husband had departed, those two wives / went right then to a sacrificial session of the sages of purified self,

sanskrit_iast:
brahmavṛndasamākīrṇaṃ gaṅgātīrasamāśritam
unmatte te ubhe nityaṃ vayaḥsaṃpattigarvite //
meaning:
ब्रह्मवृन्दसमाकीर्णं गङ्गातीरसमाश्रितम्
उन्मत्ते ते उभे नित्यं वयःसंपत्तिगर्विते //
text_mt: which was crowded with an assembly of Brahmā’s offspring, situated on the bank of the Gaṅgā. / Those two were continually reckless, proud of their youth and prosperity.

sanskrit_iast:
nivāryamāṇe bahuśo munibhis tattvadarśibhiḥ
vikurvatyau tatra sattre samāni ca havīṃṣi ca //
meaning:
निवार्यमाणे बहुशो मुनिभिस् तत्त्वदर्शिभिः
विकुर्वत्यौ तत्र सत्त्रे समानि च हवींषि च //
text_mt: Though restrained many times by the sages who saw reality, / they disrupted the sacrificial offerings and sacrificial materials in that sacrificial session.

sanskrit_iast:
yoṣitāṃ durvilasitaṃ kaḥ saṃvaritum īśvaraḥ
te dṛṣṭvā cukṣubhur viprā apamārgarate ubhe //
meaning:
योषितां दुर्विलसितं कः संवरितुम् ईश्वरः
ते दृष्ट्वा चुक्षुभुर् विप्रा अपमार्गरते उभे //
text_mt: Who is able to hold back the wicked wantonness of women? / Seeing the two devoted to wrongful ways, the brahmins were agitated:

sanskrit_iast:
apamārgasthite yasmād āpage hi bhaviṣyathaḥ
suparṇā caiva kadrūś ca nadyau te saṃbabhūvatuḥ //
meaning:
अपमार्गस्थिते यस्माद् आपगे हि भविष्यथः
सुपर्णा चैव कद्रूश् च नद्यौ ते संबभूवतुः //
text_mt: “Because you stand on a wrongful path, you will become rivers!” / And so Suparṇā and Kadrū became two rivers.

sanskrit_iast:
sa kadācid gṛhaṃ prāyāt kaśyapo 'tha prajāpatiḥ
ṛṣibhyas tatra vṛttāntaṃ śāpaṃ tābhyāṃ savistaram //
meaning:
स कदाचिद् गृहं प्रायात् कश्यपो ऽथ प्रजापतिः
ऋषिभ्यस् तत्र वृत्तान्तं शापं ताभ्यां सविस्तरम् //
text_mt: Then, at some time, Kaśyapa, the lord of creatures, came home. / Having heard from the sages the full account of the curse upon them,

sanskrit_iast:
śrutvā tu vismayāviṣṭaḥ kiṃ karomīty acintayat
ṛṣibhyaḥ kathayām āsa vālakhilyā iti śrutāḥ //
meaning:
श्रुत्वा तु विस्मयाविष्टः किं करोमीत्य् अचिन्तयत्
ऋषिभ्यः कथयाम् आस वालखिल्या इति श्रुताः //
text_mt: overcome with astonishment, he thought: “What shall I do?” / He spoke to the sages who are known as the Vālakhilyas.

sanskrit_iast:
ta ūcuḥ kaśyapaṃ vipraṃ gatvā gaṅgāṃ tu gautamīm
tatra stuhi maheśānaṃ punar bhārye bhaviṣyataḥ //
meaning:
त ऊचुः कश्यपं विप्रं गत्वा गङ्गां तु गौतमीम्
तत्र स्तुहि महेशानं पुनर् भार्ये भविष्यतः //
text_mt: They said to the brahmin Kaśyapa: “Having gone to the Gautamī Gaṅgā, / praise Maheśāna there; they will become wives again.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmahatyābhayād eva yatra devo maheśvaraḥ
gaṅgāmadhye sadā hy āste madhyameśvarasaṃjñayā //
meaning:
ब्रह्महत्याभयाद् एव यत्र देवो महेश्वरः
गङ्गामध्ये सदा ह्य् आस्ते मध्यमेश्वरसंज्ञया //
text_mt: Where, solely out of fear of killing a brahmin, the god Maheśvara / always resides in the midst of the Gaṅgā under the name Madhyameśvara.”

sanskrit_iast:
tathety uktvā kaśyapo 'pi snātvā gaṅgāṃ jitavrataḥ
tuṣṭāva stavanaiḥ puṇyair devadevaṃ maheśvaram //
meaning:
तथेत्य् उक्त्वा कश्यपो ऽपि स्नात्वा गङ्गां जितव्रतः
तुष्टाव स्तवनैः पुण्यैर् देवदेवं महेश्वरम् //
text_mt: Saying “So be it,” Kaśyapa also bathed in the Gaṅgā, firm in his vow, / and praised the god of gods, Maheśvara, with holy hymns of praise.

sanskrit_iast:
kaśyapa uvāca
lokatrayaikādhipater na yasya
kutrāpi vastuny abhimānaleśaḥ
sa siddhanātho 'khilaviśvakartā
bhartā śivāyā bhavatu prasannaḥ
meaning:
कश्यप उवाच
लोकत्रयैकाधिपतेर् न यस्य
कुत्रापि वस्तुन्य् अभिमानलेशः
स सिद्धनाथो ऽखिलविश्वकर्ता
भर्ता शिवाया भवतु प्रसन्नः
text_mt: Kaśyapa said: / “May the husband of Śivā be gracious—the sole sovereign of the three worlds, / who has not the slightest trace of pride toward any object whatsoever, / the lord of perfected beings, the creator of the entire universe.

sanskrit_iast:
tāpatrayoṣṇadyutitāpitānām
itas tato vai paridhāvatāṃ ca
śarīriṇāṃ sthāvarajaṅgamānāṃ
tvam eva duḥkhavyapanodadakṣaḥ
meaning:
तापत्रयोष्णद्युतितापितानाम्
इतस् ततो वै परिधावतां च
शरीरिणां स्थावरजङ्गमानां
त्वम् एव दुःखव्यपनोददक्षः
text_mt: For embodied beings, both stationary and moving, / who are scorched by the blazing heat of the three afflictions and who run here and there, / you alone are skilled in removing sorrow.

sanskrit_iast:
sattvādiyogas trividho 'pi yasya
śakrādibhir vaktum aśakya eva
vicitravṛttiṃ paricintya somaṃ
sukhī sadā dānaparo vareṇyaḥ
meaning:
सत्त्वादियोगस् त्रिविधो ऽपि यस्य
शक्रादिभिर् वक्तुम् अशक्य एव
विचित्रवृत्तिं परिचिन्त्य सोमं
सुखी सदा दानपरो वरेण्यः
text_mt: Whose threefold connection with sattva and the other gunas / is impossible to describe even by Indra and the gods; / contemplating him who has wondrous activities, who is accompanied by Umā, / one is always happy, devoted to generosity, the most excellent.”

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
ityādistutibhir devaḥ stuto gaurīpatiḥ śivaḥ
prasanno hy adadāc chaṃbhuḥ kaśyapāya varān bahūn //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इत्यादिस्तुतिभिर् देवः स्तुतो गौरीपतिः शिवः
प्रसन्नो ह्य् अददाच् छंभुः कश्यपाय वरान् बहून् //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Having been praised with these and other hymns, the god Śiva, Gaurī’s husband, / Śambhu, pleased, granted many boons to Kaśyapa.

sanskrit_iast:
bhāryārthinaṃ tu taṃ prāha syātāṃ bhārye ubhe tu te
nadīsvarūpe patnyau ye gaṅgāṃ prāpya saridvarām //
meaning:
भार्यार्थिनं तु तं प्राह स्यातां भार्ये उभे तु ते
नदीस्वरूपे पत्न्यौ ये गङ्गां प्राप्य सरिद्वराम् //
text_mt: To him who sought his wives, he said: “Let those two be your wives. / The two wives who have the nature of rivers, upon reaching the Gaṅgā, best of streams,

sanskrit_iast:
tatsaṃgamanamātreṇa tābhyāṃ bhūyāt svakaṃ vapuḥ
te garbhiṇyau punar jāte gaṅgāyāś ca prasādataḥ //
meaning:
तत्संगमनमात्रेण ताभ्यां भूयात् स्वकं वपुः
ते गर्भिण्यौ पुनर् जाते गङ्गायाश् च प्रसादतः //
text_mt: merely by confluence with it, will regain their own forms.” / And by the favor of the Gaṅgā, they became pregnant once again.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ prajāpatiḥ prīto bhārye prāpya mahāmanāḥ
āhvayām āsa tān viprān gautamītīram āśritān //
meaning:
ततः प्रजापतिः प्रीतो भार्ये प्राप्य महामनाः
आह्वयाम् आस तान् विप्रान् गौतमीतीरम् आश्रितान् //
text_mt: Then the lord of creatures, large-minded, pleased at regaining his two wives, / invited the brahmins residing on the bank of the Gautamī.

sanskrit_iast:
sīmantonnayanaṃ cakre tābhyāṃ prītaḥ prajāpatiḥ
brāhmaṇān pūjayām āsa vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā //
meaning:
सीमन्तोन्नयनं चक्रे ताभ्यां प्रीतः प्रजापतिः
ब्राह्मणान् पूजयाम् आस विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा //
text_mt: The lord of creatures, delighted, performed the hair-parting rite for them, / and honored the brahmins with the rites prescribed by rule.

sanskrit_iast:
bhuktavatsv atha vipreṣu kaśyapasyātha mandire
bhartṛsamīpopaviṣṭā kadrūr viprān nirīkṣya ca //
meaning:
भुक्तवत्स्व् अथ विप्रेषु कश्यपस्याथ मन्दिरे
भर्तृसमीपोपविष्टा कद्रूर् विप्रान् निरीक्ष्य च //
text_mt: Then, when the brahmins had eaten in the house of Kaśyapa, / Kadrū, seated beside her husband, looked at the brahmins.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ kadrūr ṛṣīn akṣṇā prāhasat te ca cukṣubhuḥ
yenākṣṇā hasitā pāpe bhajyatāṃ te 'kṣi pāpavat //
meaning:
ततः कद्रूर् ऋषीन् अक्ष्णा प्राहसत् ते च चुक्षुभुः
येनाक्ष्णा हसिता पापे भज्यतां ते ऽक्षि पापवत् //
text_mt: Then Kadrū laughed at the sages with her eye, and they were agitated: / “O sinful woman, the eye with which you laughed shall be destroyed, like a sinful woman!”

sanskrit_iast:
kāṇābhavat tataḥ kadrūḥ sarpamāteti yocyate
tataḥ prasādayām āsa kaśyapo bhagavān ṛṣīn //
meaning:
काणाभवत् ततः कद्रूः सर्पमातेति योच्यते
ततः प्रसादयाम् आस कश्यपो भगवान् ऋषीन् //
text_mt: Then Kadrū, who is called the mother of serpents, became one-eyed. / Then the venerable Kaśyapa propitiated the sages.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ prasannās te procur gautamī saritāṃ varā
aparādhasahasrebhyo rakṣiṣyati ca sevanāt //
meaning:
ततः प्रसन्नास् ते प्रोचुर् गौतमी सरितां वरा
अपराधसहस्रेभ्यो रक्षिष्यति च सेवनात् //
text_mt: Then, pleased, they said: “The Gautamī, the best of rivers, / will protect her from thousands of offenses through attendance upon it.”

sanskrit_iast:
bhāryānvitas tathā cakre kaśyapo munisattamaḥ
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrtham ubhayoḥ saṃgamaṃ viduḥ
sarvapāpapraśamanaṃ sarvakratuphalapradam //
meaning:
भार्यान्वितस् तथा चक्रे कश्यपो मुनिसत्तमः
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थम् उभयोः संगमं विदुः
सर्वपापप्रशमनं सर्वक्रतुफलप्रदम् //
text_mt: Together with his wife, Kaśyapa, best of sages, did so. / From then on, they know that sacred place as the confluence of the two, / which quells all sins and grants the fruit of all sacrifices.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
purūravasam ākhyātaṃ tīrthaṃ vedavido viduḥ
smaraṇād eva pāpānāṃ nāśanaṃ kiṃ tu darśanāt //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
पुरूरवसम् आख्यातं तीर्थं वेदविदो विदुः
स्मरणाद् एव पापानां नाशनं किं तु दर्शनात् //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Those who know the Veda know the sacred place called Purūravas; / it destroys sins merely by remembering it, how much more by beholding it!

sanskrit_iast:
purūravā brahmasadaḥ prāpya tatra sarasvatīm
yadṛcchayā devanadīṃ hasantīṃ brahmaṇo 'ntike
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā rūpasaṃpannām urvaśīṃ prāha bhūpatiḥ //
meaning:
पुरूरवा ब्रह्मसदः प्राप्य तत्र सरस्वतीम्
यदृच्छया देवनदीं हसन्तीं ब्रह्मणो ऽन्तिके
तां दृष्ट्वा रूपसंपन्नाम् उर्वशीं प्राह भूपतिः //
text_mt: Purūravas, having arrived at Brahmā’s assembly, saw there the Sarasvatī, / the river of the gods, who was laughing by chance near Brahmā; / seeing her endowed with beauty, the king said to Urvaśī:

sanskrit_iast:
rājovāca
keyaṃ rūpavatī sādhvī sthiteyaṃ brahmaṇo 'ntike
sarvāsām uttamā yoṣid dīpayantī sabhām imām //
meaning:
राजोवाच
केयं रूपवती साध्वी स्थितेयं ब्रह्मणो ऽन्तिके
सर्वासाम् उत्तमा योषिद् दीपयन्ती सभाम् इमाम् //
text_mt: The king said: / “Who is this beautiful, virtuous woman standing near Brahmā, / the most excellent woman among all, illuminating this assembly?”

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
urvaśī prāha rājānam iyaṃ devanadī śubhā
sarasvatī brahmasutā nityam eti ca yāti ca
tac chrutvā vismito rājā ānayemāṃ mamāntikam //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
उर्वशी प्राह राजानम् इयं देवनदी शुभा
सरस्वती ब्रह्मसुता नित्यम् एति च याति च
तच् छ्रुत्वा विस्मितो राजा आनयेमां ममान्तिकम् //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Urvaśī said to the king: “This is the auspicious celestial river, / the Sarasvatī, Brahmā’s daughter; she comes and goes constantly.” / Hearing that, the astonished king said: “Bring her to me.”

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
urvaśī punar apy āha rājānaṃ bhūridakṣiṇam //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
उर्वशी पुनर् अप्य् आह राजानं भूरिदक्षिणम् //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Urvaśī spoke again to the king of generous sacrificial gifts:

sanskrit_iast:
urvaśy uvāca
ānīyate mahārāja tasyāḥ sarvaṃ nivedya ca //
meaning:
उर्वश्य् उवाच
आनीयते महाराज तस्याः सर्वं निवेद्य च //
text_mt: Urvaśī said: / “She will be brought, great king, after having informed her of everything.”

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
tatas tāṃ prāhiṇot tatra rājā prītyā tadorvaśīm
sā gatvā rājavacanaṃ nyavedayad athorvaśī //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततस् तां प्राहिणोत् तत्र राजा प्रीत्या तदोर्वशीम्
सा गत्वा राजवचनं न्यवेदयद् अथोर्वशी //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Then the king affectionately sent Urvaśī there. / Urvaśī, having gone, conveyed the king’s words.

sanskrit_iast:
sarasvaty api tan mene urvaśyā yan niveditam
sā tatheti pratijñāya prāyād yatra purūravāḥ //
meaning:
सरस्वत्य् अपि तन् मेने उर्वश्या यन् निवेदितम्
सा तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय प्रायाद् यत्र पुरूरवाः //
text_mt: The Sarasvatī agreed to what had been conveyed by Urvaśī. / Promising “So be it,” she went to where Purūravas was.

sanskrit_iast:
sarasvatyās tatas tīre sa reme bahulāḥ samāḥ
sarasvān abhavat putro yasya putro bṛhadrathaḥ //
meaning:
सरस्वत्यास् ततस् तीरे स रेमे बहुलाः समाः
सरस्वान् अभवत् पुत्रो यस्य पुत्रो बृहद्रथः //
text_mt: Then he took his pleasure on the bank of the Sarasvatī for many years. / Sarasvān became his son, whose son was Bṛhadratha.

sanskrit_iast:
tāṃ gacchantīṃ nṛpagṛhaṃ nityam eva sarasvatīm
sarasvantaṃ tato lakṣma jñātvānyeṣu tathā kṛtam //
meaning:
तां गच्छन्तीं नृपगृहं नित्यम् एव सरस्वतीम्
सरस्वन्तं ततो लक्ष्म ज्ञात्वान्येषु तथा कृतम् //
text_mt: To that Sarasvatī who was constantly going to the king's palace, / perceiving the mark of the ocean, it was done likewise to the others.

sanskrit_iast:
tasyai dadāv ahaṃ śāpaṃ bhūyā iti mahānadī
macchāpabhītā vāgīśā prāgād devīṃ ca gautamīm //
meaning:
तस्यै ददाव् अहं शापं भूया इति महानदी
मच्छापभीता वागीशा प्रागाद् देवीं च गौतमीम् //
text_mt: 'May you become a great river!'—I gave her this curse. / Frightened by my curse, the goddess of speech went to the divine Gautamī,

sanskrit_iast:
kamaṇḍalubhavāṃ pūtāṃ mātaraṃ lokapāvanīm
tāpatrayopaśamanīm aihikāmuṣmikapradām //
meaning:
कमण्डलुभवां पूतां मातरं लोकपावनीम्
तापत्रयोपशमनीम् ऐहिकामुष्मिकप्रदाम् //
text_mt: who was born from a water jar, pure, mother and purifier of the world, / pacifier of the threefold suffering, granter of this world and the next.

sanskrit_iast:
sā gatvā gautamīṃ devīṃ prāha macchāpam āditaḥ
gaṅgāpi mām uvācedaṃ viśāpāṃ kartum arhasi //
meaning:
सा गत्वा गौतमीं देवीं प्राह मच्छापम् आदितः
गङ्गापि माम् उवाचेदं विशापां कर्तुम् अर्हसि //
text_mt: She went to the goddess Gautamī and told her of my curse from the beginning. / Gaṅgā too spoke this to me: “You ought to free her from the curse.

sanskrit_iast:
na yuktaṃ yat sarasvatyāḥ śāpaṃ tvaṃ dattavān asi
strīṇām eṣa svabhāvo vai puṃskāmā yoṣito yataḥ //
meaning:
न युक्तं यत् सरस्वत्याः शापं त्वं दत्तवान् असि
स्त्रीणाम् एष स्वभावो वै पुंस्कामा योषितो यतः //
text_mt: It was not right that you cursed Sarasvatī. / Indeed, this is the nature of women, since women desire men.

sanskrit_iast:
svabhāvacapalā brahman yoṣitaḥ sakalā api
tvaṃ kathaṃ tu na jānīṣe jagatsraṣṭāmbujāsana //
meaning:
स्वभावचपला ब्रह्मन् योषितः सकला अपि
त्वं कथं तु न जानीषे जगत्स्रष्टाम्बुजासन //
text_mt: All women, O Brahmā, are fickle by nature. / How is it that you, the lotus-seated creator of the world, do not know this?

sanskrit_iast:
viḍambayati kaṃ vā na kāmo vāpi svabhāvataḥ
tato viśāpam avadaṃ dṛśyāpi syāt sarasvatī //
meaning:
विडम्बयति कं वा न कामो वापि स्वभावतः
ततो विशापम् अवदं दृश्यापि स्यात् सरस्वती //
text_mt: Whom does desire not mock by its very nature?” / Thereupon I spoke the release from the curse: “Sarasvatī shall also become visible.”

sanskrit_iast:
tasmāc chāpān nadī martye dṛśyādṛśyā sarasvatī
yatraiṣā saṃgatā devī gaṅgāyāṃ śāpavihvalā //
meaning:
तस्माच् छापान् नदी मर्त्ये दृश्यादृश्या सरस्वती
यत्रैषा संगता देवी गङ्गायां शापविह्वला //
text_mt: Because of that curse, Sarasvatī is both visible and invisible among mortals as a river. / Where this goddess, distraught by the curse, united with Gaṅgā,

sanskrit_iast:
tatra prāyān nṛpavaro dhārmikaḥ sa purūravāḥ
tapas taptvā samārādhya devaṃ siddheśvaraṃ haram //
meaning:
तत्र प्रायान् नृपवरो धार्मिकः स पुरूरवाः
तपस् तप्त्वा समाराध्य देवं सिद्धेश्वरं हरम् //
text_mt: there went that righteous Purūravas, best of kings. / Having performed austerities and propitiated the god Hara, the Lord of the Siddhas,

sanskrit_iast:
sarvān kāmān athāvāpa gaṅgāyāś ca prasādataḥ
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrthaṃ purūravasam ucyate //
meaning:
सर्वान् कामान् अथावाप गङ्गायाश् च प्रसादतः
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थं पुरूरवसम् उच्यते //
text_mt: he then attained all his desires through the grace of Gaṅgā. / From that time on, that tīrtha is called Paurūravasa.

sanskrit_iast:
sarasvatīsaṃgamaṃ ca brahmatīrthaṃ tad ucyate
siddheśvaro yatra devaḥ sarvakāmapradaṃ tu tat //
meaning:
सरस्वतीसंगमं च ब्रह्मतीर्थं तद् उच्यते
सिद्धेश्वरो यत्र देवः सर्वकामप्रदं तु तत् //
text_mt: It is also called the confluence of Sarasvatī and the tīrtha of Brahmā. / Where the god Siddheśvara resides, that [place] grants every desire.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
sāvitrī caiva gāyatrī śraddhā medhā sarasvatī
etāni pañca tīrthāni puṇyāni munayo viduḥ //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
सावित्री चैव गायत्री श्रद्धा मेधा सरस्वती
एतानि पञ्च तीर्थानि पुण्यानि मुनयो विदुः //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Sāvitrī, Gāyatrī, Śraddhā, Medhā, and Sarasvatī: / the sages know these five sacred tīrthas.

sanskrit_iast:
tatra snātvā tu pītvā tu mucyate sarvakalmaṣāt
sāvitrī caiva gāyatrī śraddhā medhā sarasvatī //
meaning:
तत्र स्नात्वा तु पीत्वा तु मुच्यते सर्वकल्मषात्
सावित्री चैव गायत्री श्रद्धा मेधा सरस्वती //
text_mt: Bathing and drinking there, one is freed from all sin: / Sāvitrī, Gāyatrī, Śraddhā, Medhā, and Sarasvatī.

sanskrit_iast:
etā mama sutā jyeṣṭhā dharmasaṃsthānahetavaḥ
sarvāsām uttamāṃ kāṃcin nirmame lokasundarīm //
meaning:
एता मम सुता ज्येष्ठा धर्मसंस्थानहेतवः
सर्वासाम् उत्तमां कांचिन् निर्ममे लोकसुन्दरीम् //
text_mt: These elder daughters of mine are the causes of the establishment of dharma. / From all of them I created a certain woman of supreme beauty in the world.

sanskrit_iast:
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā vikṛtā buddhir mamāsīn munisattama
gṛhyamāṇā mayā bālā sā māṃ dṛṣṭvā palāyitā //
meaning:
तां दृष्ट्वा विकृता बुद्धिर् ममासीन् मुनिसत्तम
गृह्यमाणा मया बाला सा मां दृष्ट्वा पलायिता //
text_mt: Seeing her, my mind was agitated, O best of sages. / Being seized by me, that maiden saw me and fled.

sanskrit_iast:
mṛgībhūtā tu sā bālā mṛgo 'ham abhavaṃ tadā
mṛgavyādho 'bhavac chaṃbhur dharmasaṃrakṣaṇāya ca //
meaning:
मृगीभूता तु सा बाला मृगो ऽहम् अभवं तदा
मृगव्याधो ऽभवच् छंभुर् धर्मसंरक्षणाय च //
text_mt: The maiden turned into a female deer, and I then became a buck. / Sambhu became a deer-hunter in order to protect dharma.

sanskrit_iast:
tā madbhītāḥ pañca sutā gaṅgām īyur mahānadīm
tato maheśvaraḥ prāyād dharmasaṃrakṣaṇāya saḥ //
meaning:
ता मद्भीताः पञ्च सुता गङ्गाम् ईयुर् महानदीम्
ततो महेश्वरः प्रायाद् धर्मसंरक्षणाय सः //
text_mt: Terrified of me, those five daughters went to the great river Gaṅgā. / Then Maheśvara went forth to protect dharma.

sanskrit_iast:
dhanur gṛhītvā saśaram īśo 'pi mṛgarūpiṇam
mām uvāca vadhiṣye tvāṃ mṛgavyādhas tadā haraḥ //
meaning:
धनुर् गृहीत्वा सशरम् ईशो ऽपि मृगरूपिणम्
माम् उवाच वधिष्ये त्वां मृगव्याधस् तदा हरः //
text_mt: Taking a bow with an arrow, the Lord, Hara, then as a deer-hunter, / said to me who had assumed the form of a deer: “I will kill you!”

sanskrit_iast:
tatkarmaṇo nivṛtto 'haṃ prādāṃ kanyāṃ vivasvate
sāvitryādyāḥ pañca sutā nadīrūpeṇa saṃgatāḥ //
meaning:
तत्कर्मणो निवृत्तो ऽहं प्रादां कन्यां विवस्वते
सावित्र्याद्याः पञ्च सुता नदीरूपेण संगताः //
text_mt: Desisting from that act, I gave the maiden to Vivasvat. / The five daughters, Sāvitrī and the others, united in the form of rivers.

sanskrit_iast:
tā āgatāḥ punaś cāpi svargaṃ lokaṃ mamāntikam
yatra tāḥ saṃgatā devyā pañca tīrthāni nārada //
meaning:
ता आगताः पुनश् चापि स्वर्गं लोकं ममान्तिकम्
यत्र ताः संगता देव्या पञ्च तीर्थानि नारद //
text_mt: They also returned to heaven, to my presence. / Where they united with the goddess, O Nārada, are the five tīrthas,

sanskrit_iast:
saṃgatāni ca puṇyāni pañca nadyaḥ sarasvatī
teṣu snānaṃ tathā dānaṃ yat kiṃcit kurute naraḥ //
meaning:
संगतानि च पुण्यानि पञ्च नद्यः सरस्वती
तेषु स्नानं तथा दानं यत् किंचित् कुरुते नरः //
text_mt: sacred and conjoined—the five rivers and Sarasvatī. / Whatever bathing and donation a person performs in them

sanskrit_iast:
sarvakāmapradaṃ tat syān naiṣkarmyān muktidaṃ smṛtam
tatrābhavan mṛgavyādhaṃ tīrthaṃ sarvārthadaṃ nṛṇām
svargamokṣaphalaṃ cānyad brahmatīrthaphalaṃ smṛtam //
meaning:
सर्वकामप्रदं तत् स्यान् नैष्कर्म्यान् मुक्तिदं स्मृतम्
तत्राभवन् मृगव्याधं तीर्थं सर्वार्थदं नृणाम्
स्वर्गमोक्षफलं चान्यद् ब्रह्मतीर्थफलं स्मृतम् //
text_mt: grants all desires; it is remembered as bestowing liberation through actionlessness. / There the tīrtha Mṛgavyādha arose, granting all goals to humans; / and the fruit of the tīrtha of Brahmā is remembered as yielding heaven and liberation.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
śamītīrtham iti khyātaṃ sarvapāpopaśāntidam
tasyākhyānaṃ pravakṣyāmi śṛṇu yatnena nārada //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
शमीतीर्थम् इति ख्यातं सर्वपापोपशान्तिदम्
तस्याख्यानं प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणु यत्नेन नारद //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / There is the well-known Śamītīrtha, which brings peace from all sins. / I will narrate its story; listen attentively, O Nārada.

sanskrit_iast:
āsīt priyavrato nāma kṣatriyo jayatāṃ varaḥ
gautamyā dakṣiṇe tīre dīkṣāṃ cakre purodhasā //
meaning:
आसीत् प्रियव्रतो नाम क्षत्रियो जयतां वरः
गौतम्या दक्षिणे तीरे दीक्षां चक्रे पुरोधसा //
text_mt: There was a kṣatriya named Priyavrata, the foremost of conquerors. / On the southern bank of the Gautamī, he undertook initiation with his family priest.

sanskrit_iast:
hayamedha upakrānte ṛtvigbhir ṛṣibhir vṛte
tasya rājño mahābāhor vasiṣṭhas tu purohitaḥ //
meaning:
हयमेध उपक्रान्ते ऋत्विग्भिर् ऋषिभिर् वृते
तस्य राज्ञो महाबाहोर् वसिष्ठस् तु पुरोहितः //
text_mt: When the horse sacrifice was begun, attended by sacrificial priests and sages, / Vasiṣṭha was the domestic priest of that long-armed king.

sanskrit_iast:
tadyajñavāṭam agamad dānavo 'tha hiraṇyakaḥ
taṃ dānavam abhiprekṣya devās tv indrapurogamāḥ //
meaning:
तद्यज्ञवाटम् अगमद् दानवो ऽथ हिरण्यकः
तं दानवम् अभिप्रेक्ष्य देवास् त्व् इन्द्रपुरोगमाः //
text_mt: Then the Dānava Hiraṇyaka came to that sacrificial enclosure. / Beholding that Dānava, the gods, led by Indra,

sanskrit_iast:
bhītāḥ kecid divaṃ jagmur havyavāṭ śamim āviśat
aśvatthaṃ viṣṇur agamad bhānur arkaṃ vaṭaṃ śivaḥ //
meaning:
भीताः केचिद् दिवं जग्मुर् हव्यवाट् शमिम् आविशत्
अश्वत्थं विष्णुर् अगमद् भानुर् अर्कं वटं शिवः //
text_mt: fled in fear, some going to heaven. The sacrificial fire entered a śamī tree; / Viṣṇu went to an aśvattha tree; the Sun to an arka tree; Śiva to a banyan tree;

sanskrit_iast:
somaḥ palāśam agamad gaṅgāmbho havyavāhanaḥ
aśvinau tu hayaṃ gṛhya vāyaso 'bhūd yamaḥ svayam //
meaning:
सोमः पलाशम् अगमद् गङ्गाम्भो हव्यवाहनः
अश्विनौ तु हयं गृह्य वायसो ऽभूद् यमः स्वयम् //
text_mt: Soma went to a palāśa tree; the fire bearer [Agni] to the water of the Gaṅgā; / the two Aśvins, taking the horse, [went away]; and Yama himself became a crow.

sanskrit_iast:
etasminn antare tatra vasiṣṭho bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
yaṣṭim ādāya daiteyān nyavārayad athājñayā //
meaning:
एतस्मिन्न् अन्तरे तत्र वसिष्ठो भगवान् ऋषिः
यष्टिम् आदाय दैतेयान् न्यवारयद् अथाज्ञया //
text_mt: Meanwhile, the venerable sage Vasiṣṭha / took up a staff and by his command warded off the Daiteyas.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ pravṛttaḥ punar eva yajño
daityo gataḥ svena balena yuktaḥ
imāni tīrthāni tataḥ śubhāni
daśāśvamedhasya phalāni dadyuḥ
meaning:
ततः प्रवृत्तः पुनर् एव यज्ञो
दैत्यो गतः स्वेन बलेन युक्तः
इमानि तीर्थानि ततः शुभानि
दशाश्वमेधस्य फलानि दद्युः
text_mt: Then the sacrifice proceeded once more; / the Daitya departed accompanied by his own army. / These auspicious tīrthas, arising from that, / bestow the fruits of ten horse sacrifices:

sanskrit_iast:
prathamaṃ tu śamītīrthaṃ dvitīyaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ viduḥ
ārkaṃ śaivaṃ ca saumyaṃ ca vāsiṣṭhaṃ sarvakāmadam //
meaning:
प्रथमं तु शमीतीर्थं द्वितीयं वैष्णवं विदुः
आर्कं शैवं च सौम्यं च वासिष्ठं सर्वकामदम् //
text_mt: The first they know as Śamītīrtha; the second is Vaiṣṇava; / Ārka, Śaiva, Saumya, and Vāsiṣṭha, granting all desires.

sanskrit_iast:
devāś ca ṛṣayaḥ sarve nivṛtte makhavistare
tuṣṭāḥ procur vasiṣṭhaṃ taṃ yajamānaṃ priyavratam //
meaning:
देवाश् च ऋषयः सर्वे निवृत्ते मखविस्तरे
तुष्टाः प्रोचुर् वसिष्ठं तं यजमानं प्रियव्रतम् //
text_mt: When the extensive sacrifice was concluded, all the gods and sages, / pleased, spoke to Vasiṣṭha and to the sacrificer Priyavrata,

sanskrit_iast:
tāṃś ca vṛkṣāṃs tāṃ ca gaṅgāṃ mudā yuktāḥ punaḥ punaḥ
hayamedhasya niṣpattyai ete yātā itas tataḥ //
meaning:
तांश् च वृक्षांस् तां च गङ्गां मुदा युक्ताः पुनः पुनः
हयमेधस्य निष्पत्त्यै एते याता इतस् ततः //
text_mt: and repeatedly with joy to those trees and that Gaṅgā: / “For the accomplishment of the horse sacrifice, these have fled here and there;

sanskrit_iast:
hayamedhaphalaṃ dadyus tīrthānīty avadan surāḥ
tasmāt snānena dānena teṣu tīrtheṣu nārada
hayamedhaphalaṃ puṇyaṃ prāpnoti na mṛṣā vacaḥ //
meaning:
हयमेधफलं दद्युस् तीर्थानीत्य् अवदन् सुराः
तस्मात् स्नानेन दानेन तेषु तीर्थेषु नारद
हयमेधफलं पुण्यं प्राप्नोति न मृषा वचः //
text_mt: the tīrthas shall give the fruit of a horse sacrifice!”—so said the gods. / Therefore, through bathing and gifting at those tīrthas, O Nārada, / one attains the merit of a horse sacrifice; this word is not false.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
viśvāmitraṃ hariścandraṃ śunaḥśepaṃ ca rohitam
vāruṇaṃ brāhmam āgneyam aindram aindavam aiśvaram //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
विश्वामित्रं हरिश्चन्द्रं शुनःशेपं च रोहितम्
वारुणं ब्राह्मम् आग्नेयम् ऐन्द्रम् ऐन्दवम् ऐश्वरम् //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Viśvāmitra, Hariścandra, Śunaḥśepa, Rohita, / Vāruṇa, Brāhma, Āgneya, Aindra, Aindava, Aiśvara,

sanskrit_iast:
maitraṃ ca vaiṣṇavaṃ caiva yāmyam āśvinam auśanam
eteṣāṃ puṇyatīrthānāṃ nāmadheyaṃ śṛṇuṣva me //
meaning:
मैत्रं च वैष्णवं चैव याम्यम् आश्विनम् औशनम्
एतेषां पुण्यतीर्थानां नामधेयं शृणुष्व मे //
text_mt: Maitra, Vaiṣṇava, Yāmya, Āśvina, and Auśana: / hear from me the names of these sacred tīrthas.

sanskrit_iast:
hariścandra iti tv āsīd ikṣvākuprabhavo nṛpaḥ
tasya gṛhe munī prāptau nāradaḥ parvatas tathā
kṛtvātithyaṃ tayoḥ samyag ghariścandro 'bravīd ṛṣī //
meaning:
हरिश्चन्द्र इति त्व् आसीद् इक्ष्वाकुप्रभवो नृपः
तस्य गृहे मुनी प्राप्तौ नारदः पर्वतस् तथा
कृत्वातिथ्यं तयोः सम्यग् घरिश्चन्द्रो ऽब्रवीद् ऋषी //
text_mt: There was a king named Hariścandra, born in the lineage of Ikṣvāku. / The two sages Nārada and Parvata arrived at his house. / Having shown them hospitality properly, Hariścandra said to the two sages:

sanskrit_iast:
hariścandra uvāca
putrārthaṃ kliśyate lokaḥ kiṃ putreṇa bhaviṣyati
jñānī vāpy athavājñānī uttamo madhyamo 'thavā
etaṃ me saṃśayaṃ nityaṃ brūtām ṛṣivarāv ubhau //
meaning:
हरिश्चन्द्र उवाच
पुत्रार्थं क्लिश्यते लोकः किं पुत्रेण भविष्यति
ज्ञानी वाप्य् अथवाज्ञानी उत्तमो मध्यमो ऽथवा
एतं मे संशयं नित्यं ब्रूताम् ऋषिवराव् उभौ //
text_mt: Hariścandra said: / “The world toils for the sake of a son; what comes of having a son? / Whether wise or ignorant, superior or mediocre— / do both of you, best of sages, resolve this constant doubt of mine.”

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
tāv ūcatur hariścandraṃ parvato nāradas tathā //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ताव् ऊचतुर् हरिश्चन्द्रं पर्वतो नारदस् तथा //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Parvata and Nārada both spoke to Hariścandra:

sanskrit_iast:
nāradaparvatāv ūcatuḥ
ekadhā daśadhā rājañ śatadhā ca sahasradhā
uttaraṃ vidyate samyak tathāpy etad udīryate //
meaning:
नारदपर्वताव् ऊचतुः
एकधा दशधा राजञ् शतधा च सहस्रधा
उत्तरं विद्यते सम्यक् तथाप्य् एतद् उदीर्यते //
text_mt: Nārada and Parvata said: / “O King, an answer exists singly, tenfold, / a hundredfold, and a thousandfold; nevertheless, this is declared:

sanskrit_iast:
nāputrasya paro loko vidyate nṛpasattama
jāte putre pitā snānaṃ yaḥ karoti janādhipa //
meaning:
नापुत्रस्य परो लोको विद्यते नृपसत्तम
जाते पुत्रे पिता स्नानं यः करोति जनाधिप //
text_mt: There is no other world for a sonless man, O best of kings. / A father who bathes when a son is born, O ruler of people,

sanskrit_iast:
daśānām aśvamedhānām abhiṣekaphalaṃ labhet
ātmapratiṣṭhā putrāt syāj jāyate cāmarottamaḥ //
meaning:
दशानाम् अश्वमेधानाम् अभिषेकफलं लभेत्
आत्मप्रतिष्ठा पुत्रात् स्याज् जायते चामरोत्तमः //
text_mt: attains the fruit of the consecration of ten horse sacrifices. / The establishment of the self comes from a son, and he becomes the best of immortals.

sanskrit_iast:
amṛtenāmarā devāḥ putreṇa brāhmaṇādayaḥ
triṛṇān mocayet putraḥ pitaraṃ ca pitāmahān //
meaning:
अमृतेनामरा देवाः पुत्रेण ब्राह्मणादयः
त्रिऋणान् मोचयेत् पुत्रः पितरं च पितामहान् //
text_mt: The gods are immortal through nectar; brahmins and others, through a son. / A son frees his father and grandfathers from the three debts.

sanskrit_iast:
kiṃ tu mūlaṃ kim u jalaṃ kiṃ tu śmaśrūṇi kiṃ tapaḥ
vinā putreṇa rājendra svargo muktiḥ sutāt smṛtāḥ //
meaning:
किं तु मूलं किम् उ जलं किं तु श्मश्रूणि किं तपः
विना पुत्रेण राजेन्द्र स्वर्गो मुक्तिः सुतात् स्मृताः //
text_mt: What use are roots, what use is water, what use are beards, what use is asceticism / without a son, O king of kings? Heaven and liberation are traditionally said to come from a son.

sanskrit_iast:
putra eva paro loko dharmaḥ kāmo 'rtha eva ca
putro muktiḥ paraṃ jyotis tārakaḥ sarvadehinām //
meaning:
पुत्र एव परो लोको धर्मः कामो ऽर्थ एव च
पुत्रो मुक्तिः परं ज्योतिस् तारकः सर्वदेहिनाम् //
text_mt: A son alone is the higher world, dharma, desire, and wealth. / A son is liberation, the supreme light, the savior of all embodied beings.”

sanskrit_iast:
vinā putreṇa rājendra svargamokṣau sudurlabhau
putra eva paro loke dharmakāmārthasiddhaye //
meaning:
विना पुत्रेण राजेन्द्र स्वर्गमोक्षौ सुदुर्लभौ
पुत्र एव परो लोके धर्मकामार्थसिद्धये //
text_mt:
“Without a son, O best of kings, heaven and liberation are very hard to attain.
Only a son in this world brings about the attainment of dharma, desire, and wealth.

sanskrit_iast:
vinā putreṇa yad dattaṃ vinā putreṇa yad dhutam
vinā putreṇa yaj janma vyarthaṃ tad avabhāti me //
meaning:
विना पुत्रेण यद् दत्तं विना पुत्रेण यद् धुतम्
विना पुत्रेण यज् जन्म व्यर्थं तद् अवभाति मे //
text_mt:
Whatever is given without a son, whatever is offered in sacrifice without a son,
whatever birth is had without a son—all that seems useless to me.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmāt putrasamaṃ kiṃcit kāmyaṃ nāsti jagattraye
tac chrutvā vismayavāṃs tāv uvāca nṛpaḥ punaḥ //
meaning:
तस्मात् पुत्रसमं किंचित् काम्यं नास्ति जगत्त्रये
तच् छ्रुत्वा विस्मयवांस् ताव् उवाच नृपः पुनः //
text_mt:
Therefore, there is nothing in the three worlds desirable like a son.”
Having heard that, amazed, the king spoke again to the two of them:

sanskrit_iast:
hariścandra uvāca
kathaṃ me syāt suto brūtāṃ yatra kvāpi yathātatham
yena kenāpy upāyena kṛtvā kiṃcit tu pauruṣam
mantreṇa yāgadānābhyām utpādyo 'sau suto mayā //
meaning:
हरिश्चन्द्र उवाच
कथं मे स्यात् सुतो ब्रूतां यत्र क्वापि यथातथम्
येन केनाप्य् उपायेन कृत्वा किंचित् तु पौरुषम्
मन्त्रेण यागदानाभ्याम् उत्पाद्यो ऽसौ सुतो मया //
text_mt:
Hariścandra said:
“Tell me truly how I may have a son, anywhere [or by any means] whatsoever.
By performing some manly effort through any means at all,
through mantra, sacrifice, or gifts, that son must be engendered by me.”

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
tāv ūcatur nṛpaśreṣṭhaṃ hariścandraṃ sutārthinam
dhyātvā kṣaṇaṃ tathā samyag gautamīṃ yāhi mānada //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ताव् ऊचतुर् नृपश्रेष्ठं हरिश्चन्द्रं सुतार्थिनम्
ध्यात्वा क्षणं तथा सम्यग् गौतमीं याहि मानद //
text_mt:
Brahmā said:
Having meditated for a moment properly, the two said to the best of kings,
to Hariścandra, who was longing for a son: “Go to the Gautamī, O bestower of honor.

sanskrit_iast:
tatrāpāṃpatir utkṛṣṭaṃ dadāti manasīpsitam
varuṇaḥ sarvadātā vai munibhiḥ parikīrtitaḥ //
meaning:
तत्रापांपतिर् उत्कृष्टं ददाति मनसीप्सितम्
वरुणः सर्वदाता वै मुनिभिः परिकीर्तितः //
text_mt:
There the lord of waters grants the supreme wish of the heart.
Varuṇa, the giver of everything, has indeed been celebrated by the sages.

sanskrit_iast:
sa tu prītaḥ śanaiḥ kāle tava putraṃ pradāsyati
etac chrutvā nṛpaśreṣṭho munivākyaṃ tathākarot //
meaning:
स तु प्रीतः शनैः काले तव पुत्रं प्रदास्यति
एतच् छ्रुत्वा नृपश्रेष्ठो मुनिवाक्यं तथाकरोत् //
text_mt:
He, being pleased, will give you a son in due course of time.”
Having heard this, the best of kings carried out the sages’ word.

sanskrit_iast:
toṣayām āsa varuṇaṃ gautamītīram āśritaḥ
tataś ca tuṣṭo varuṇo hariścandram uvāca ha //
meaning:
तोषयाम् आस वरुणं गौतमीतीरम् आश्रितः
ततश् च तुष्टो वरुणो हरिश्चन्द्रम् उवाच ह //
text_mt:
Taking refuge on the bank of the Gautamī, he gratified Varuṇa.
And then Varuṇa, being pleased, spoke to Hariścandra:

sanskrit_iast:
varuṇa uvāca
putraṃ dāsyāmi te rājaṃl lokatrayavibhūṣaṇam
yadi yakṣyasi tenaiva tava putro bhaved dhruvam //
meaning:
वरुण उवाच
पुत्रं दास्यामि ते राजंल् लोकत्रयविभूषणम्
यदि यक्ष्यसि तेनैव तव पुत्रो भवेद् ध्रुवम् //
text_mt:
Varuṇa said:
“I will give you a son, O king, an ornament to the three worlds,
if you will sacrifice to me with him alone; then your son shall surely come to be.”

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
hariścandro 'pi varuṇaṃ yakṣye tenety avocata
tato gatvā hariścandraś caruṃ kṛtvā tu vāruṇam //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
हरिश्चन्द्रो ऽपि वरुणं यक्ष्ये तेनेत्य् अवोचत
ततो गत्वा हरिश्चन्द्रश् चरुं कृत्वा तु वारुणम् //
text_mt:
Brahmā said:
Hariścandra also said to Varuṇa: “I shall sacrifice with him.”
Then, having gone, Hariścandra prepared a sacrificial rice-offering sacred to Varuṇa,

sanskrit_iast:
bhāryāyai nṛpatiḥ prādāt tato jātaḥ suto nṛpāt
jāte putre apām īśaḥ provāca vadatāṃ varaḥ //
meaning:
भार्यायै नृपतिः प्रादात् ततो जातः सुतो नृपात्
जाते पुत्रे अपाम् ईशः प्रोवाच वदतां वरः //
text_mt:
and the king gave it to his wife; then a son was born from the king.
When the son was born, the lord of waters, the best of speakers, said:

sanskrit_iast:
varuṇa uvāca
adyaiva putro yaṣṭavyaḥ smarase vacanaṃ purā //
meaning:
वरुण उवाच
अद्यैव पुत्रो यष्टव्यः स्मरसे वचनं पुरा //
text_mt:
Varuṇa said:
“The son must be sacrificed this very day. Do you remember the word [given] previously?”

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
hariścandro 'pi varuṇaṃ provācedaṃ kramāgatam //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
हरिश्चन्द्रो ऽपि वरुणं प्रोवाचेदं क्रमागतम् //
text_mt:
Brahmā said:
Hariścandra also spoke this to Varuṇa, which followed in order:

sanskrit_iast:
hariścandra uvāca
nirdaśo medhyatāṃ yāti paśur yakṣye tato hy aham //
meaning:
हरिश्चन्द्र उवाच
निर्दशो मेध्यतां याति पशुर् यक्ष्ये ततो ह्य् अहम् //
text_mt:
Hariścandra said:
“Only when past ten days of age does an animal become fit for sacrifice; then indeed I shall sacrifice.”

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
tac chrutvā vacanaṃ rājño varuṇo 'gāt svam ālayam
nirdaśe punar abhyetya yajasvety āha taṃ nṛpam //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तच् छ्रुत्वा वचनं राज्ञो वरुणो ऽगात् स्वम् आलयम्
निर्दशे पुनर् अभ्येत्य यजस्वेत्य् आह तं नृपम् //
text_mt:
Brahmā said:
Having heard those words of the king, Varuṇa went to his own abode.
When the ten days had passed, he approached again and said to the king: “Sacrifice!”

sanskrit_iast:
rājāpi varuṇaṃ prāha nirdanto niṣphalaḥ paśuḥ
paśor danteṣu jāteṣu ehi gacchādhunāppate //
meaning:
राजापि वरुणं प्राह निर्दन्तो निष्फलः पशुः
पशोर् दन्तेषु जातेषु एहि गच्छाधुनाप्पते //
text_mt:
The king also said to Varuṇa: “A toothless sacrificial animal is useless.
When teeth have grown in the animal, come [back]; go now, O lord of waters!”

sanskrit_iast:
tac chrutvā rājavacanaṃ punaḥ prāyād apāṃpatiḥ
jāteṣu caiva danteṣu saptavarṣeṣu nārada //
meaning:
तच् छ्रुत्वा राजवचनं पुनः प्रायाद् अपांपतिः
जातेषु चैव दन्तेषु सप्तवर्षेषु नारद //
text_mt:
Having heard those words of the king, the lord of waters went away again.
And when the teeth had grown in seven years, O Nārada,

sanskrit_iast:
punar apy āha rājānaṃ yajasveti tato 'bravīt
rājāpi varuṇaṃ prāha patsyantīme apāṃpate //
meaning:
पुनर् अप्य् आह राजानं यजस्वेति ततो ऽब्रवीत्
राजापि वरुणं प्राह पत्स्यन्तीमे अपांपते //
text_mt:
he spoke again to the king: “Sacrifice!” Then he said.
The king also said to Varuṇa: “These teeth will fall out, O lord of waters,
