text_mt: Glorious Pṛthu became king, endowed with brahmanical power. / All the gods, having approached him and greeted him with auspicious boons,

sanskrit_iast:
tasmai dadus tathāstrāṇi mantrāṇi guṇavanti ca
tato 'bruvan munigaṇās taṃ pṛthuṃ kapilena ca //
meaning:
तस्मै ददुस् तथास्त्राणि मन्त्राणि गुणवन्ति च
ततो ऽब्रुवन् मुनिगणास् तं पृथुं कपिलेन च //
text_mt: gave him divine weapons and efficacious mantras. / Then the hosts of sages, together with Kapila, said to that Pṛthu:

sanskrit_iast:
munaya ūcuḥ
āhāraṃ dehi jīvebhyo bhuvā grastauṣadhīr api //
meaning:
मुनय ऊचुः
आहारं देहि जीवेभ्यो भुवा ग्रस्तौषधीर् अपि //
text_mt: The sages said: / 'Provide food for living beings, along with the plants that have been swallowed by the earth!'

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
tataḥ sa dhanur ādāya bhuvam āha nṛpottamaḥ //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततः स धनुर् आदाय भुवम् आह नृपोत्तमः //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Then that best of kings, taking up his bow, addressed the earth:

sanskrit_iast:
pṛthur uvāca
oṣadhīr dehi yā grastāḥ prajānāṃ hitakāmyayā //
meaning:
पृथुर् उवाच
ओषधीर् देहि या ग्रस्ताः प्रजानां हितकाम्यया //
text_mt: Pṛthu said: / 'Give up the plants that have been swallowed, desiring the welfare of your creatures!'

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
tam uvāca mahī bhītā pṛthuṃ taṃ pṛthulocanam //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तम् उवाच मही भीता पृथुं तं पृथुलोचनम् //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / The earth, terrified, spoke to that large-eyed Pṛthu:

sanskrit_iast:
mahy uvāca
mayi jīrṇā mahauṣadhyaḥ kathaṃ dātum ahaṃ kṣamā //
meaning:
मह्य् उवाच
मयि जीर्णा महौषध्यः कथं दातुम् अहं क्षमा //
text_mt: The earth said: / 'The great plants have been digested within me. How am I able to give them?'

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
tataḥ sakopo nṛpatis tām āha pṛthivīṃ punaḥ //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततः सकोपो नृपतिस् ताम् आह पृथिवीं पुनः //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Then the king, enraged, spoke again to the earth:

sanskrit_iast:
pṛthur uvāca
no ced dadāsy adya tvāṃ vai hatvā dāsye mahauṣadhīḥ //
meaning:
पृथुर् उवाच
नो चेद् ददास्य् अद्य त्वां वै हत्वा दास्ये महौषधीः //
text_mt: Pṛthu said: / 'If you do not give them today, I shall kill you and provide the great plants!'

sanskrit_iast:
bhūmir uvāca
kathaṃ haṃsi striyaṃ rājañ jñānī bhūtvā nṛpottama
vinā mayā kathaṃ cemāḥ prajāḥ saṃdhārayiṣyasi //
meaning:
भूमिर् उवाच
कथं हंसि स्त्रियं राजञ् ज्ञानी भूत्वा नृपोत्तम
विना मया कथं चेमाः प्रजाः संधारयिष्यसि //
text_mt: The earth said: / 'How will you kill a woman, O king, having become wise, O best of kings? / And how, without me, will you sustain these creatures?'

sanskrit_iast:
pṛthur uvāca
yatropakāro 'nekānām ekanāśe bhaviṣyati
na doṣas tatra pṛthivi tapasā dhāraye prajāḥ //
meaning:
पृथुर् उवाच
यत्रोपकारो ऽनेकानाम् एकनाशे भविष्यति
न दोषस् तत्र पृथिवि तपसा धारये प्रजाः //
text_mt: Pṛthu said: / 'Where benefit for many will come to be by the destruction of one, / there is no fault in that, O earth; I shall sustain the creatures by asceticism.

sanskrit_iast:
na doṣam atra paśyāmi nācakṣe 'narthakaṃ vacaḥ
yasmin nipātite saukhyaṃ bahūnām upajāyate
munayas tadvadhaṃ prāhur aśvamedhaśatādhikam //
meaning:
न दोषम् अत्र पश्यामि नाचक्षे ऽनर्थकं वचः
यस्मिन् निपातिते सौख्यं बहूनाम् उपजायते
मुनयस् तद्वधं प्राहुर् अश्वमेधशताधिकम् //
text_mt: I see no fault in this, nor do I speak a meaningless word. / The sage says that the killing of one whose downfall brings happiness to many / is greater than a hundred horse-sacrifices.'

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
tato devāś ca ṛṣayaḥ sāntvayitvā nṛpottamam
mahīṃ ca mātaraṃ devīm ūcuḥ suragaṇās tadā //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततो देवाश् च ऋषयः सान्त्वयित्वा नृपोत्तमम्
महीं च मातरं देवीम् ऊचुः सुरगणास् तदा //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Then the gods and the ṛṣis, having consoled that best of kings, / and the hosts of gods then spoke to the goddess Earth, the mother:

sanskrit_iast:
devā ūcuḥ
bhūme gorūpiṇī bhūtvā payorūpā mahauṣadhīḥ
dehi tvaṃ pṛthave rājñe tataḥ prīto bhaven nṛpaḥ
prajāsaṃrakṣaṇaṃ ca syāt tataḥ kṣemaṃ bhaviṣyati //
meaning:
देवा ऊचुः
भूमे गोरूपिणी भूत्वा पयोरूपा महौषधीः
देहि त्वं पृथवे राज्ञे ततः प्रीतो भवेन् नृपः
प्रजासंरक्षणं च स्यात् ततः क्षेमं भविष्यति //
text_mt: The gods said: / 'O Earth, having assumed the form of a cow, give the great plants / in the form of milk to King Pṛthu; then the king will be pleased, / and there will be protection of the subjects; from that, well-being will ensue.'

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
tato gorūpam āsthāya bhūmy āsīt kapilāntike
dudoha ca mahauṣadhyo rājā venakarodbhavaḥ //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततो गोरूपम् आस्थाय भूम्य् आसीत् कपिलान्तिके
दुदोह च महौषध्यो राजा वेनकरोद्भवः //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Then, having assumed the form of a cow, the earth stood in the presence of Kapila, / and the king born from the hand of Vena milked the great plants.

sanskrit_iast:
yatra devāḥ sagandharvā ṛṣayaḥ kapilo muniḥ
mahīṃ gorūpam āpannāṃ narmadāyāṃ mahāmune //
meaning:
यत्र देवाः सगन्धर्वा ऋषयः कपिलो मुनिः
महीं गोरूपम् आपन्नां नर्मदायां महामुने //
text_mt: Where the gods, along with the Gandharvas, the ṛṣis, and the sage Kapila [were present], / O great sage, the earth having assumed the form of a cow at the Narmadā,

sanskrit_iast:
sarasvatyāṃ bhāgīrathyāṃ godāvaryāṃ viśeṣataḥ
mahānadīṣu sarvāsu duduhe 'sau payo mahat //
meaning:
सरस्वत्यां भागीरथ्यां गोदावर्यां विशेषतः
महानदीषु सर्वासु दुदुहे ऽसौ पयो महत् //
text_mt: at the Sarasvatī, at the Bhāgīrathī, and especially at the Godāvarī, / at all the great rivers, he milked that great milk.

sanskrit_iast:
sā duhyamānā pṛthunā puṇyatoyābhavan nadī
gautamyā saṃgatā cābhūt tad adbhutam ivābhavat //
meaning:
सा दुह्यमाना पृथुना पुण्यतोयाभवन् नदी
गौतम्या संगता चाभूत् तद् अद्भुतम् इवाभवत् //
text_mt: Being milked by Pṛthu, she became a river of sacred waters / and joined with the Gautamī; that was like a wonder.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrthaṃ kapilāsaṃgamaṃ viduḥ
tatrāṣṭāśītiḥ pūjyāni sahasrāṇi mahāmate //
meaning:
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थं कपिलासंगमं विदुः
तत्राष्टाशीतिः पूज्यानि सहस्राणि महामते //
text_mt: From that time on, they know that tīrtha as Kapilāsaṅgama. / There, O wise one, eighty-eight thousand sacred tīrthas

sanskrit_iast:
tīrthāny āhur munigaṇāḥ smaraṇād api nārada
pāvanāni jagaty asmiṃs tāni sarvāṇy anukramāt //
meaning:
तीर्थान्य् आहुर् मुनिगणाः स्मरणाद् अपि नारद
पावनानि जगत्य् अस्मिंस् तानि सर्वाण्य् अनुक्रमात् //
text_mt: the hosts of sages declare, O Nārada, all of which in succession / purify in this world merely by remembrance.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
devasthānam iti khyātaṃ tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam
tasya prabhāvaṃ vakṣyāmi śṛṇu yatnena nārada //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
देवस्थानम् इति ख्यातं तीर्थं त्रैलोक्यविश्रुतम्
तस्य प्रभावं वक्ष्यामि शृणु यत्नेन नारद //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / There is a tīrtha celebrated in the three worlds known as Devasthāna. / I shall tell its power; listen attentively, O Nārada.

sanskrit_iast:
purā kṛtayugasyādau devadānavasaṃgare
pravṛtte vā siṃhiketi vikhyātā daityasundarī //
meaning:
पुरा कृतयुगस्यादौ देवदानवसंगरे
प्रवृत्ते वा सिंहिकेति विख्याता दैत्यसुन्दरी //
text_mt: Long ago, at the beginning of the Kṛta age, when the battle between gods and Dānavas had begun, / there was a lovely Daitya woman renowned as Siṃhikā.

sanskrit_iast:
tasyāḥ putro mahādaityo rāhur nāma mahābalaḥ
amṛte tu samutpanne saiṃhikeye ca bhedite //
meaning:
तस्याः पुत्रो महादैत्यो राहुर् नाम महाबलः
अमृते तु समुत्पन्ने सैंहिकेये च भेदिते //
text_mt: Her son was a great Daitya named Rāhu of immense strength. / But when the nectar was produced and that son of Siṃhikā was severed,

sanskrit_iast:
tasya putro mahādaityo meghahāsa iti śrutaḥ
pitaraṃ ghātitaṃ śrutvā tapas tepe 'tiduḥkhitaḥ //
meaning:
तस्य पुत्रो महादैत्यो मेघहास इति श्रुतः
पितरं घातितं श्रुत्वा तपस् तेपे ऽतिदुःखितः //
text_mt: his son, a great Daitya renowned as Meghahāsa, / hearing that his father had been killed, performed asceticism, deeply sorrowful.

sanskrit_iast:
tapasyantaṃ rāhusutaṃ gautamītīram āśritam
devāś ca ṛṣayaḥ sarve tam ūcur atibhītavat //
meaning:
तपस्यन्तं राहुसुतं गौतमीतीरम् आश्रितम्
देवाश् च ऋषयः सर्वे तम् ऊचुर् अतिभीतवत् //
text_mt: To the son of Rāhu, who was performing austerities having resorted to the bank of the Gautamī, / the gods and all the sages spoke, as if terrified:

sanskrit_iast:
devarṣaya ūcuḥ
tapo jahi mahābāho yat te manasi saṃsthitam
sarvaṃ bhavatu nāmedaṃ śivagaṅgāprasādataḥ
śivagaṅgāprasādena kiṃ nāmāsty atra durlabham //
meaning:
देवर्षय ऊचुः
तपो जहि महाबाहो यत् ते मनसि संस्थितम्
सर्वं भवतु नामेदं शिवगङ्गाप्रसादतः
शिवगङ्गाप्रसादेन किं नामास्त्य् अत्र दुर्लभम् //
text_mt: The divine sages said: / "Abandon your austerity, O mighty-armed one! Whatever is settled in your mind, / may all that indeed come to pass by the grace of Śivagaṅgā! / What indeed is difficult to attain here by the grace of Śivagaṅgā?"

sanskrit_iast:
meghahāsa uvāca
paribhūtaḥ pitā pūjyo yuṣmābhir mama daivatam
tasyāpi mama cātyantaṃ prītiś ca kriyate yadi //
meaning:
मेघहास उवाच
परिभूतः पिता पूज्यो युष्माभिर् मम दैवतम्
तस्यापि मम चात्यन्तं प्रीतिश् च क्रियते यदि //
text_mt: Meghahāsa said: / "My father, who was worthy of worship, my deity, was humiliated by you. / If profound affection is shown both to him and to me

sanskrit_iast:
bhavadbhis tapaso 'smāc ca ahaṃ vairān nivartaye
vairaniryātanaṃ kāryaṃ putreṇa pitur ādarāt
prārthayante bhavantaś cet pūrṇās tan me manorathāḥ //
meaning:
भवद्भिस् तपसो ऽस्माच् च अहं वैरान् निवर्तये
वैरनिर्यातनं कार्यं पुत्रेण पितुर् आदरात्
प्रार्थयन्ते भवन्तश् चेत् पूर्णास् तन् मे मनोरथाः //
text_mt: by you, then from this austerity and from enmity I shall desist. / Retribution for enmity must be performed by a son out of devotion to his father; / but if you implore, then my desires are fulfilled."

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
tataḥ suragaṇāḥ sarve rāhuṃ cakrur grahānugam
taṃ cāpi meghahāsaṃ te cakrū rākṣasapuṃgavam //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ततः सुरगणाः सर्वे राहुं चक्रुर् ग्रहानुगम्
तं चापि मेघहासं ते चक्रू राक्षसपुंगवम् //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Then all the hosts of gods made Rāhu an attendant among the planets, / and that Meghahāsa they made an eminent rākṣasa.

sanskrit_iast:
tato 'bhavad rāhusuto nairṛtādhipatiḥ prabhuḥ
punaś cāha surān daityo mama khyātir yathā bhavet //
meaning:
ततो ऽभवद् राहुसुतो नैरृताधिपतिः प्रभुः
पुनश् चाह सुरान् दैत्यो मम ख्यातिर् यथा भवेत् //
text_mt: Then the son of Rāhu became the lord and master of the southwest; / and the daitya spoke again to the gods: "So that I may have renown,

sanskrit_iast:
tīrthasyāsya prabhāvaś ca dātavya iti me matiḥ
tathety uktvā dadur devāḥ sarvam eva manogatam //
meaning:
तीर्थस्यास्य प्रभावश् च दातव्य इति मे मतिः
तथेत्य् उक्त्वा ददुर् देवाः सर्वम् एव मनोगतम् //
text_mt: and the glory of this tīrtha must be granted—this is my wish." / Saying "So be it," the gods granted everything that was in his heart.

sanskrit_iast:
daityeśvarasya devarṣe tannāmnā tīrtham ucyate
devā yato 'bhavan sarve tatra sthāne mahāmate //
meaning:
दैत्येश्वरस्य देवर्षे तन्नाम्ना तीर्थम् उच्यते
देवा यतो ऽभवन् सर्वे तत्र स्थाने महामते //
text_mt: The tīrtha is named after that lord of daityas, O divine sage; / and since all the gods assembled in that place, O highly intelligent one,

sanskrit_iast:
devasthānaṃ tu tat tīrthaṃ devānām api durlabham
yatra deveśvaro devo devatīrthaṃ tataḥ smṛtam //
meaning:
देवस्थानं तु तत् तीर्थं देवानाम् अपि दुर्लभम्
यत्र देवेश्वरो देवो देवतीर्थं ततः स्मृतम् //
text_mt: that tīrtha is Devasthāna, hard to attain even for the gods; / where the god who is the lord of gods [abides], hence it is known as Devatīrtha.

sanskrit_iast:
tatrāṣṭādaśa tīrthāni daityapūjyāni nārada
teṣu snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca mahāpātakanāśanam //
meaning:
तत्राष्टादश तीर्थानि दैत्यपूज्यानि नारद
तेषु स्नानं च दानं च महापातकनाशनम् //
text_mt: There are eighteen tīrthas there, worshipped by the daityas, O Nārada; / bathing and gifting in them destroys great sins.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
siddhatīrtham iti khyātaṃ yatra siddheśvaro haraḥ
tasya prabhāvaṃ vakṣyāmi sarvasiddhikaraṃ nṛṇām //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
सिद्धतीर्थम् इति ख्यातं यत्र सिद्धेश्वरो हरः
तस्य प्रभावं वक्ष्यामि सर्वसिद्धिकरं नृणाम् //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / It is renowned as Siddhatīrtha, where Hara is the Lord of Siddhas. / I shall declare its power, which confers all accomplishments upon men.

sanskrit_iast:
pulastyavaṃśasaṃbhūto rāvaṇo lokarāvaṇaḥ
diśo vijitya sarvāś ca somalokam ajīgamat //
meaning:
पुलस्त्यवंशसंभूतो रावणो लोकरावणः
दिशो विजित्य सर्वाश् च सोमलोकम् अजीगमत् //
text_mt: Born in the lineage of Pulastya, Rāvaṇa, the terror of the worlds, / having conquered all the directions, went to the world of Soma.

sanskrit_iast:
somena saha yotsyantaṃ daśāsyam aham abravam
mantraṃ dāsye nivartasva somayuddhād daśānana //
meaning:
सोमेन सह योत्स्यन्तं दशास्यम् अहम् अब्रवम्
मन्त्रं दास्ये निवर्तस्व सोमयुद्धाद् दशानन //
text_mt: To the ten-faced one who was about to fight with Soma, I said: / 'I shall grant a mantra; turn back from fighting with Soma, O ten-faced one!'

sanskrit_iast:
ity uktvāṣṭottaraṃ mantraṃ śatanāmabhir anvitam
śivasya rākṣasendrāya prādāṃ nārada śāntaye //
meaning:
इत्य् उक्त्वाष्टोत्तरं मन्त्रं शतनामभिर् अन्वितम्
शिवस्य राक्षसेन्द्राय प्रादां नारद शान्तये //
text_mt: Having spoken thus, I gave the one-hundred-and-eight[-syllable] mantra endowed with the hundred names / of Śiva to the king of rākṣasas for the sake of peace, O Nārada.

sanskrit_iast:
niḥśrīkāṇāṃ vipannānāṃ nānākleśajuṣāṃ nṛṇām
śaraṇaṃ śiva evātra saṃsāre 'nyo na kaścana //
meaning:
निःश्रीकाणां विपन्नानां नानाक्लेशजुषां नृणाम्
शरणं शिव एवात्र संसारे ऽन्यो न कश्चन //
text_mt: For men who have lost their fortune, are fallen into misfortune, and afflicted with manifold troubles, / Śiva alone is the refuge here in this saṃsāra, none other.

sanskrit_iast:
tato nivṛttaḥ sa ha mantriyuktas
tat somalokāj jayam āpya rakṣaḥ
sa puṣpakārūḍhagatiḥ sagarvo
lokān punaḥ prāpa javād daśāsyaḥ
meaning:
ततो निवृत्तः स ह मन्त्रियुक्तस्
तत् सोमलोकाज् जयम् आप्य रक्षः
स पुष्पकारूढगतिः सगर्वो
लोकान् पुनः प्राप जवाद् दशास्यः
text_mt: Then that rākṣasa, accompanied by his ministers, turned back, / having gained victory over that world of Soma. / Proudly travelling mounted on the Puṣpaka, / the ten-faced one swiftly reached the worlds once more.

sanskrit_iast:
sa prekṣamāṇo devam antarikṣaṃ
bhuvaṃ ca nāgāṃś ca gajāṃś ca viprān
ālokayām āsa nagaṃ mahāntaṃ
kailāsam āvāsa umāpater yaḥ
meaning:
स प्रेक्षमाणो देवम् अन्तरिक्षं
भुवं च नागांश् च गजांश् च विप्रान्
आलोकयाम् आस नगं महान्तं
कैलासम् आवास उमापतेर् यः
text_mt: Beholding the gods, the intermediate space, / the earth, the nāgas, the elephants, and the brahmins, / he gazed upon a great mountain, / Kailāsa, which is the dwelling of the husband of Umā.

sanskrit_iast:
rāvaṇa uvāca
ko vā girāv atra vasen mahātmā
giriṃ nayāmy enam athādhi bhūmeḥ
laṅkāgato 'yaṃ girir āśu śobhāṃ
laṅkāpi satyaṃ śriyam ātanoti
meaning:
रावण उवाच
को वा गिराव् अत्र वसेन् महात्मा
गिरिं नयाम्य् एनम् अथाधि भूमेः
लङ्कागतो ऽयं गिरिर् आशु शोभां
लङ्कापि सत्यं श्रियम् आतनोति
text_mt: Rāvaṇa said: / "Who indeed is the great soul that dwells on this mountain? / I shall take this mountain away from above the earth. / If brought to Laṅkā, this mountain will swiftly radiate splendor; / Laṅkā too truly enhances its beauty."

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
itthaṃ vaco rākṣasamantriṇau tau
niśamya rakṣodhipateś ca bhāvam
na yuktam ity ūcatur iṣṭabuddhyā
niśācaras tadvacanaṃ na mene
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इत्थं वचो राक्षसमन्त्रिणौ तौ
निशम्य रक्षोधिपतेश् च भावम्
न युक्तम् इत्य् ऊचतुर् इष्टबुद्ध्या
निशाचरस् तद्वचनं न मेने
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Hearing such words and the intent of the king of rākṣasas, / those two rākṣasa ministers, / wishing him well, said: "It is not proper!" / But the night-wanderer did not heed their words.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃsthāpya tat puṣpakam āśu rakṣaḥ
puplāva kailāsagireś ca mūle
hindolayām āsa giriṃ daśāsyo
jñātvā bhavaḥ kṛtyam idaṃ cakāra
meaning:
संस्थाप्य तत् पुष्पकम् आशु रक्षः
पुप्लाव कैलासगिरेश् च मूले
हिन्दोलयाम् आस गिरिं दशास्यो
ज्ञात्वा भवः कृत्यम् इदं चकार
text_mt: Having swiftly stationed that Puṣpaka, the rākṣasa / leapt to the foot of Mount Kailāsa. / The ten-faced one shook the mountain; / knowing this, Bhava performed this act:

sanskrit_iast:
jitvā digīśāṃś ca sagarvitasya
kailāsam āndolayataḥ surāreḥ
aṅguṣṭhakṛtyaiva rasātalādi
lokāṃś ca yātasya daśānanasya
meaning:
जित्वा दिगीशांश् च सगर्वितस्य
कैलासम् आन्दोलयतः सुरारेः
अङ्गुष्ठकृत्यैव रसातलादि
लोकांश् च यातस्य दशाननस्य
text_mt: Of that enemy of the gods who was proud after conquering the lords of the directions, / who was shaking Kailāsa, / the ten-faced one who went down to the realms of Rasātala and below / merely by the action of [Śiva's] big toe,

sanskrit_iast:
ālūnakāyasya giraṃ niśamya
vihasya devyā saha dattam iṣṭam
tasmai prasannaḥ kupito 'pi śaṃbhur
ayuktadāteti na saṃśayo 'tra
meaning:
आलूनकायस्य गिरं निशम्य
विहस्य देव्या सह दत्तम् इष्टम्
तस्मै प्रसन्नः कुपितो ऽपि शंभुर्
अयुक्तदातेति न संशयो ऽत्र
text_mt: hearing the cry of him whose body was crushed, / laughing together with the goddess, [Śiva] granted his desire. / Gracious to him though angered, Śaṃbhu / is a giver even of what is improper; of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit_iast:
tato 'yam āvāpya varān suvīro
bhavaprasādāt kusumaṃ jagāma
gacchan sa laṅkāṃ bhavapūjanāya
gaṅgām agāc chaṃbhujaṭāprasūtām
meaning:
ततो ऽयम् आवाप्य वरान् सुवीरो
भवप्रसादात् कुसुमं जगाम
गच्छन् स लङ्कां भवपूजनाय
गङ्गाम् अगाच् छंभुजटाप्रसूताम्
text_mt: Then, having obtained boons through the grace of Bhava, that great hero / went to the flower[-chariot]. / Going to Laṅkā, he went to the Gaṅgā born from the matted hair of Śaṃbhu / in order to worship Bhava.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃpūjayitvā vividhaiś ca mantrair
gaṅgājalaiḥ śaṃbhum adīnasattvaḥ
asiṃ sa lebhe śaśikhaṇḍabhūṣāt
siddhiṃ ca sarvarddhim abhīpsitāṃ ca
meaning:
संपूजयित्वा विविधैश् च मन्त्रैर्
गङ्गाजलैः शंभुम् अदीनसत्त्वः
असिं स लेभे शशिखण्डभूषात्
सिद्धिं च सर्वर्द्धिम् अभीप्सितां च
text_mt: Having worshipped Śaṃbhu with various mantras / and waters of the Gaṅgā, the one of undaunted spirit / obtained a sword from the one adorned with the crescent moon, / as well as accomplishment and all desired prosperity.

sanskrit_iast:
maddattamantraṃ śaśirakṣaṇāya
sa sādhayām āsa bhavaṃ prapūjya
siddhe tu mantre punar eva laṅkām
ayāt sa rakṣodhipatiḥ sa tuṣṭaḥ
meaning:
मद्दत्तमन्त्रं शशिरक्षणाय
स साधयाम् आस भवं प्रपूज्य
सिद्धे तु मन्त्रे पुनर् एव लङ्काम्
अयात् स रक्षोधिपतिः स तुष्टः
text_mt: Having worshipped Bhava, he mastered / the mantra given by me for the protection of Soma. / When the mantra was mastered, that lord of the rākṣasas, / well satisfied, went once again to Laṅkā.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ prabhṛty etad atiprabhāvaṃ
tīrthaṃ mahāsiddhidam iṣṭadaṃ ca
samastapāpaughavināśanaṃ ca
siddhair aśeṣaiḥ parisevitaṃ ca
meaning:
ततः प्रभृत्य् एतद् अतिप्रभावं
तीर्थं महासिद्धिदम् इष्टदं च
समस्तपापौघविनाशनं च
सिद्धैर् अशेषैः परिसेवितं च
text_mt: From that time on, this most powerful / tīrtha bestows great accomplishments, grants desires, / destroys the multitude of all sins, / and is frequented by all the perfected ones.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
paruṣṇīsaṃgamaṃ ceti tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam
tasya svarūpaṃ vakṣyāmi śṛṇu pāpavināśanam //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
परुष्णीसंगमं चेति तीर्थं त्रैलोक्यविश्रुतम्
तस्य स्वरूपं वक्ष्यामि शृणु पापविनाशनम् //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / The confluence of the Paruṣṇī is a tīrtha renowned throughout the three worlds. / I shall describe its true nature, which destroys sins; listen!

sanskrit_iast:
atrir ārādhayām āsa brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarān
teṣu tuṣṭeṣu sa prāha putrā yūyaṃ bhaviṣyatha //
meaning:
अत्रिर् आराधयाम् आस ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वरान्
तेषु तुष्टेषु स प्राह पुत्रा यूयं भविष्यथ //
text_mt: Atri worshipped Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara; / when they were pleased, he said: "May you become my sons!

sanskrit_iast:
tathā caikā rūpavatī kanyā mama bhavet surāḥ
tathā putratvam āpus te brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ //
meaning:
तथा चैका रूपवती कन्या मम भवेत् सुराः
तथा पुत्रत्वम् आपुस् ते ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वराः //
text_mt: And likewise, may there be a beautiful daughter for me, O gods!" / In this way, they—Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara—attained sonship.

sanskrit_iast:
kanyāṃ ca janayām āsa śubhātreyīti nāmataḥ
dattaḥ somo 'tha durvāsāḥ putrās tasya mahātmanaḥ //
meaning:
कन्यां च जनयाम् आस शुभात्रेयीति नामतः
दत्तः सोमो ऽथ दुर्वासाः पुत्रास् तस्य महात्मनः //
text_mt: And he begot a daughter named the auspicious Ātreyī. / Datta, Soma, and Durvāsas were the sons of that great soul.

sanskrit_iast:
agner aṅgiraso jāto hy aṅgārair aṅgirā yataḥ
tasmād aṅgirase prādād ātreyīm atirociṣam //
meaning:
अग्नेर् अङ्गिरसो जातो ह्य् अङ्गारैर् अङ्गिरा यतः
तस्माद् अङ्गिरसे प्रादाद् आत्रेयीम् अतिरोचिषम् //
text_mt: Since Aṅgiras was born from Agni, indeed from the glowing coals (aṅgāra), / therefore he gave the exceedingly radiant Ātreyī to Aṅgiras.

sanskrit_iast:
agneḥ prabhāvāt paruṣam ātreyīṃ sarvadāvadat
ātreyy api ca śuśrūṣāṃ kurvatī sarvadābhavat //
meaning:
अग्नेः प्रभावात् परुषम् आत्रेयीं सर्वदावदत्
आत्रेय्य् अपि च शुश्रूषां कुर्वती सर्वदाभवत् //
text_mt: Through the power of Agni, he always spoke harshly to Ātreyī; / yet Ātreyī continually served him attentively.

sanskrit_iast:
tasyām āṅgirasā jātā mahābalaparākramāḥ
aṅgirāḥ paruṣaṃ vādīd ātreyīṃ nityam eva ca //
meaning:
तस्याम् आङ्गिरसा जाता महाबलपराक्रमाः
अङ्गिराः परुषं वादीद् आत्रेयीं नित्यम् एव च //
text_mt: From her were born the descendants of Aṅgiras, of great strength and valor; / and Aṅgiras constantly spoke harsh words to Ātreyī.

sanskrit_iast:
putrās tv āṅgirasā nityaṃ pitaraṃ śamayanti te
sā kadācid bhartṛvākyād udvignā paruṣākṣarāt
kṛtāñjalipuṭā dīnā prābravīc chvaśuraṃ gurum //
meaning:
पुत्रास् त्व् आङ्गिरसा नित्यं पितरं शमयन्ति ते
सा कदाचिद् भर्तृवाक्याद् उद्विग्ना परुषाक्षरात्
कृताञ्जलिपुटा दीना प्राब्रवीच् छ्वशुरं गुरुम् //
text_mt: The sons of Aṅgiras were constantly soothing their father. / Once, distressed by the harsh words of her husband, / the miserable woman, joining her hands in reverence, spoke to her father-in-law, her elder:

sanskrit_iast:
ātreyy uvāca
atrijāhaṃ havyavāha bhāryā tava sutasya vai
śuśrūṣaṇaparā nityaṃ putrāṇāṃ bhartur eva ca //
meaning:
आत्रेय्य् उवाच
अत्रिजाहं हव्यवाह भार्या तव सुतस्य वै
शुश्रूषणपरा नित्यं पुत्राणां भर्तुर् एव च //
text_mt: Ātreyī said: / "I am born of Atri, O carrier of oblations, and indeed the wife of your son, / ever devoted to the service of my sons and my husband.

sanskrit_iast:
patir māṃ paruṣaṃ vakti vṛthaivodvīkṣate ruṣā
praśādhi māṃ surajyeṣṭha bhartāraṃ mama daivatam //
meaning:
पतिर् मां परुषं वक्ति वृथैवोद्वीक्षते रुषा
प्रशाधि मां सुरज्येष्ठ भर्तारं मम दैवतम् //
text_mt: My husband speaks harshly to me and glares in anger for no reason at all. / Admonish my husband, the eldest among the gods, who is my deity!"

sanskrit_iast:
jvalana uvāca
aṅgārebhyaḥ samudbhūto bhartā te hy aṅgirā ṛṣiḥ
yathā śānto bhaved bhadre tathā nītir vidhīyatām //
meaning:
ज्वलन उवाच
अङ्गारेभ्यः समुद्भूतो भर्ता ते ह्य् अङ्गिरा ऋषिः
यथा शान्तो भवेद् भद्रे तथा नीतिर् विधीयताम् //
text_mt: The fire said: / "Born from glowing coals is your husband, the sage Aṅgiras; / let conduct be arranged, O auspicious one, so that he may become peaceful.

sanskrit_iast:
āgneyo 'gniṃ samāyāto tava bhartā varānane
tadā tvaṃ jalarūpeṇa plāvayethā madājñayā //
meaning:
आग्नेयो ऽग्निं समायातो तव भर्ता वरानने
तदा त्वं जलरूपेण प्लावयेथा मदाज्ञया //
text_mt: When your husband, of fiery nature, enters the fire, O fair-faced woman, / then you, in the form of water, should inundate [him] by my command."

sanskrit_iast:
ātreyy uvāca
saheyaṃ paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ mā bhartāgniṃ samāviśet
bhartari pratikūlānāṃ yoṣitāṃ jīvanena kim //
meaning:
आत्रेय्य् उवाच
सहेयं परुषं वाक्यं मा भर्ताग्निं समाविशेत्
भर्तरि प्रतिकूलानां योषितां जीवनेन किम् //
text_mt: Ātreyī said: / "I would endure harsh speech, lest my husband enter the fire! / What is the use of life for women who are adverse to their husband?

sanskrit_iast: iccheyaṃ śāntivākyāni bhartāraṃ labhate tathā //
meaning: इच्छेयं शान्तिवाक्यानि भर्तारं लभते तथा //
text_mt: I would wish for words of peace, so that I may win over my husband."

sanskrit_iast:
jvalana uvāca
agnis tv apsu śarīreṣu sthāvare jaṅgame tathā
tava bhartur ahaṃ dhāma nityaṃ ca janako mataḥ //
meaning:
ज्वलन उवाच
अग्निस् त्व् अप्सु शरीरेषु स्थावरे जङ्गमे तथा
तव भर्तुर् अहं धाम नित्यं च जनको मतः //
text_mt: The fire said: / "Fire is in the waters, in bodies, and in the motionless and moving; / I am considered the eternal abode and the father of your husband."

sanskrit_iast:
yo 'haṃ so 'ham iti jñātvā na cintāṃ kartum arhasi
kiṃ cāpo mātaro devyo hy agniḥ śvaśura ity api
iti buddhyā viniścitya mā viṣaṇṇā bhava snuṣe //
meaning:
यो ऽहं सो ऽहम् इति ज्ञात्वा न चिन्तां कर्तुम् अर्हसि
किं चापो मातरो देव्यो ह्य् अग्निः श्वशुर इत्य् अपि
इति बुद्ध्या विनिश्चित्य मा विषण्णा भव स्नुषे //
text_mt:
Knowing, 'I am who I am', you should not worry.
Moreover, the waters are divine mothers, and Agni is indeed the father-in-law.
Having firmly resolved this with your intellect, do not be sorrowful, O daughter-in-law.

sanskrit_iast:
snuṣovāca
āpo jananya iti yad babhāṣe
agner ahaṃ tava putrasya bhāryā
kathaṃ bhūtvā jananī cāpi bhāryā
viruddham etaj jalarūpeṇa nātha
meaning:
स्नुषोवाच
आपो जनन्य इति यद् बभाषे
अग्नेर् अहं तव पुत्रस्य भार्या
कथं भूत्वा जननी चापि भार्या
विरुद्धम् एतज् जलरूपेण नाथ
text_mt:
The daughter-in-law said:
As to what you have said, 'The waters are mothers',
I am the wife of Agni, your son.
Having become a mother, how can I also be a wife?
O Lord, this is contradictory through the form of water.

sanskrit_iast:
jvalana uvāca
ādau tu patnī bharaṇāt tu bhāryā
janes tu jāyā svaguṇaiḥ kalatram
ityādirūpāṇi bibharṣi bhadre
kuruṣva vākyaṃ madudīritaṃ yat
meaning:
ज्वलन उवाच
आदौ तु पत्नी भरणात् तु भार्या
जनेस् तु जाया स्वगुणैः कलत्रम्
इत्यादिरूपाणि बिभर्षि भद्रे
कुरुष्व वाक्यं मदुदीरितं यत्

sanskrit_iast:
yo 'syāṃ prajātaḥ sa tu putra eva
sā tasya mātaiva na saṃśayo 'tra
tasmād vadanti śrutitattvavijñāḥ
sā naiva yoṣit tanaye 'bhijāte
meaning:
यो ऽस्यां प्रजातः स तु पुत्र एव
सा तस्य मातैव न संशयो ऽत्र
तस्माद् वदन्ति श्रुतितत्त्वविज्ञाः
सा नैव योषित् तनये ऽभिजाते
text_mt:
The one who is born in her is indeed a son;
she is truly his mother, there is no doubt about this.
Therefore those who know the truth of the Vedic revelation say:
She is not merely a woman once a son has been born.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
śvaśurasya tu tad vākyaṃ śrutvātreyī tadaiva tat
āgneyaṃ rūpam āpannam ambhasāplāvayat patim //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
श्वशुरस्य तु तद् वाक्यं श्रुत्वात्रेयी तदैव तत्
आग्नेयं रूपम् आपन्नम् अम्भसाप्लावयत् पतिम् //
text_mt:
Brahmā said:
Hearing that word of her father-in-law, Ātreyī immediately
flooded with water her husband who had assumed the form of fire.

sanskrit_iast:
ubhau tau daṃpatī brahman saṃgatau gāṅgavāriṇā
śāntarūpadharau cobhau daṃpatī saṃbabhūvatuḥ //
meaning:
उभौ तौ दंपती ब्रह्मन् संगतौ गाङ्गवारिणा
शान्तरूपधरौ चोभौ दंपती संबभूवतुः //
text_mt:
O brahmin, those two spouses came together in the waters of the Gautamī,
and both husband and wife assumed tranquil forms.

sanskrit_iast:
lakṣmyā yukto yathā viṣṇur umayā śaṃkaro yathā
rohiṇyā ca yathā candras tathābhūn mithunaṃ tadā //
meaning:
लक्ष्म्या युक्तो यथा विष्णुर् उमया शंकरो यथा
रोहिण्या च यथा चन्द्रस् तथाभून् मिथुनं तदा //
text_mt:
As Viṣṇu is united with Lakṣmī, as Śaṅkara with Umā,
and as the Moon with Rohiṇī, so the couple was then united.

sanskrit_iast:
bhartāraṃ plāvayantī sā dadhārāmbumayaṃ vapuḥ
paruṣṇī ceti vikhyātā gaṅgayā saṃgatā nadī //
meaning:
भर्तारं प्लावयन्ती सा दधाराम्बुमयं वपुः
परुष्णी चेति विख्याता गङ्गया संगता नदी //
text_mt:
Flooding her husband, she assumed a body made of water,
and the river, famous as the Paruṣṇī, met with the Gautamī.

sanskrit_iast:
gośatārpaṇajaṃ puṇyaṃ paruṣṇīsnānato bhavet
tatra cāṅgirasāś cakrur yajñāṃś ca bahudakṣiṇān //
meaning:
गोशतार्पणजं पुण्यं परुष्णीस्नानतो भवेत्
तत्र चाङ्गिरसाश् चक्रुर् यज्ञांश् च बहुदक्षिणान् //
text_mt:
The merit arising from the gift of a hundred cows is obtained by bathing in the Paruṣṇī.
And there the descendants of Aṅgiras performed sacrifices with bountiful sacrificial fees.

sanskrit_iast:
tatra trīṇi sahasrāṇi tīrthāny āhuḥ purāṇagāḥ
ubhayos tīrayos tāta pṛthag yāgaphalaṃ viduḥ //
meaning:
तत्र त्रीणि सहस्राणि तीर्थान्य् आहुः पुराणगाः
उभयोस् तीरयोस् तात पृथग् यागफलं विदुः //
text_mt:
There are three thousand holy places there, say those versed in the Purāṇas.
On both banks, dear child, they know the distinct reward of a sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast:
teṣu snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca vājapeyādhikaṃ matam
viśeṣatas tu gaṅgāyāḥ paruṣṇyā saha saṃgame //
meaning:
तेषु स्नानं च दानं च वाजपेयाधिकं मतम्
विशेषतस् तु गङ्गायाः परुष्ण्या सह संगमे //
text_mt:
Bathing and giving gifts at them is considered superior to the Vājapeya sacrifice,
especially at the confluence of the Gautamī with the Paruṣṇī.

sanskrit_iast: snānadānādibhiḥ puṇyaṃ yat tad vaktuṃ na śakyate //
meaning: स्नानदानादिभिः पुण्यं यत् तद् वक्तुं न शक्यते //
text_mt: The merit that comes from bathing, gift-giving, and other rites cannot be expressed.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
mārkaṇḍeyaṃ nāma tīrthaṃ sarvapāpavimocanam
sarvakratuphalaṃ puṇyam aghaughavinivāraṇam //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
मार्कण्डेयं नाम तीर्थं सर्वपापविमोचनम्
सर्वक्रतुफलं पुण्यम् अघौघविनिवारणम् //
text_mt:
Brahmā said:
The holy place named Mārkaṇḍeya frees from all sins,
gives the fruit of every sacrifice, is sacred, and wards off a flood of transgressions.

sanskrit_iast:
tasya prabhāvaṃ vakṣyāmi śṛṇu nārada yatnataḥ
mārkaṇḍeyo bharadvājo vasiṣṭho 'triś ca gautamaḥ //
meaning:
तस्य प्रभावं वक्ष्यामि शृणु नारद यत्नतः
मार्कण्डेयो भरद्वाजो वसिष्ठो ऽत्रिश् च गौतमः //
text_mt:
I shall describe its power; listen attentively, O Nārada.
Mārkaṇḍeya, Bharadvāja, Vasiṣṭha, Atri, Gautama,

sanskrit_iast:
yājñavalkyaś ca jābālir munayo 'nye 'pi nārada
ete śāstrapraṇetāro vedavedāṅgapāragāḥ //
meaning:
याज्ञवल्क्यश् च जाबालिर् मुनयो ऽन्ये ऽपि नारद
एते शास्त्रप्रणेतारो वेदवेदाङ्गपारगाः //
text_mt:
Yājñavalkya, Jābāli, and other sages as well, O Nārada—
these authors of treatises who had crossed to the other side of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas,

sanskrit_iast:
purāṇanyāyamīmāṃsākathāsu pariniṣṭhitāḥ
mithaḥ samūcur vidvāṃso muktiṃ prati yathāmati //
meaning:
पुराणन्यायमीमांसाकथासु परिनिष्ठिताः
मिथः समूचुर् विद्वांसो मुक्तिं प्रति यथामति //
text_mt:
well-versed in discourses on the Purāṇas, Nyāya, and Mīmāṃsā,
those learned men spoke with one another concerning liberation according to their understanding.

sanskrit_iast:
kecij jñānaṃ praśaṃsanti kecit karma tathobhayam
evaṃ vivadamānās te mām ūcur ubhayaṃ matam //
meaning:
केचिज् ज्ञानं प्रशंसन्ति केचित् कर्म तथोभयम्
एवं विवदमानास् ते माम् ऊचुर् उभयं मतम् //
text_mt:
Some praised knowledge, some action, and likewise others both.
Disputing thus, they presented both views to me.

sanskrit_iast:
madīyaṃ tu mataṃ jñātvā yayuś cakragadādharam
tasya cāpi mataṃ jñātvā ṛṣayas te mahaujasaḥ //
meaning:
मदीयं तु मतं ज्ञात्वा ययुश् चक्रगदाधरम्
तस्य चापि मतं ज्ञात्वा ऋषयस् ते महौजसः //
text_mt:
Having learned my opinion, they went to the bearer of the discus and mace [Viṣṇu].
And having learned his opinion as well, those sages of great splendor,

sanskrit_iast:
punar vivadamānās te śaṃkaraṃ praṣṭum udyatāḥ
gaṅgāyāṃ ca bhavaṃ pūjya tam evārthaṃ śaśaṃsire //
meaning:
पुनर् विवदमानास् ते शंकरं प्रष्टुम् उद्यताः
गङ्गायां च भवं पूज्य तम् एवार्थं शशंसिरे //
text_mt:
disputing again, prepared to ask Śaṅkara.
Having worshipped Śiva at the Gautamī, they inquired about that very matter.

sanskrit_iast:
karmaṇas tu pradhānatvam uvāca tripurāntakaḥ
kriyārūpaṃ ca taj jñānaṃ kriyā saiva tad ucyate //
meaning:
कर्मणस् तु प्रधानत्वम् उवाच त्रिपुरान्तकः
क्रियारूपं च तज् ज्ञानं क्रिया सैव तद् उच्यते //
text_mt:
The destroyer of Tripura stated the primacy of action (karman):
Knowledge has the nature of action, and action is called that very thing.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmāt sarvāṇi bhūtāni karmaṇā siddhim āpnuyuḥ
karmaiva viśvatovyāpi tadṛte nāsti kiṃcana //
meaning:
तस्मात् सर्वाणि भूतानि कर्मणा सिद्धिम् आप्नुयुः
कर्मैव विश्वतोव्यापि तदृते नास्ति किंचन //
text_mt:
Therefore all beings attain perfection through action.
Action alone pervades everything; without it, nothing exists.

sanskrit_iast:
vidyābhyāso yajñakṛtir yogābhyāsaḥ śivārcanam
sarvaṃ karmaiva nākarmī prāṇī kvāpy atra vidyate //
meaning:
विद्याभ्यासो यज्ञकृतिर् योगाभ्यासः शिवार्चनम्
सर्वं कर्मैव नाकर्मी प्राणी क्वाप्य् अत्र विद्यते //
text_mt:
The practice of learning, the performance of sacrifices, the practice of yoga, and the worship of Śiva—
all is action alone; nowhere here does any living creature exist without action.

sanskrit_iast:
karmaiva kāraṇaṃ tasmād anyad unmattaceṣṭitam
ṛṣīṇāṃ yatra saṃvādo yatra devo maheśvaraḥ //
meaning:
कर्मैव कारणं तस्माद् अन्यद् उन्मत्तचेष्टितम्
ऋषीणां यत्र संवादो यत्र देवो महेश्वरः //
text_mt:
Therefore action alone is the cause; anything else is the behavior of a madman.
Where the dialogue of the sages took place, where the god Maheśvara

sanskrit_iast:
cakāra nirṇayaṃ sarvaṃ karmaṇāvāpyate nṛbhiḥ
mārkaṇḍaṃ mukhyataḥ kṛtvā tato mārkaṇḍam ucyate //
meaning:
चकार निर्णयं सर्वं कर्मणावाप्यते नृभिः
मार्कण्डं मुख्यतः कृत्वा ततो मार्कण्डम् उच्यते //
text_mt:
made the determination that all is attained by men through action,
having placed Mārkaṇḍa at the head, it is therefore called Mārkaṇḍa.

sanskrit_iast:
tīrtham ṛṣigaṇākīrṇaṃ gaṅgāyā uttare taṭe
pitṝṇāṃ pāvanaṃ puṇyaṃ smaraṇād api sarvadā //
meaning:
तीर्थम् ऋषिगणाकीर्णं गङ्गाया उत्तरे तटे
पितॄणां पावनं पुण्यं स्मरणाद् अपि सर्वदा //
text_mt:
That holy place, crowded with hosts of sages, is on the northern bank of the Gautamī;
it purifies the ancestors and brings merit even from being remembered at all times.

sanskrit_iast:
tatrāṣṭau navatis tāta tīrthāny āha jaganmayaḥ
vedena cāpi tat proktam ṛṣayo menire ca tat //
meaning:
तत्राष्टौ नवतिस् तात तीर्थान्य् आह जगन्मयः
वेदेन चापि तत् प्रोक्तम् ऋषयो मेनिरे च तत् //
text_mt:
There, dear child, he who contains the universe declared ninety-eight holy places;
this has also been stated by the Veda, and the sages acknowledged it.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
yāyātam aparaṃ tīrthaṃ yatra kālañjaraḥ śivaḥ
sarvapāpapraśamanaṃ tadvṛttam ucyate mayā //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
यायातम् अपरं तीर्थं यत्र कालञ्जरः शिवः
सर्वपापप्रशमनं तद्वृत्तम् उच्यते मया //

sanskrit_iast:
yayātir nāhuṣo rājā sākṣād indra ivāparaḥ
tasya bhāryādvayaṃ cāsīt kulalakṣaṇabhūṣitam //
meaning:
ययातिर् नाहुषो राजा साक्षाद् इन्द्र इवापरः
तस्य भार्याद्वयं चासीत् कुललक्षणभूषितम् //
text_mt:
King Yayāti, the son of Nahuṣa, was like another Indra in visible form.
He had two wives endowed with auspicious family marks.

sanskrit_iast:
jyeṣṭhā tu devayānīti nāmnā śukrasutā śubhā
śarmiṣṭheti dvitīyā sā sutā syād vṛṣaparvaṇaḥ //
meaning:
ज्येष्ठा तु देवयानीति नाम्ना शुक्रसुता शुभा
शर्मिष्ठेति द्वितीया सा सुता स्याद् वृषपर्वणः //
text_mt:
The elder was the auspicious daughter of Śukra, Devayānī by name;
the second was Śarmiṣṭhā, who was the daughter of Vṛṣaparvan.

sanskrit_iast:
brāhmaṇy api mahāprājñā devayānī sumadhyamā
yayāter abhavad bhāryā sā tu śukraprasādataḥ //
meaning:
ब्राह्मण्य् अपि महाप्राज्ञा देवयानी सुमध्यमा
ययातेर् अभवद् भार्या सा तु शुक्रप्रसादतः //
text_mt:
Although a brāhmaṇa woman, the highly wise, slender-waisted Devayānī
became the wife of Yayāti through the favor of Śukra.

sanskrit_iast:
śarmiṣṭhā cāpi tasyaiva bhāryā yā vṛṣaparvajā
devayānī śukrasutā dvau putrau samajījanat //
meaning:
शर्मिष्ठा चापि तस्यैव भार्या या वृषपर्वजा
देवयानी शुक्रसुता द्वौ पुत्रौ समजीजनत् //
text_mt:
And Śarmiṣṭhā, the daughter born of Vṛṣaparvan, was also his wife.
Devayānī, daughter of Śukra, gave birth to two sons,

sanskrit_iast:
yaduṃ ca turvasuṃ caiva devaputrasamāv ubhau
śarmiṣṭhā ca nṛpāl lebhe trīn putrān devasaṃnibhān //
meaning:
यदुं च तुर्वसुं चैव देवपुत्रसमाव् उभौ
शर्मिष्ठा च नृपाल् लेभे त्रीन् पुत्रान् देवसंनिभान् //
text_mt:
Yadu and Turvasu, both equal to the sons of the gods.
And Śarmiṣṭhā obtained from the king three sons resembling gods,

sanskrit_iast:
druhyuṃ cānuṃ ca pūruṃ ca yayāter nṛpasattamāt
devayānyāḥ sutau brahman sadṛśau śukrarūpataḥ //
meaning:
द्रुह्युं चानुं च पूरुं च ययातेर् नृपसत्तमात्
देवयान्याः सुतौ ब्रह्मन् सदृशौ शुक्ररूपतः //
text_mt:
Druhyu, Anu, and Pūru, from Yayāti, the best of kings.
O brahmin, the two sons of Devayānī resembled Śukra in appearance,

sanskrit_iast:
śarmiṣṭhāyās tu tanayāḥ śakrāgnivaruṇaprabhāḥ
devayānī kadācit tu pitaraṃ prāha duḥkhitā //
meaning:
शर्मिष्ठायास् तु तनयाः शक्राग्निवरुणप्रभाः
देवयानी कदाचित् तु पितरं प्राह दुःखिता //
text_mt:
while the sons of Śarmiṣṭhā had the luster of Indra, Agni, and Varuṇa.
Once, Devayānī, grieving, spoke to her father:

sanskrit_iast:
devayāny uvāca
mama tv apatyadvitayam abhāgyāyā bhṛgūdvaha
mama dāsyāḥ sabhāgyāyā apatyatritayaṃ pitaḥ //
meaning:
देवयान्य् उवाच
मम त्व् अपत्यद्वितयम् अभाग्याया भृगूद्वह
मम दास्याः सभाग्याया अपत्यत्रितयं पितः //
text_mt:
Devayānī said:
I, unfortunate woman, have only two children, O upholder of the Bhṛgu race,
while my handmaid, fortunate, has three children, O father!

sanskrit_iast:
tad etad anumṛśyāyaṃ duḥkham atyantam āgatā
mariṣye dānavaguro yayātikṛtavipriyāt
mānabhaṅgād varaṃ tāta maraṇaṃ hi manasvinām //
meaning:
तद् एतद् अनुमृश्यायं दुःखम् अत्यन्तम् आगता
मरिष्ये दानवगुरो ययातिकृतविप्रियात्
मानभङ्गाद् वरं तात मरणं हि मनस्विनाम् //
text_mt:
Reflecting on this, I have reached extreme distress.
I shall die, O teacher of the Dānavas, from the displeasure caused by Yayāti.
Death is indeed better than humiliation for the high-minded, O father!

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
tad etat putrikāvākyaṃ śrutvā śukraḥ pratāpavān
kupito 'bhyāyayau śīghraṃ yayātim idam abravīt //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तद् एतत् पुत्रिकावाक्यं श्रुत्वा शुक्रः प्रतापवान्
कुपितो ऽभ्याययौ शीघ्रं ययातिम् इदम् अब्रवीत् //
text_mt:
Brahmā said:
Hearing those words of his daughter, the powerful Śukra,
enraged, went quickly and said this to Yayāti:

sanskrit_iast:
śukra uvāca
yad idaṃ vipriyaṃ me tvaṃ sutāyāḥ kṛtavān asi
rūponmattena rājendra tasmād vṛddho bhaviṣyasi //
meaning:
शुक्र उवाच
यद् इदं विप्रियं मे त्वं सुतायाः कृतवान् असि
रूपोन्मत्तेन राजेन्द्र तस्माद् वृद्धो भविष्यसि //
text_mt:
Śukra said:
Because, infatuated by beauty, you have done this displeasure to my daughter,
therefore, O lord of kings, you shall become old!

sanskrit_iast:
na ca bhoktuṃ na ca tyaktuṃ śaknoti viṣayāturaḥ
spṛhayan manasaivāste niḥśvāsocchvāsanaṣṭadhīḥ //
meaning:
न च भोक्तुं न च त्यक्तुं शक्नोति विषयातुरः
स्पृहयन् मनसैवास्ते निःश्वासोच्छ्वासनष्टधीः //
text_mt:
Afflicted by sensual desires, one can neither enjoy nor renounce;
he remains longing only in his mind, his intellect ruined by sighing and gasping.

sanskrit_iast:
vṛddhatvam eva maraṇaṃ jīvatām api dehinām
tasmāc chīghraṃ prayāhi tvaṃ jarāṃ bhūpātidurdharām //
meaning:
वृद्धत्वम् एव मरणं जीवताम् अपि देहिनाम्
तस्माच् छीघ्रं प्रयाहि त्वं जरां भूपातिदुर्धराम् //
text_mt:
Old age itself is death for embodied beings even while alive.
Therefore, O king, go quickly into old age, which is exceedingly hard to endure!

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
etac chrutvā yayātis tu śāpaṃ śukrasya dhīmataḥ
kṛtāñjalipuṭo rājā yayātiḥ śukram abravīt //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एतच् छ्रुत्वा ययातिस् तु शापं शुक्रस्य धीमतः
कृताञ्जलिपुटो राजा ययातिः शुक्रम् अब्रवीत् //
text_mt:
Brahmā said:
Hearing this curse of the wise Śukra,
King Yayāti, joining his hands in reverence, said to Śukra:

sanskrit_iast:
yayātir uvāca
nāparādhye na saṃkupye naivādharmaṃ pravartaye
adharmakāriṇaḥ pāpāḥ śāsyā eva mahātmanām //
meaning:
ययातिर् उवाच
नापराध्ये न संकुप्ये नैवाधर्मं प्रवर्तये
अधर्मकारिणः पापाः शास्या एव महात्मनाम् //
text_mt:
Yayāti said:
I do not commit offenses, I do not get angry, nor do I promote unrighteousness.
Those who act unrighteously are sinners, fit to be punished by the great-souled.

sanskrit_iast:
dharmam eva carantaṃ vai kathaṃ māṃ śaptavān asi
devayānī dvijaśreṣṭha vṛthā māṃ vakti kiṃcana //
meaning:
धर्मम् एव चरन्तं वै कथं मां शप्तवान् असि
देवयानी द्विजश्रेष्ठ वृथा मां वक्ति किंचन //
text_mt:
Why have you cursed me, who am indeed practicing dharma?
Devayānī speaks falsely of me, O best of the twice-born!

sanskrit_iast:
tasmān na mama viprendra śāpaṃ dātuṃ tvam arhasi
vidvāṃso 'pi hi nirdoṣe yadi kupyanti mohitāḥ
tadā na doṣo mūrkhāṇāṃ dveṣāgnipluṣṭacetasām //
meaning:
तस्मान् न मम विप्रेन्द्र शापं दातुं त्वम् अर्हसि
विद्वांसो ऽपि हि निर्दोषे यदि कुप्यन्ति मोहिताः
तदा न दोषो मूर्खाणां द्वेषाग्निप्लुष्टचेतसाम् //
text_mt:
Therefore you should not curse me, O lord of brahmins.
For if even the wise, being deluded, become angry with the innocent,
then there is no fault in fools whose minds are scorched by the fire of hatred.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
yayātivākyāc chukro 'pi sasmāra sutayā kṛtam
asakṛd vipriyaṃ tasya divā rātrau pracaṇḍayā //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ययातिवाक्याच् छुक्रो ऽपि सस्मार सुतया कृतम्
असकृद् विप्रियं तस्य दिवा रात्रौ प्रचण्डया //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Upon the word of Yayāti, Śukra also remembered the unpleasant deed / done repeatedly against him, day and night, by his fierce daughter.

sanskrit_iast: gatakopo 'ham ity uktvā kāvyo rājānam abravīt //
meaning: गतकोपो ऽहम् इत्य् उक्त्वा काव्यो राजानम् अब्रवीत् //
text_mt: Saying, 'My anger is gone,' the descendant of Kavi said to the king:

sanskrit_iast:
śukra uvāca
jñātaṃ mayānayākāri vipriyaṃ na vade 'nṛtam
śāpasyemaṃ kariṣyāmi śṛṇuṣvānugrahaṃ nṛpa //
meaning:
शुक्र उवाच
ज्ञातं मयानयाकारि विप्रियं न वदे ऽनृतम्
शापस्येमं करिष्यामि शृणुष्वानुग्रहं नृप //
text_mt: Śukra said: / 'It is known to me that this unpleasant deed was done by her; I do not speak a falsehood. / I shall grant this mitigation of the curse; listen, O king!'

sanskrit_iast:
yasmai putrāya saṃdātuṃ jarām icchasi mānada
tasya sā yātv iyaṃ rājañ jarā putrāya madvarāt //
meaning:
यस्मै पुत्राय संदातुं जराम् इच्छसि मानद
तस्य सा यात्व् इयं राजञ् जरा पुत्राय मद्वरात् //
text_mt: “To whichever son you wish to transfer your old age, O honor-giver, / by my boon may this old age go to that son, O king.”

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
punar yayātiḥ śvaśuraṃ śukraṃ prāha vinītavat //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
पुनर् ययातिः श्वशुरं शुक्रं प्राह विनीतवत् //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Then Yayāti spoke again to his father-in-law Śukra with humility:

sanskrit_iast:
yayātir uvāca
yo gṛhṇāti mayā dattāṃ jarāṃ bhaktisamanvitaḥ
sa rājā syād daityaguro tad etad anumanyatām //
meaning:
ययातिर् उवाच
यो गृह्णाति मया दत्तां जरां भक्तिसमन्वितः
स राजा स्याद् दैत्यगुरो तद् एतद् अनुमन्यताम् //
text_mt: Yayāti said: / “Whoever receives the old age given by me, endowed with devotion, / let him become the king, O preceptor of the Daityas; let this be approved [by you]!

sanskrit_iast:
yo madvākyaṃ nābhinandet suto daityaguro dṛḍham
taṃ śapeyam anujñātra dātavyaiva tvayā guro //
meaning:
यो मद्वाक्यं नाभिनन्देत् सुतो दैत्यगुरो दृढम्
तं शपेयम् अनुज्ञात्र दातव्यैव त्वया गुरो //
text_mt: Whoever of my sons firmly does not heed my word, O preceptor of the Daityas, / him I would curse; your permission must surely be granted in this matter, O preceptor!”

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
evam astv iti rājānam uvāca bhṛgunandanaḥ
tato yayātiḥ svaṃ putram āhūyedaṃ vaco 'bravīt //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवम् अस्त्व् इति राजानम् उवाच भृगुनन्दनः
ततो ययातिः स्वं पुत्रम् आहूयेदं वचो ऽब्रवीत् //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / “So be it,” said the son of Bhṛgu to the king. / Thereupon Yayāti called his son and spoke these words:

sanskrit_iast:
yayātir uvāca
yado gṛhāṇa me śāpāj jarāṃ jātāṃ suto bhavān
jyeṣṭhaḥ sarvārthavit prauḍhaḥ putrāṇāṃ dhuri saṃsthitaḥ
putrī tenaiva janako yas tadājñāvaśe sthitaḥ //
meaning:
ययातिर् उवाच
यदो गृहाण मे शापाज् जरां जातां सुतो भवान्
ज्येष्ठः सर्वार्थवित् प्रौढः पुत्राणां धुरि संस्थितः
पुत्री तेनैव जनको यस् तदाज्ञावशे स्थितः //
text_mt: Yayāti said: / “O Yadu, accept my old age born from a curse; you are my son, / the eldest, knower of all things, mature, standing at the head of my sons. / A father has a son only through him who abides by his command.”

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
nety uvāca yadus tātaṃ yayātiṃ bhūridakṣiṇam
yayātiś ca yaduṃ śaptvā turvasuṃ kāmam abravīt //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
नेत्य् उवाच यदुस् तातं ययातिं भूरिदक्षिणम्
ययातिश् च यदुं शप्त्वा तुर्वसुं कामम् अब्रवीत् //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Yadu said “No” to his father Yayāti of abundant sacrificial gifts. / And Yayāti, having cursed Yadu, spoke as he wished to Turvasu.

sanskrit_iast:
nāgṛhṇāt turvasuś cāpi pitrā dattāṃ jarāṃ tadā
taṃ śaptvā cābravīd druhyuṃ gṛhāṇemāṃ jarāṃ mama //
meaning:
नागृह्णात् तुर्वसुश् चापि पित्रा दत्तां जरां तदा
तं शप्त्वा चाब्रवीद् द्रुह्युं गृहाणेमां जरां मम //
text_mt: Turvasu also did not accept the old age given by his father then. / Having cursed him, he spoke to Druhyu: “Accept this old age of mine!”

sanskrit_iast:
druhyuś ca naicchat tāṃ dattāṃ jarāṃ rūpavināśinīm
anum apy abravīd rājā gṛhāṇemāṃ jarāṃ mama //
meaning:
द्रुह्युश् च नैच्छत् तां दत्तां जरां रूपविनाशिनीम्
अनुम् अप्य् अब्रवीद् राजा गृहाणेमां जरां मम //
text_mt: Druhyu too did not desire that offered old age, which destroys beauty. / The king spoke also to Anu: “Accept this old age of mine!”

sanskrit_iast:
anur neti tadovāca śaptvā taṃ pūrum abravīt
abhinandya tadā pūrur jarāṃ tāṃ jagṛhe pituḥ //
meaning:
अनुर् नेति तदोवाच शप्त्वा तं पूरुम् अब्रवीत्
अभिनन्द्य तदा पूरुर् जरां तां जगृहे पितुः //
text_mt: Anu then said “No.” Having cursed him, he spoke to Pūru. / Pūru, rejoicing, then took that old age of his father.

sanskrit_iast:
sahasram ekaṃ varṣāṇāṃ yāvat prīto 'bhavat pitā
yauvane yāni bhogyāni vastūni vividhāni ca //
meaning:
सहस्रम् एकं वर्षाणां यावत् प्रीतो ऽभवत् पिता
यौवने यानि भोग्यानि वस्तूनि विविधानि च //
text_mt: For a thousand years, as long as his father was delighted, / whatever diverse objects were to be enjoyed in youth,

sanskrit_iast:
putrayauvanasaṃtuṣṭo yayātir bubhuje sukham
tatas tṛpto 'bhavad rājā sarvabhogeṣu nāhuṣaḥ
tato harṣāt samāhūya pūruṃ putram athābravīt //
meaning:
पुत्रयौवनसंतुष्टो ययातिर् बुभुजे सुखम्
ततस् तृप्तो ऽभवद् राजा सर्वभोगेषु नाहुषः
ततो हर्षात् समाहूय पूरुं पुत्रम् अथाब्रवीत् //
text_mt: Yayāti, contented with his son’s youth, enjoyed pleasure. / Then the king, the son of Nahuṣa, became satiated with all pleasures. / Thereupon, out of joy, he summoned his son Pūru and spoke to him:

sanskrit_iast:
yayātir uvāca
tṛpto 'smi sarvabhogeṣu yauvanena tavānagha
gṛhāṇa yauvanaṃ putra jarāṃ me dehi kaśmalām //
meaning:
ययातिर् उवाच
तृप्तो ऽस्मि सर्वभोगेषु यौवनेन तवानघ
गृहाण यौवनं पुत्र जरां मे देहि कश्मलाम् //
text_mt: Yayāti said: / “I am satiated with all pleasures through your youth, O sinless one. / Take your youth, O son, and give me back my wretched old age.”

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
nety uvāca tadā pūrur jarayā kṣīyate mayā
vikārās tāta bhāvānāṃ durnivārāḥ śarīriṇām //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
नेत्य् उवाच तदा पूरुर् जरया क्षीयते मया
विकारास् तात भावानां दुर्निवाराः शरीरिणाम् //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Pūru then said: “No, let me decline through old age. / O father, changes of states are inevitable for embodied beings.

sanskrit_iast:
balāt kālāgatā sahyā jarāpy akhiladehibhiḥ
sā ced gurūpakārāya gṛhītā tyajyate katham //
meaning:
बलात् कालागता सह्या जराप्य् अखिलदेहिभिः
सा चेद् गुरूपकाराय गृहीता त्यज्यते कथम् //
text_mt: Even old age, arrived through time by force, is endured by all embodied beings. / If it was accepted for the benefit of an elder, how can it be cast aside?

sanskrit_iast:
svīkṛtatyāgapāpād dhi dehināṃ maraṇaṃ varam
athavā tu jarāṃ rājaṃs tapasā nāśayāmy aham //
meaning:
स्वीकृतत्यागपापाद् धि देहिनां मरणं वरम्
अथवा तु जरां राजंस् तपसा नाशयाम्य् अहम् //
text_mt: Death is indeed better for embodied beings than the sin of abandoning what was accepted. / Or rather, O king, I shall destroy this old age through ascetic penance.”

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
evam uktvā tu pitaraṃ yayau gaṅgām anuttamām
gautamyā dakṣiṇe pāre tatas tepe tapo mahat //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवम् उक्त्वा तु पितरं ययौ गङ्गाम् अनुत्तमाम्
गौतम्या दक्षिणे पारे ततस् तेपे तपो महत् //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Having spoken thus to his father, he went to the peerless Gaṅgā. / There, on the southern bank of the Gautamī, he performed great ascetic penance.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ prīto 'bhavad devaḥ kālena mahatā śivaḥ
lokātītamahodāraguṇasanmaṇibhūṣitam
kiṃ dadāmīti taṃ prāha pūruṃ sa surasattamaḥ //
meaning:
ततः प्रीतो ऽभवद् देवः कालेन महता शिवः
लोकातीतमहोदारगुणसन्मणिभूषितम्
किं ददामीति तं प्राह पूरुं स सुरसत्तमः //
text_mt: Then, after a long time, the god Śiva was pleased. / Adorned with the jewel-like virtues of great generosity that transcend the worlds, / that best of gods said to Pūru: “What shall I grant you?”

sanskrit_iast:
pūrur uvāca
śāpaprāptāṃ jarāṃ nātha pitur mama surādhipa
tāṃ nāśayasva deveśa pitṛśaptāṃś ca kopataḥ
madbhrātṝñ śāpato muktān kuruṣva surapūjita //
meaning:
पूरुर् उवाच
शापप्राप्तां जरां नाथ पितुर् मम सुराधिप
तां नाशयस्व देवेश पितृशप्तांश् च कोपतः
मद्भ्रातॄञ् शापतो मुक्तान् कुरुष्व सुरपूजित //
text_mt: Pūru said: / “O Lord, O sovereign of the gods, the old age incurred from a curse / belonging to my father—destroy it, O ruler of the gods! And my brothers, cursed in anger / by our father—render them freed from the curse, O one worshipped by the gods!”

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
tathety uktvā jagannāthaḥ śāpāj jātāṃ jarāṃ tathā
anāśayaj jagannātho bhrātṝṃś cakre viśāpinaḥ //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तथेत्य् उक्त्वा जगन्नाथः शापाज् जातां जरां तथा
अनाशयज् जगन्नाथो भ्रातॄंश् चक्रे विशापिनः //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Saying “So be it,” the Lord of the Universe destroyed that old age / born from a curse, and the Lord of the Universe freed the brothers from the curse.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ prabhṛti tat tīrthaṃ jarārogavināśanam
akālajajarādīnāṃ smaraṇād api nāśanam //
meaning:
ततः प्रभृति तत् तीर्थं जरारोगविनाशनम्
अकालजजरादीनां स्मरणाद् अपि नाशनम् //
text_mt: From that time forward, that tīrtha destroys old age and disease; / it destroys premature old age and other afflictions even by being remembered.

sanskrit_iast:
tannāmnā cāpi vikhyātaṃ kālañjaram udāhṛtam
yāyātaṃ nāhuṣaṃ pauraṃ śaukraṃ śārmiṣṭham eva ca //
meaning:
तन्नाम्ना चापि विख्यातं कालञ्जरम् उदाहृतम्
यायातं नाहुषं पौरं शौक्रं शार्मिष्ठम् एव च //
text_mt: It is celebrated by that name and is proclaimed as Kālañjara, / as well as Yāyāta, Nāhuṣa, paura, Śaukra, and Śārmiṣṭha.

sanskrit_iast:
evamādīni tīrthāni tatrāṣṭottaram eva ca
śataṃ vidyān mahābuddhe sarvasiddhikaraṃ tathā //
meaning:
एवमादीनि तीर्थानि तत्राष्टोत्तरम् एव च
शतं विद्यान् महाबुद्धे सर्वसिद्धिकरं तथा //
text_mt: One should know that there are one hundred and eight such tīrthas / there, O one of great intellect, bestowing all accomplishments.

sanskrit_iast:
teṣu snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca śravaṇaṃ paṭhanaṃ tathā
sarvapāpapraśamanaṃ bhuktimuktipradaṃ bhavet //
meaning:
तेषु स्नानं च दानं च श्रवणं पठनं तथा
सर्वपापप्रशमनं भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदं भवेत् //
text_mt: Bathing and making gifts there, as well as listening and reciting, / calms all sins and bestows enjoyment and liberation.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
apsaroyugam ākhyātam apsarāsaṃgamaṃ tataḥ
tīre ca dakṣiṇe puṇyaṃ smaraṇāt subhago bhavet //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
अप्सरोयुगम् आख्यातम् अप्सरासंगमं ततः
तीरे च दक्षिणे पुण्यं स्मरणात् सुभगो भवेत् //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / There is the holy place celebrated as Apsaroyuga, and then Apsarāsaṃgama / on the southern bank; by remembering it, one becomes fortunate.

sanskrit_iast:
mukto bhavaty asaṃdehaṃ tatra snānādinā naraḥ
strī satī saṃgame tasminn ṛtusnātā ca nārada //
meaning:
मुक्तो भवत्य् असंदेहं तत्र स्नानादिना नरः
स्त्री सती संगमे तस्मिन्न् ऋतुस्नाता च नारद //
text_mt: A person undoubtedly becomes liberated by bathing and other rites there. / A chaste woman at that confluence who has bathed after her courses, O Nārada,

sanskrit_iast:
vandhyāpi janayet putraṃ trimāsāt patinā saha
snānadānena vartantī nānyathā madvaco bhavet //
meaning:
वन्ध्यापि जनयेत् पुत्रं त्रिमासात् पतिना सह
स्नानदानेन वर्तन्ती नान्यथा मद्वचो भवेत् //
text_mt: even if barren, will bear a son with her husband after three months, / if she engages in bathing and giving gifts; my word will not prove otherwise.

sanskrit_iast:
apsaroyugam ākhyātaṃ tīrthaṃ yena ca hetunā
tatredaṃ kāraṇaṃ vakṣye śṛṇu nārada yatnataḥ //
meaning:
अप्सरोयुगम् आख्यातं तीर्थं येन च हेतुना
तत्रेदं कारणं वक्ष्ये शृणु नारद यत्नतः //
text_mt: And for the reason why that tīrtha is proclaimed as Apsaroyuga, / I will state that cause; listen attentively, O Nārada.

sanskrit_iast:
spardhāsīn mahatī brahman viśvāmitravasiṣṭhayoḥ
tapasyantaṃ gādhisutaṃ brāhmaṇyārthe yatavratam //
meaning:
स्पर्धासीन् महती ब्रह्मन् विश्वामित्रवसिष्ठयोः
तपस्यन्तं गाधिसुतं ब्राह्मण्यार्थे यतव्रतम् //
text_mt: There was a great rivalry, O brahmin, between Viśvāmitra and Vasiṣṭha. / While the son of Gādhi was performing ascetic penance, keeping his vows to attain brahminhood,

sanskrit_iast:
gaṅgādvāre samāsīnaṃ preritendreṇa menakā
taṃ gatvā tapaso bhraṣṭaṃ kuru bhadre mamājñayā //
meaning:
गङ्गाद्वारे समासीनं प्रेरितेन्द्रेण मेनका
तं गत्वा तपसो भ्रष्टं कुरु भद्रे ममाज्ञया //
text_mt: seated at Gaṅgādvāra, Menakā was dispatched by Indra: / ‘Go to him and cause him to fall from his penance by my command, O blessed woman!’

sanskrit_iast:
tadoktendreṇa sā menā viśvāmitraṃ tapaścyutam
kṛtvā kanyāṃ tathā dattvā jagāmendrapuraṃ punaḥ //
meaning:
तदोक्तेन्द्रेण सा मेना विश्वामित्रं तपश्च्युतम्
कृत्वा कन्यां तथा दत्त्वा जगामेन्द्रपुरं पुनः //
text_mt: Instructed then by Indra, Menakā caused Viśvāmitra to fall from his penance; / having given birth to a daughter, she returned to the city of Indra.

sanskrit_iast:
tasyāṃ gatāyāṃ sasmāra gādhiputro 'khilaṃ kṛtam
taṃ tu deśaṃ parityajya tīrthaṃ tu suravallabham //
meaning:
तस्यां गतायां सस्मार गाधिपुत्रो ऽखिलं कृतम्
तं तु देशं परित्यज्य तीर्थं तु सुरवल्लभम् //
text_mt: When she was gone, the son of Gādhi remembered all that had happened. / Leaving that region for a tīrtha beloved of the gods,

sanskrit_iast:
jagāma dakṣiṇāṃ gaṅgāṃ yatra kālañjaro haraḥ
tapasyantaṃ tadovāca punar indraḥ sahasradṛk //
meaning:
जगाम दक्षिणां गङ्गां यत्र कालञ्जरो हरः
तपस्यन्तं तदोवाच पुनर् इन्द्रः सहस्रदृक् //
text_mt: he went to the southern Gaṅgā where Hara is present as Kālañjara. / As he was performing ascetic penance, the thousand-eyed Indra spoke again:

sanskrit_iast:
urvaśīṃ ca tato menāṃ rambhāṃ cāpi tilottamām
naivety ūcur bhayatrastāḥ punar āha śacīpatiḥ //
meaning:
उर्वशीं च ततो मेनां रम्भां चापि तिलोत्तमाम्
नैवेत्य् ऊचुर् भयत्रस्ताः पुनर् आह शचीपतिः //
text_mt: Then to Urvaśī, and to Menakā, and to Rambhā, and to Tilottamā; / terrified with fear, they said, ‘Certainly not!’ The husband of Śacī spoke once more,

sanskrit_iast:
gambhīrāṃ cātigambhīrām ubhe ye garvite tadā
te ūcatur ubhe devaṃ sahasrākṣaṃ puraṃdaram //
meaning:
गम्भीरां चातिगम्भीराम् उभे ये गर्विते तदा
ते ऊचतुर् उभे देवं सहस्राक्षं पुरंदरम् //
text_mt: to Gambhīrā and Atigambhīrā, both of whom were proud at that time. / Both of them said to the thousand-eyed god, the breaker of citadels:

sanskrit_iast:
gambhīrātigambhīre ūcatuḥ
āvāṃ gatvā tapasyantaṃ gādhiputraṃ mahādyutim
cyāvayāvo nṛtyagītai rūpayauvanasaṃpadā //
meaning:
गम्भीरातिगम्भीरे ऊचतुः
आवां गत्वा तपस्यन्तं गाधिपुत्रं महाद्युतिम्
च्यावयावो नृत्यगीतै रूपयौवनसंपदा //
text_mt: Gambhīrā and Atigambhīrā said: / ‘We two shall go to the son of Gādhi of great splendor who is performing ascetic penance, / and cause him to fall through dance, song, and the wealth of beauty and youth.

sanskrit_iast:
yāsām apāṅge hasite vāci vibhramasaṃpadi
nityaṃ vasati pañceṣus tābhiḥ ko 'tra na jīyate //
meaning:
यासाम् अपाङ्गे हसिते वाचि विभ्रमसंपदि
नित्यं वसति पञ्चेषुस् ताभिः को ऽत्र न जीयते //
text_mt: In whose side-glance, smile, speech, and abundance of allure / the five-arrowed god constantly dwells—who would not be conquered by them here?’

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
tathety ukte sahasrākṣe te āgatya mahānadīm
dadṛśāte tapasyantaṃ viśvāmitraṃ mahāmunim //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
तथेत्य् उक्ते सहस्राक्षे ते आगत्य महानदीम्
ददृशाते तपस्यन्तं विश्वामित्रं महामुनिम् //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / When the thousand-eyed god said ‘So be it,’ they came to the great river / and saw the great sage Viśvāmitra performing ascetic penance,

sanskrit_iast:
mṛtyor api durādharṣaṃ bhūmistham iva dhūrjaṭim
sahasram ekaṃ varṣāṇām īkṣituṃ na ca śaknutaḥ //
meaning:
मृत्योर् अपि दुराधर्षं भूमिस्थम् इव धूर्जटिम्
सहस्रम् एकं वर्षाणाम् ईक्षितुं न च शक्नुतः //
text_mt: unassailable even by Death, like Dhūrjaṭi stationed on earth. / For a thousand years they were not able even to look upon him.

sanskrit_iast:
dūre sthite nṛtyagītacāṭukārarate tadā
vilokya muniśārdūlas tataḥ kopākulo 'bhavat //
meaning:
दूरे स्थिते नृत्यगीतचाटुकाररते तदा
विलोक्य मुनिशार्दूलस् ततः कोपाकुलो ऽभवत् //
text_mt: Standing at a distance, engaged then in flattering gestures with song and dance, / seeing them, the tiger among sages then became agitated with anger.

sanskrit_iast:
pratīpācaraṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā krodhaḥ kasya na jāyate
nispṛho 'pi mahābāhus tam indraṃ prahasann iva //
meaning:
प्रतीपाचरणं दृष्ट्वा क्रोधः कस्य न जायते
निस्पृहो ऽपि महाबाहुस् तम् इन्द्रं प्रहसन्न् इव //
text_mt: Seeing hostile conduct, in whom does anger not arise? / Though devoid of desire, the mighty-armed one, as if mocking Indra,

sanskrit_iast:
ābhyāṃ muktaḥ sahasrākṣo hy apsarobhyāṃ bruvann iva
śaśāpa te sa gādheyo dravarūpe bhaviṣyathaḥ //
meaning:
आभ्यां मुक्तः सहस्राक्षो ह्य् अप्सरोभ्यां ब्रुवन्न् इव
शशाप ते स गाधेयो द्रवरूपे भविष्यथः //
text_mt: as if saying that the thousand-eyed one had been freed by these two apsarases, / that son of Gādhi cursed them: ‘You two shall take liquid form!

sanskrit_iast:
dravituṃ māṃ samāyāte yatas tv iha tato laghu
tataḥ prasāditas tābhyāṃ śāpamokṣaṃ cakāra saḥ //
meaning:
द्रवितुं मां समायाते यतस् त्व् इह ततो लघु
ततः प्रसादितस् ताभ्यां शापमोक्षं चकार सः //
text_mt: Since you came here swiftly to melt me!’ / Then, propitiated by the two, he granted release from the curse:

sanskrit_iast:
bhavetāṃ divyarūpe vāṃ gaṅgayā saṃgate yadā
tacchāpāt te nadīrūpe tatkṣaṇāt saṃbabhūvatuḥ //
meaning:
भवेतां दिव्यरूपे वां गङ्गया संगते यदा
तच्छापात् ते नदीरूपे तत्क्षणात् संबभूवतुः //
text_mt: ‘You two shall assume divine forms when you unite with the Gaṅgā.’ / By his curse, they instantly became rivers.

sanskrit_iast:
apsaroyugam ākhyātaṃ nadīdvayam ato 'bhavat
tābhyāṃ parasparaṃ cāpi tābhyāṃ gaṅgāsusaṃgamaḥ //
meaning:
अप्सरोयुगम् आख्यातं नदीद्वयम् अतो ऽभवत्
ताभ्यां परस्परं चापि ताभ्यां गङ्गासुसंगमः //
text_mt: Hence arose the pair of rivers known as Apsaroyuga, / and there is the auspicious confluence between the two and of them with the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvalokeṣu vikhyāto bhuktimuktipradaḥ śivaḥ
tatrāste dṛṣṭa evāsau sarvasiddhipradāyakaḥ //
meaning:
सर्वलोकेषु विख्यातो भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदः शिवः
तत्रास्ते दृष्ट एवासौ सर्वसिद्धिप्रदायकः //
text_mt: Śiva is renowned throughout all worlds as the giver of enjoyment and liberation. / Residing there, he grants all attainments merely when seen.

sanskrit_iast: tatra snātvā tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā mucyate sarvabandhanāt //
meaning: तत्र स्नात्वा तु तं दृष्ट्वा मुच्यते सर्वबन्धनात् //
text_mt: Bathing there and seeing him, one is freed from every bond.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
koṭitīrtham iti khyātaṃ gaṅgāyā dakṣiṇe taṭe
yasyānusmaraṇād eva sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
कोटितीर्थम् इति ख्यातं गङ्गाया दक्षिणे तटे
यस्यानुस्मरणाद् एव सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Renowned as Koṭitīrtha on the southern bank of the Gaṅgā is [the place] / by merely remembering which one is fully freed from all sins.

sanskrit_iast:
yatra koṭīśvaro devaḥ sarvaṃ koṭiguṇaṃ bhavet
koṭidvayaṃ tatra pūrṇaṃ tīrthānāṃ śubhadāyinām //
meaning:
यत्र कोटीश्वरो देवः सर्वं कोटिगुणं भवेत्
कोटिद्वयं तत्र पूर्णं तीर्थानां शुभदायिनाम् //
text_mt: Where the god Koṭīśvara resides, everything becomes multiplied ten-millionfold. / A full two crores of auspicious tīrthas are present there.

sanskrit_iast:
tatra vyuṣṭiṃ pravakṣyāmi śṛṇu nārada tanmanāḥ
kaṇvasya tu suto jyeṣṭho bāhlīka iti viśrutaḥ //
meaning:
तत्र व्युष्टिं प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणु नारद तन्मनाः
कण्वस्य तु सुतो ज्येष्ठो बाह्लीक इति विश्रुतः //
text_mt: I shall tell you its efficacy; listen attentively, Nārada. / Kaṇva had an eldest son famed as Bāhlīka;

sanskrit_iast:
kāṇvaś ceti janaiḥ khyāto vedavedāṅgapāragaḥ
iṣṭīḥ pārvāyaṇānīr yāḥ sabhāryo vedapāragaḥ //
meaning:
काण्वश् चेति जनैः ख्यातो वेदवेदाङ्गपारगः
इष्टीः पार्वायणानीर् याः सभार्यो वेदपारगः //
text_mt: he was also known by people as Kāṇva, a master of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas. / Master of the Vedas, together with his wife [he performed] the regular and seasonal sacrifices;

sanskrit_iast:
kurvann āste sa gautamyās tīrastho lokapūjitaḥ
prātaḥkāle sabhāryo 'sau juhvad agnau samāhitaḥ //
meaning:
कुर्वन्न् आस्ते स गौतम्यास् तीरस्थो लोकपूजितः
प्रातःकाले सभार्यो ऽसौ जुह्वद् अग्नौ समाहितः //
text_mt: he dwelt on the bank of the Gautamī, revered by the world. / In the morning, accompanied by his wife, concentrated in mind, he poured oblations into the fire.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvadāste kadācit tu havanāya samudyataḥ
ekāhutiṃ sa hutvā tu samiddhe havyavāhane //
meaning:
सर्वदास्ते कदाचित् तु हवनाय समुद्यतः
एकाहुतिं स हुत्वा तु समिद्धे हव्यवाहने //
text_mt: Thus he always remained. Once, when he was prepared to offer an oblation, / having poured a single offering into the ignited carrier of oblations,

sanskrit_iast:
āhutyantaradānāya havir dravyaṃ kare 'grahīt
etasminn antare vahnir upaśānto 'bhavat tadā //
meaning:
आहुत्यन्तरदानाय हविर् द्रव्यं करे ऽग्रहीत्
एतस्मिन्न् अन्तरे वह्निर् उपशान्तो ऽभवत् तदा //
text_mt: he took into his hand the sacrificial substance to offer another oblation. / Just at that moment, the fire suddenly went out.

sanskrit_iast:
tataś cintāparaḥ kāṇvaḥ kartavyaṃ kiṃ bhaved iti
antar vicārayām āsa viṣādaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ //
meaning:
ततश् चिन्तापरः काण्वः कर्तव्यं किं भवेद् इति
अन्तर् विचारयाम् आस विषादं परमं गतः //
text_mt: Then Kāṇva was filled with anxiety, wondering what was to be done; / falling into utter despair, he deliberated within himself:

sanskrit_iast:
āhutyoś ca dvayor madhya upaśānto hutāśanaḥ
agnyantaram upādeyaṃ vaidikaṃ laukikaṃ tathā //
meaning:
आहुत्योश् च द्वयोर् मध्य उपशान्तो हुताशनः
अग्न्यन्तरम् उपादेयं वैदिकं लौकिकं तथा //
text_mt: “Between two oblations, the fire has become extinguished. / Should another fire be taken—one Vedic or profane?

sanskrit_iast:
kva hoṣyaṃ syād dvitīyaṃ tu āhutyantaram eva ca
evaṃ mīmāṃsamāne tu daivī vāg abravīt tadā //
meaning:
क्व होष्यं स्याद् द्वितीयं तु आहुत्यन्तरम् एव च
एवं मीमांसमाने तु दैवी वाग् अब्रवीत् तदा //
text_mt: Where should the second, the subsequent oblation be offered?” / While he was deliberating thus, a divine voice spoke then:

sanskrit_iast:
agnyantaraṃ naiva te 'tra upādeyaṃ bhaviṣyati
yāni tatra bhaviṣyanti śakalāni samīpataḥ //
meaning:
अग्न्यन्तरं नैव ते ऽत्र उपादेयं भविष्यति
यानि तत्र भविष्यन्ति शकलानि समीपतः //
text_mt: “No other fire is to be taken by you here. / The chips of wood that are near at hand,

sanskrit_iast:
ardhadagdheṣu kāṣṭheṣu viprarāja prahūyatām
nety uvāca tadā kāṇvaḥ saiva vāg abravīt punaḥ //
meaning:
अर्धदग्धेषु काष्ठेषु विप्रराज प्रहूयताम्
नेत्य् उवाच तदा काण्वः सैव वाग् अब्रवीत् पुनः //
text_mt: into those half-burnt pieces of wood, best of brahmins, let the offering be poured!” / “No,” said Kāṇva then. That same voice spoke again:

sanskrit_iast:
agneḥ putro hiraṇyas tu pitā putraḥ sa eva tu
putre dattaṃ priyāyaiva pituḥ prītyai bhaviṣyati //
meaning:
अग्नेः पुत्रो हिरण्यस् तु पिता पुत्रः स एव तु
पुत्रे दत्तं प्रियायैव पितुः प्रीत्यै भविष्यति //
text_mt: “Gold is the son of Fire, and the father is indeed the son. / What is given to the beloved son will surely be for the father's pleasure.

sanskrit_iast:
pitre deyaṃ sute dadyāt koṭiprītiguṇaṃ bhavet
daivī vāg abravīd evaṃ tataḥ sarve maharṣayaḥ //
meaning:
पित्रे देयं सुते दद्यात् कोटिप्रीतिगुणं भवेत्
दैवी वाग् अब्रवीद् एवं ततः सर्वे महर्षयः //
text_mt: What is to be given to the father, let him give to the son: it will result in ten-millionfold affection.” / Thus the divine voice spoke. Thereupon all the great sages,

sanskrit_iast:
niścitya dharmasarvasvaṃ tathā cakrur yathoditam
etaj jñātvā jagaty atra putre dattaṃ pitur bhavet //
meaning:
निश्चित्य धर्मसर्वस्वं तथा चक्रुर् यथोदितम्
एतज् ज्ञात्वा जगत्य् अत्र पुत्रे दत्तं पितुर् भवेत् //
text_mt: having determined the essence of dharma, did as had been said. / Knowing this, what is given to the son in this world belongs to the father.

sanskrit_iast:
apatyādyupakāreṇa pitroḥ prītir yathā bhavet
tathā nānyena kenāpi jagaty etad dhi viśrutam //
meaning:
अपत्याद्युपकारेण पित्रोः प्रीतिर् यथा भवेत्
तथा नान्येन केनापि जगत्य् एतद् धि विश्रुतम् //
text_mt: The pleasure that comes to parents through kindness to their offspring / is not produced by anything else; this is well known in the world.

sanskrit_iast:
suprasiddhaṃ jagaty etat sarvalokeṣu pūjitam
tasmin datte bhavet puṇyaṃ sarvaṃ koṭiguṇaṃ suta //
meaning:
सुप्रसिद्धं जगत्य् एतत् सर्वलोकेषु पूजितम्
तस्मिन् दत्ते भवेत् पुण्यं सर्वं कोटिगुणं सुत //
text_mt: This is celebrated in the world and revered in all realms. / When a gift is made to him, my son, all merit is multiplied ten-millionfold,

sanskrit_iast:
manoglāninivṛttiś ca jāyate ca mahat sukham
punar apy āha sā vāṇī kāṇve 'smiṃs tīrtha uttame //
meaning:
मनोग्लानिनिवृत्तिश् च जायते च महत् सुखम्
पुनर् अप्य् आह सा वाणी काण्वे ऽस्मिंस् तीर्थ उत्तमे //
text_mt: and removal of mental distress and great happiness arise.” / That voice spoke once again: “In this excellent Kāṇva-tīrtha—

sanskrit_iast:
abhavat tan mahat tīrthaṃ kāṇva puṇyaprabhāvataḥ
lokatrayāśrayāśeṣatīrthebhyo 'pi mahāphalam //
meaning:
अभवत् तन् महत् तीर्थं काण्व पुण्यप्रभावतः
लोकत्रयाश्रयाशेषतीर्थेभ्यो ऽपि महाफलम् //
text_mt: O Kāṇva, by the power of merit, that great tīrtha has come to be, / bearing greater fruit than all the tīrthas in the three worlds.

sanskrit_iast:
snānadānādikaṃ kiṃcid bhaktyā kurvan samāhitaḥ
phalaṃ prāpsyasy aśeṣeṇa sarvaṃ koṭiguṇaṃ mune //
meaning:
स्नानदानादिकं किंचिद् भक्त्या कुर्वन् समाहितः
फलं प्राप्स्यस्य् अशेषेण सर्वं कोटिगुणं मुने //
text_mt: Performing bathing, gifting, and other rites with devotion, concentrated in mind, / you will fully obtain the fruit, all multiplied ten-millionfold, O sage.

sanskrit_iast:
yat kiṃcit kriyate cātra snānadānādikaṃ naraiḥ
sarvaṃ koṭiguṇaṃ vidyāt koṭitīrthaṃ tato viduḥ //
meaning:
यत् किंचित् क्रियते चात्र स्नानदानादिकं नरैः
सर्वं कोटिगुणं विद्यात् कोटितीर्थं ततो विदुः //
text_mt: Whatever bathing, gifting, and so forth is performed here by men, / one should know that it is all multiplied ten-millionfold; therefore they know it as Koṭitīrtha.

sanskrit_iast:
yatraitad vṛttam āgneyaṃ kāṇvaṃ pautraṃ hiraṇyakam
vāṇīsaṃjñaṃ koṭitīrthaṃ koṭitīrthaphalaṃ yataḥ //
meaning:
यत्रैतद् वृत्तम् आग्नेयं काण्वं पौत्रं हिरण्यकम्
वाणीसंज्ञं कोटितीर्थं कोटितीर्थफलं यतः //
text_mt: Because this episode of Agni, of Kāṇva, of his grandson, and of gold took place here, / it is named Vāṇītīrtha and Koṭitīrtha, granting the fruit of ten million tīrthas.

sanskrit_iast:
koṭitīrthasya māhātmyam atra vaktuṃ na śakyate
vācaspatiprabhṛtibhir athavānyaiḥ surair api //
meaning:
कोटितीर्थस्य माहात्म्यम् अत्र वक्तुं न शक्यते
वाचस्पतिप्रभृतिभिर् अथवान्यैः सुरैर् अपि //
text_mt: The majesty of Koṭitīrtha cannot be described here / even by Vācaspati and others, or by the other gods.

sanskrit_iast:
yatrānuṣṭhīyamānaṃ hi sarvaṃ karma yathā tathā
godāvaryāḥ prasādena sarvaṃ koṭiguṇaṃ bhavet //
meaning:
यत्रानुष्ठीयमानं हि सर्वं कर्म यथा तथा
गोदावर्याः प्रसादेन सर्वं कोटिगुणं भवेत् //
text_mt: For whatever rite is performed here in any manner, / by the grace of the Godāvarī, it all becomes multiplied ten-millionfold.

sanskrit_iast:
koṭitīrthe dvijāgryāya gām ekāṃ yaḥ prayacchati
tasya tīrthasya māhātmyād gokoṭiphalam aśnute //
meaning:
कोटितीर्थे द्विजाग्र्याय गाम् एकां यः प्रयच्छति
तस्य तीर्थस्य माहात्म्याद् गोकोटिफलम् अश्नुते //
text_mt: Whoever gives a single cow to an eminent twice-born at Koṭitīrtha / enjoys the fruit of ten million cows by the majesty of that tīrtha.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmiṃs tīrthe śucir bhūtvā bhūmidānaṃ karoti yaḥ
śraddhāyuktena manasā syāt tatkoṭiguṇottaram //
meaning:
तस्मिंस् तीर्थे शुचिर् भूत्वा भूमिदानं करोति यः
श्रद्धायुक्तेन मनसा स्यात् तत्कोटिगुणोत्तरम् //
text_mt: Becoming pure, whoever makes a gift of land at that tīrtha / with a mind full of faith, its reward becomes ten-millionfold more.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvatra gautamītīre pitṝṇāṃ dānam uttamam
viśeṣataḥ koṭitīrthe tad anantaphalapradam
atraikanyūnapañcāśat tīrthāni munayo viduḥ //
meaning:
सर्वत्र गौतमीतीरे पितॄणां दानम् उत्तमम्
विशेषतः कोटितीर्थे तद् अनन्तफलप्रदम्
अत्रैकन्यूनपञ्चाशत् तीर्थानि मुनयो विदुः //
text_mt: Everywhere on the bank of the Gautamī, offerings to the ancestors are excellent, / but especially at Koṭitīrtha it yields endless fruit. / The sages know forty-nine tīrthas here.”

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
nārasiṃham iti khyātaṃ gaṅgāyā uttare taṭe
tasyānubhāvaṃ vakṣyāmi sarvarakṣāvidhāyakam //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
नारसिंहम् इति ख्यातं गङ्गाया उत्तरे तटे
तस्यानुभावं वक्ष्यामि सर्वरक्षाविधायकम् //
text_mt: Brahmā said: / Renowned as Nārasiṃha on the northern bank of the Gaṅgā is [a tīrtha]; / I shall speak of its power, which grants complete protection.

sanskrit_iast:
hiraṇyakaśipuḥ pūrvam abhavad balināṃ varaḥ
tapasā vikrameṇāpi devānām aparājitaḥ //
meaning:
हिरण्यकशिपुः पूर्वम् अभवद् बलिनां वरः
तपसा विक्रमेणापि देवानाम् अपराजितः //
text_mt: Formerly, Hiraṇyakaśipu was the foremost among the strong; / through austerity and prowess, he was undefeated by the gods.

sanskrit_iast:
haribhaktātmajadveṣakaluṣīkṛtamānasaḥ
āvirbhūya sabhāstambhād viśvātmatvaṃ pradarśayan //
meaning:
हरिभक्तात्मजद्वेषकलुषीकृतमानसः
आविर्भूय सभास्तम्भाद् विश्वात्मत्वं प्रदर्शयन् //
text_mt: His mind was corrupted by hatred for his son who was devoted to Hari. / Manifesting from the pillar of the assembly hall, demonstrating his universal nature,

sanskrit_iast:
taṃ hatvā narasiṃhas tatsainyam adrāvayat tadā
sarvān hatvā mahādaityān krameṇājau mahāmṛgaḥ //
meaning:
तं हत्वा नरसिंहस् तत्सैन्यम् अद्रावयत् तदा
सर्वान् हत्वा महादैत्यान् क्रमेणाजौ महामृगः //
text_mt: Narasiṃha slew him and then routed his army. / Having slain all the great Daityas one by one in battle, that great beast,

sanskrit_iast:
rasātalasthāñ śatrūṃś ca jitvā svarlokam īyivān
tatra jitvā bhuvaṃ gatvā daityān hatvā nagasthitān //
meaning:
रसातलस्थाञ् शत्रूंश् च जित्वा स्वर्लोकम् ईयिवान्
तत्र जित्वा भुवं गत्वा दैत्यान् हत्वा नगस्थितान् //
text_mt: after conquering the enemies residing in Rasātala, went to heaven; / having conquered there and gone to earth, having slain the Daityas residing on mountains,

sanskrit_iast:
samudrasthān nadīsaṃsthān grāmasthān vanavāsinaḥ
nānārūpadharān daityān nijaghāna mṛgākṛtiḥ //
meaning:
समुद्रस्थान् नदीसंस्थान् ग्रामस्थान् वनवासिनः
नानारूपधरान् दैत्यान् निजघान मृगाकृतिः //
text_mt: those in the ocean, in rivers, in villages, and those dwelling in the forest— / Daityas assuming various forms—he killed them in the shape of a beast:

sanskrit_iast:
ākāśagān vāyusaṃsthāñ jyotirlokam upāgatān
vajrapātādhikanakhaḥ samuddhūtamahāsaṭaḥ //
meaning:
आकाशगान् वायुसंस्थाञ् ज्योतिर्लोकम् उपागतान्
वज्रपाताधिकनखः समुद्धूतमहासटः //
text_mt: those traveling in the sky, those abiding in the wind, those who had reached the world of luminaries. / His claws were fiercer than a thunderbolt, his great mane was tossed up;

sanskrit_iast:
daityagarbhasrāvigarjī nirjitāśeṣarākṣasaḥ
mahānādair vīkṣitaiś ca pralayānalasaṃnibhaiḥ //
meaning:
दैत्यगर्भस्राविगर्जी निर्जिताशेषराक्षसः
महानादैर् वीक्षितैश् च प्रलयानलसंनिभैः //
text_mt: his roar caused the embryos of Daitya women to miscarry, and all the Rākṣasas were overcome by him. / With great roars and glances resembling the fire of cosmic dissolution,

sanskrit_iast:
capeṭair aṅgavikṣepair asurān paryacūrṇayat
evaṃ hatvā bahuvidhān gautamīm agamad dhariḥ //
meaning:
चपेटैर् अङ्गविक्षेपैर् असुरान् पर्यचूर्णयत्
एवं हत्वा बहुविधान् गौतमीम् अगमद् धरिः //
text_mt: with slaps and flailing of his limbs, he pounded the Asuras to dust. / Having slain many such, Hari went to the Gautamī,

sanskrit_iast:
svapadāmbujasaṃbhūtāṃ manonayananandinīm
tatrāmbarya iti khyāto daṇḍakādhipate ripuḥ //
meaning:
स्वपदाम्बुजसंभूतां मनोनयननन्दिनीम्
तत्राम्बर्य इति ख्यातो दण्डकाधिपते रिपुः //
text_mt: who had sprung from his own lotus feet and delighted the mind and eyes. / There an enemy named Ambarya, a foe of the lord of Daṇḍaka,

sanskrit_iast:
devānāṃ durjayo yoddhā balena mahatāvṛtaḥ
tenābhavan mahāraudraṃ bhīṣaṇaṃ lomaharṣaṇam //
meaning:
देवानां दुर्जयो योद्धा बलेन महतावृतः
तेनाभवन् महारौद्रं भीषणं लोमहर्षणम् //
text_mt: a warrior invincible to the gods, surrounded by a mighty army [stood]. / With him, the son of a Daitya, took place a battle with Hari that was exceedingly terrible,

sanskrit_iast:
śastrāstravarṣaṇaṃ yuddhaṃ hariṇā daityasūnunā
nijaghāna hariḥ śrīmāṃs taṃ ripuṃ hy uttare taṭe //
meaning:
शस्त्रास्त्रवर्षणं युद्धं हरिणा दैत्यसूनुना
निजघान हरिः श्रीमांस् तं रिपुं ह्य् उत्तरे तटे //
text_mt: fearsome, hair-raising, showering weapons and missiles. / The glorious Hari slew that enemy on the northern bank.

sanskrit_iast:
gaṅgāyāṃ nārasiṃhaṃ tu tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam
snānadānādikaṃ tatra sarvapāpagrahārdanam //
meaning:
गङ्गायां नारसिंहं तु तीर्थं त्रैलोक्यविश्रुतम्
स्नानदानादिकं तत्र सर्वपापग्रहार्दनम् //
text_mt: The Nārasiṃha tīrtha on the Gaṅgā is famed in the three worlds; / bathing, gifting, and so forth there destroys all sins and baleful planets.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvarakṣākaraṃ nityaṃ jarāmaraṇavāraṇam
yathā surāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ na kopi hariṇā samaḥ //
meaning:
सर्वरक्षाकरं नित्यं जरामरणवारणम्
यथा सुराणां सर्वेषां न कोपि हरिणा समः //
text_mt: It always provides total protection and wards off old age and death. / Just as among all gods no one is equal to Hari,

sanskrit_iast:
tīrthānām apy aśeṣāṇāṃ tathā tat tīrtham uttamam
tatra tīrthe naraḥ snātvā kuryān nṛharipūjanam //
meaning:
तीर्थानाम् अप्य् अशेषाणां तथा तत् तीर्थम् उत्तमम्
तत्र तीर्थे नरः स्नात्वा कुर्यान् नृहरिपूजनम् //
text_mt: so that tīrtha is supreme among all tīrthas without exception. / A man who bathes at that tīrtha should worship Nṛhari;

sanskrit_iast:
svarge martye tale vāpi tasya kiṃcin na durlabham
ityādy aṣṭau mune tatra mahātīrthāni nārada //
meaning:
स्वर्गे मर्त्ये तले वापि तस्य किंचिन् न दुर्लभम्
इत्याद्य् अष्टौ मुने तत्र महातीर्थानि नारद //
text_mt: in heaven, on earth, or in the underworld, nothing is difficult for him to attain. / There are eight great tīrthas beginning with this one there, O sage Nārada;

sanskrit_iast:
pṛthak pṛthak tīrthakoṭiphalam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
aśraddhayāpi yannāmni smṛte sarvāghasaṃkṣayaḥ //
meaning:
पृथक् पृथक् तीर्थकोटिफलम् आहुर् मनीषिणः
अश्रद्धयापि यन्नाम्नि स्मृते सर्वाघसंक्षयः //
text_mt: the wise say that each separately yields the fruit of ten million tīrthas. / Even without faith, when his name is remembered, all sins are destroyed;

sanskrit_iast:
bhavet sākṣān nṛsiṃho 'sau sarvadā yatra saṃsthitaḥ
tat tīrthasevāsaṃjātaṃ phalaṃ kair iha varṇyate //
meaning:
भवेत् साक्षान् नृसिंहो ऽसौ सर्वदा यत्र संस्थितः
तत् तीर्थसेवासंजातं फलं कैर् इह वर्ण्यते //
text_mt: where Nṛsiṃha himself is constantly present, / by whom can the fruit resulting from the worship of that tīrtha be described here?

sanskrit_iast:
yathā na devo nṛharer adhikaḥ kvāpi vartate
tathā nṛsiṃhatīrthena samaṃ tīrthaṃ na kutracit //
meaning:
यथा न देवो नृहरेर् अधिकः क्वापि वर्तते
तथा नृसिंहतीर्थेन समं तीर्थं न कुत्रचित् //
text_mt:
Just as there is nowhere a deity higher than Nṛhari,
so too there is nowhere a tīrtha equal to the Nṛsiṃha tīrtha.

sanskrit_iast:
brahmovāca
paiśācaṃ tīrtham ākhyātaṃ gaṅgāyā uttare taṭe
piśācatvāt purā vipro muktim āpa mahāmate //
meaning:
ब्रह्मोवाच
पैशाचं तीर्थम् आख्यातं गङ्गाया उत्तरे तटे
पिशाचत्वात् पुरा विप्रो मुक्तिम् आप महामते //
text_mt:
Brahmā said:
The Paiśāca tīrtha is renowned on the northern bank of the Gaṅgā.
Formerly, O noble-minded one, a brahmin attained liberation from the state of a piśāca there.

sanskrit_iast:
suyavasyātmajo loke jīgartir iti viśrutaḥ
kuṭumbabhāraduḥkhārto durbhikṣeṇa tu pīḍitaḥ //
meaning:
सुयवस्यात्मजो लोके जीगर्तिर् इति विश्रुतः
कुटुम्बभारदुःखार्तो दुर्भिक्षेण तु पीडितः //
text_mt:
The son of Suyavas, famed in the world as Jīgarti,
was afflicted with distress by the burden of his household and tormented by famine.

sanskrit_iast:
madhyamaṃ tu śunaḥśepaṃ putraṃ brahmavidāṃ varam
vikrītavān kṣatriyāya vadhāya bahulair dhanaiḥ //
meaning:
मध्यमं तु शुनःशेपं पुत्रं ब्रह्मविदां वरम्
विक्रीतवान् क्षत्रियाय वधाय बहुलैर् धनैः //
text_mt:
He sold his middle son, Śunaḥśepa, the best of knowers of brahman,
to a kṣatriya for slaughter, in exchange for vast wealth.

sanskrit_iast:
kiṃ nāmāpadgataḥ pāpaṃ nācaraty api paṇḍitaḥ
śamitṛtve dhanaṃ cāpi jagṛhe bahulaṃ muniḥ //
meaning:
किं नामापद्गतः पापं नाचरत्य् अपि पण्डितः
शमितृत्वे धनं चापि जगृहे बहुलं मुनिः //
text_mt:
What sin indeed does even a learned man not commit when fallen into misfortune?
And the sage also accepted abundant wealth for acting as the immolator.

sanskrit_iast:
vidāraṇārthaṃ ca dhanaṃ jagṛhe brāhmaṇādhamaḥ
tato 'pratisamādheyamahāroganipīḍitaḥ //
meaning:
विदारणार्थं च धनं जगृहे ब्राह्मणाधमः
ततो ऽप्रतिसमाधेयमहारोगनिपीडितः //
text_mt:
That vilest of brahmins took wealth for cutting him open.
Then he was afflicted by an incurable, grievous disease.

sanskrit_iast:
sa mṛtaḥ kālaparyāye narakeṣv atha pātitaḥ
bhogād ṛte na kṣayo 'sti prāktanānām ihāṃhasām //
meaning:
स मृतः कालपर्याये नरकेष्व् अथ पातितः
भोगाद् ऋते न क्षयो ऽस्ति प्राक्तनानाम् इहांहसाम् //
text_mt:
Having died in the course of time, he was then cast down into hells;
for without experiencing [their fruits], there is no destruction of past sins in this world.

sanskrit_iast:
kiṃkarair yamavākyena bahuyonyantaraṃ gataḥ
tataḥ piśāco hy abhavad dāruṇo dāruṇākṛtiḥ //
meaning:
किंकरैर् यमवाक्येन बहुयोन्यन्तरं गतः
ततः पिशाचो ह्य् अभवद् दारुणो दारुणाकृतिः //
text_mt:
Sent into various other wombs by the servants at Yama's command,
he then became a terrible piśāca of dread appearance.

sanskrit_iast:
śuṣkakāṣṭheṣv athāraṇye nirjale nirjane tathā
grīṣme grīṣmadavavyāpte kṣipyate yamakiṃkaraiḥ //
meaning:
शुष्ककाष्ठेष्व् अथारण्ये निर्जले निर्जने तथा
ग्रीष्मे ग्रीष्मदवव्याप्ते क्षिप्यते यमकिंकरैः //
text_mt:
Then, among dry wood in a waterless, desolate forest
in the summer, engulfed in summer forest fires, he was hurled about by Yama's servants.

sanskrit_iast:
kanyāputramahīvājigavāṃ vikrayakāriṇaḥ
narakān na nivartante yāvad ābhūtasaṃplavam //
meaning:
कन्यापुत्रमहीवाजिगवां विक्रयकारिणः
नरकान् न निवर्तन्ते यावद् आभूतसंप्लवम् //
text_mt:
Sellers of daughters, sons, land, horses, and cattle
do not return from hell until the dissolution of beings.

sanskrit_iast:
svakṛtāghavipākena dāruṇair yamakiṃkaraiḥ
saṃghāte pacyamāno 'sau rurodoccaiḥ kṛtaṃ smaran //
meaning:
स्वकृताघविपाकेन दारुणैर् यमकिंकरैः
संघाते पच्यमानो ऽसौ रुरोदोच्चैः कृतं स्मरन् //
text_mt:
Boiled in the Saṃghāta [hell] by the dreadful servants of Yama
through the ripening of sins done by himself, remembering what he had done, he wept aloud.

sanskrit_iast:
pathi gacchan kadācit sa jīgarter madhyamaḥ sutaḥ
śuśrāva rudato vāṇīṃ piśācasya muhur muhuḥ //
meaning:
पथि गच्छन् कदाचित् स जीगर्तेर् मध्यमः सुतः
शुश्राव रुदतो वाणीं पिशाचस्य मुहुर् मुहुः //
text_mt:
Once, as he walked along the road, that middle son of Jīgarti
heard again and again the weeping voice of the piśāca—

sanskrit_iast:
putrakretur brahmahantur jīgartes tu pitus tadā
pāpinaḥ putravikretur brahmahantuḥ pituś ca tām //
meaning:
पुत्रक्रेतुर् ब्रह्महन्तुर् जीगर्तेस् तु पितुस् तदा
पापिनः पुत्रविक्रेतुर् ब्रह्महन्तुः पितुश् च ताम् //
text_mt:
that voice of his father, the sinful Jīgarti, the killer of a brahmin,
who had bought and sold his own son, a slayer of a brahmin.

sanskrit_iast:
śunaḥśepas tadovāca ko bhavān atiduḥkhitaḥ
jīgartir abravīd duḥkhāc chunaḥśepapitā hy aham //
meaning:
शुनःशेपस् तदोवाच को भवान् अतिदुःखितः
जीगर्तिर् अब्रवीद् दुःखाच् छुनःशेपपिता ह्य् अहम् //
text_mt:
Then Śunaḥśepa said: “Who are you, so exceedingly afflicted?”
